title: Structural integration of inert porous media as a primary mitigation strategy for firewood stoves: Decoupling combustion intensification from emissions
affiliations: Universidad Técnica Federico Santa María, Universidad Técnica Federico Santa María, , Universidad Técnica Federico Santa María and Universidad Técnica Federico Santa María

detail.title: Structural integration of inert porous media as a primary mitigation strategy for firewood stoves: Decoupling combustion intensification from emissions
detail.abstract: Residential wood combustion in energy-vulnerable contexts creates a critical trade-off between thermal comfort and air quality. Conventional emission control technologies often rely on active secondary systems or complex electronic controls that require electricity and maintenance, limiting their adoption in developing regions. This study evaluates a novel stove design integrating Inert Porous Media (IPM) structurally within the combustion chamber to act as a passive primary measure for pollutant reduction. Experimental tests following an adapted EPA Method 5G protocol compared a commercial 11 kW reference stove against an IPM-integrated prototype. Results demonstrate that IPM integration induces thermal reordering that favors secondary air preheating and intensifies heat transfer through enclosure walls. This mechanism increased thermal efficiency by 23% and useful thermal power by 67% while reducing exhaust gas temperatures by 6% and raising external wall temperatures by 18%. Crucially, the prototype achieved a 57% reduction in particulate matter emission rates and a 65% decrease in mass emission factors across the entire granulometric range from TSP to PM1 despite operating at a 15.5% higher burning rate. Normalization by useful energy output revealed systematic reductions of 26% for particulate matter and 33% for carbon monoxide per gigajoule of heat delivered. These findings confirm that structural IPM integration decouples combustion intensification from pollutant formation. The proposed technology offers a scalable and electricity-free solution to reconcile residential heating needs with atmospheric decontamination goals in developing regions.

title: Epistemological Reconfiguration of Ecological Economics: Biophysical Limits and Socioecological Reproduction
affiliations: State University of Maringá and Federal Technological University of Paraná

detail.title: Epistemological Reconfiguration of Ecological Economics: Biophysical Limits and Socioecological Reproduction
detail.abstract: Ecological Economics has consistently established the biophysical limits of economic systems by redefining the economy as an open subsystem embedded within a finite natural system. However, the field has remained epistemologically incomplete because the recognition of these constraints has not been accompanied by an equally structuring integration of the social, institutional, political, and ideational dimensions that sustain socioecological reproduction. This gap has contributed to internal fragmentation and limited the field’s ability to offer an integrated analytical framework in the face of an intensifying socioecological crisis. Although approaches such as Social Ecological Economics and Radical Ecological Economics have expanded the analytical scope of the field, their contributions remain insufficiently articulated with the epistemological core of Ecological Economics. This paper develops a reconfiguration of that core. Its main contribution is an integrated framework organized into three interdependent analytical levels: biophysical, socio-institutional, and ideational. This integrated framework makes it possible to understand the economy as part of a broader process of socioecological reproduction under socioecological constraints.

title: Heat Transfer Characteristics and Apparent Energy Allocation during Drying of Low-rank Coal
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Heat Transfer Characteristics and Apparent Energy Allocation during Drying of Low-rank Coal
detail.abstract: Most coal resources in western China are high-moisture low-rank coals (LRCs), and their high moisture content reduces utilization efficiency and increases operating costs. This study compares the heat-transfer behavior of an LRC packed bed during convective drying and bottom conductive drying. Based on axial transient temperature profiles, a macroscopic control-volume energy balance model and a one-dimensional transient conduction model were established to inversely determine the apparent effective convective heat-transfer coefficient (heff) and effective thermal conductivity (keff). The Fourier number (Fo), Biot number (Bi), particle Reynolds number (Rep), and apparent Nusselt number (Nuapp) were used to characterize the heat-transfer regimes, and a dry-bed reference was further introduced to analyze the apparent energy allocation during convective drying. These results show that convective drying and bottom conductive drying represent two different energy-delivery pathways. Convective drying directly heats the packed bed by hot-air penetration, giving much smaller axial temperature differences and stronger moisture removal than bottom conductive drying, which remained diffusion-limited with little dehydration within 180 min. Under convective drying, heff increased from 52.35 to 91.29 W·m⁻²·K⁻¹ with increasing inlet temperature and from 4.98 to 58.66 W·m⁻²·K⁻¹ with increasing air velocity, whereas keff under conductive drying ranged from 0.24 to 0.32 W·m⁻¹·K⁻¹, showing limited thermal penetration. The calculated characteristic heat-transfer numbers further distinguished heat-diffusion-limited, transitional, and intensified convection-dominated regimes. For the representative condition of 80 °C and 2.0 m·s⁻¹, the apparent sink intensity (βsink) averaged 1.011 during 76–180 min, while the cumulative apparent energy allocation ratio was 0.820 at 180 min.

title: A reproducible workflow for transforming the Ecuadorian ESPAC agricultural survey into crop and livestock Life Cycle Inventory datasets
affiliations: Centre De Coopération Internationale En Recherche Agronomique Pour Le Développement (CIRAD)

detail.title: A reproducible workflow for transforming the Ecuadorian ESPAC agricultural survey into crop and livestock Life Cycle Inventory datasets
detail.abstract: National agricultural surveys contain valuable foreground information for life cycle inventory (LCI) modelling, but they are rarely released in a form that can be used directly. This paper presents a reproducible workflow that transforms the Ecuadorian ESPAC survey data into crop and livestock LCI tables and XML process files compatible with SimaPro. The method is designed for transparency, traceability, and incremental improvement rather than false completeness: median aggregation is paired with empirical min-max uncertainty bounds, and proxy layers remain distinguishable from direct survey observations for pasture yields, fuel use, irrigation, fertiliser composition, pesticide active-ingredient allocation, livestock diets, and utility requirements. The resulting workflow offers a practical route for converting national agricultural survey microdata into reviewable foreground LCI datasets in data-constrained contexts. The workflow, specifically:imports the official survey delivery into SQLite, harmonises source tables and variable dictionaries, and thenbranches into crop and livestock pipelines that construct intermediate inventories, apply explicit rule-based completion where ESPAC lacks direct inventory detail, estimate direct field emissions with documented Tier 1 and literature-derived factors, and export grouped inventories at multiple aggregation levels.

title: Pop-ups Pay Off: Simulating App-Based Trading to Boost Financial Competence
affiliations: Polytechnic of Milan, Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz - Gutenberg School of Management and Economics and Politecnico di Milano - Department of Management, Economics and Industrial Engineering

detail.title: Pop-ups Pay Off: Simulating App-Based Trading to Boost Financial Competence
detail.abstract: The advent of commission-free trading apps has drawn millions of young, financially inexperienced users into capital markets, raising concerns about their preparedness to navigate behavioral pitfalls embedded in platform design. We evaluate two short and scalable simulation-based financial education interventions in a three-arm randomized experiment with 704 undergraduate students at an Italian university (488 completers). In both treatments, participants trade fictitious assets in an incentivized 20-round game that simulates a trading-app environment, accompanied by introductory educational content on core investment concepts. The augmented treatment additionally embeds short in-game pop-ups addressing behavioral pitfalls relevant to app-based trading, including diversification, overtrading, the disposition effect, availability bias, and herd behavior. Measured two weeks after the intervention, both treatments significantly increase financial knowledge relative to a no-intervention control group, with effect sizes of approximately 0.25-0.30 SD for the baseline simulation and about 0.5 SD for the pop-up-augmented version. Both treatments also improve portfolio efficiency captured by a design-based Sharpe ratio computed from declared allocations, while the augmented treatment additionally increases realized in-game portfolio efficiency and revealed risk-taking during the incentivized simulation. By contrast, stated risk attitudes remain unchanged, indicating that the intervention improves how financial knowledge is translated into portfolio decisions rather than altering underlying risk preferences.

title: Source-decision attention multi-scale ensemble booster for multivariate time series classification
affiliations: Kunming University of Science and Technology, Kunming University of Science and Technology, Chengdu University of Information Technology, Peng Cheng Laboratory, Peng Cheng Laboratory, Kunming University of Science and Technology and Chongqing University

detail.title: Source-decision attention multi-scale ensemble booster for multivariate time series classification

keywords.keywords: multivariate time series classification ；UEA repository；ensemble ；multi-scale ；attention mechanism

detail.abstract: Multivariate Time Series Classification (MTSC) is a core task in time series analysis. While ensemble and multi-scale methods excel at this task, they rely heavily on complex preprocessing, manual strategies, and rigid structures, limiting their flexibility to integrate with other models. To address this, we propose the Source-decision Attention Multi-scale Ensemble Booster (SaMEB), a general, plug-and-play enhancement framework that requires only one hyperparameter, $n$. SaMEB significantly boosts MTSC performance without altering the base classifier's original structure. It integrates three core components: a multi-scale source attention module to adaptively extract key variable features; a probabilistic distribution co-evolution strategy for mutually reinforcing optimization during training; and a decision attention module to fuse multi-scale discriminative outputs into a robust probability distribution. Extensive experiments on the UEA repository, containing 30 multivariate time series datasets, confirm the necessity of these components. Comparisons with 14 state-of-the-art methods demonstrate that SaMEB-enhanced models achieve leading performance across key metrics, including classification accuracy and average ranking.

title: Heterogeneous Graph Contrastive Masked Autoencoder
affiliations: Henan Normal University, Hangzhou Dianzi University, Henan Normal University, Hangzhou Dianzi University and Henan Normal University

detail.title: Heterogeneous Graph Contrastive Masked Autoencoder
detail.abstract: Contrastive Learning (CL) and Masked Autoencoder (MAE) methods have been widely applied to Self-Supervised Learning (SSL) for Heterogeneous Graphs (HGs). However, existing graph MAE methods mainly focus on reconstructing node features and topological structures, while lacking the ability to perceive high-order semantic information, which limits the discriminative power of the learned representations. To address this issue, this paper proposes a novel SSL framework, termed Heterogeneous Graph Contrastive Masked Autoencoder (HGCMAE), to enhance the representational discriminability of traditional MAE-based methods. HGCMAE consists of four core modules, namely a hierarchical masking module, a generative branch, a contrastive branch, and a joint optimization module. Specifically, the hierarchical masking module applies controllable multi-level masking to node attributes and meta-path-based adjacency matrices, thereby simulating realistic data incompleteness while preserving sufficient local cues for reconstruction. Based on these masked views, the generative branch reconstructs masked node attributes and meta-path-induced subgraphs from adaptive semantic embeddings, thereby preserving relation-aware semantic feature interactions. Meanwhile, the contrastive branch leverages coherent structural embeddings to enforce cross-view consistency under topology-aware structural dependencies across meta-path-induced graphs. Finally, the joint optimization module jointly constrains the two branches under the guidance of cross-view high-order semantic correlations and dynamically balances the generative and contrastive objectives. Experimental results on four real-world HG datasets demonstrate that HGCMAE achieves competitive performance in node classification and clustering tasks.

title: A Component-Driven Closed-Loop Spatiotemporal-Frequency GraphFusion Framework for Energy Market Forecasting
affiliations: Guilin University of Technology, Guilin University of Technology, Guilin University of Technology and Guilin University of Technology

detail.title: A Component-Driven Closed-Loop Spatiotemporal-Frequency GraphFusion Framework for Energy Market Forecasting
detail.abstract: Amid global energy transitions, the stable operation of energy markets is crucial for national economic security. To accurately capture China's energy market volatility, this study employs the CSI 300 Energy Index and its core constituent stocks. We reformulate the highly non-stationary index forecasting problem into a constituent-driven log-return modeling framework, constructing a system-level feature space grounded in a micro-asset correlation network.Existing studies using graph neural networks and signal decomposition often suffer from isolated univariate modeling and static decomposition decoupled from downstream forecasting objectives. Consequently, they struggle to capture complex cross-asset spillover effects and multi-scale spatiotemporal resonance.To overcome these limitations, we propose a constituent-driven closed-loop spatio-temporal-frequency graph fusion forecasting framework (HGFCT). HGFCT integrates task-driven adaptive decomposition (TRG-VMD) with spatial graph topological evolution, introducing endogenous regularization via a closed-loop dynamic temperature annealing mechanism.Experimental results demonstrate HGFCT achieves superior log-return forecasting performance (R^2 = 0.8996, DA = 88.56%). Furthermore, reconstructed index closing prices closely match actual trajectories (R^2= 0.9886, MAPE = 0.6298%). In summary, outperforming both traditional econometric models and advanced graph neural networks, HGFCT provides a reliable paradigm for risk monitoring and intelligent quantitative decision-making in complex energy markets.

title: Insect-inspired Spiking Neural Network with Minkowski Chain Dendritic Summation for Event-driven Small Target Motion Detection
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Guangzhou Maritime University, University of Leicester, Huaihua University, Guangzhou University - School of Mathematics and Information Science and Sun Yat-sen University (SYSU)

detail.title: Insect-inspired Spiking Neural Network with Minkowski Chain Dendritic Summation for Event-driven Small Target Motion Detection
detail.abstract: Visual small target motion detection is crucial for time-critical applications such as real-time UAV surveillance, autonomous robotics perception, and target tracking. However, conventional frame-based cameras are fundamentally limited by low sampling rates and motion blur. Event cameras, which provide asynchronous outputs with microsecond temporal resolution by recording only brightness changes, offer a promising alternative. Despite these advantages, event-based small target detection remains challenging due to the incompatibility of image-processing paradigms and the dominance of noise events that obscure sparse small target motion signals. Inspired by the spike-based processing of insect small target motion detector (STMD) neurons, which naturally align with event data, we propose a novel STMD-based spiking neural network model (sSTMD) to address the incompatibility issues. To further enhance noise suppression, we introduce a Minkowski-chain dendritic summation mechanism integrated into the sSTMD, which leverages strict spatiotemporal causality—modeled via Minkowski spacetime intervals—to distinguish coherent target motion from uncorrelated noise. Theoretical analysis and numerical experiments on a dedicated dataset demonstrate that our method robustly detects small target motion while significantly outperforming existing models in noise suppression. This work not only provides an effective bio-inspired solution for event-based small target detection but also introduces a principled, causality-driven approach to enhancing noise resilience in spiking neural networks.

title: Intraday Volatility Spillovers from Crude Oil Prices to Sectoral Stock Indices: Evidence from Oil-Importing and Oil-Exporting Economies
affiliations: Imperial College London

detail.title: Intraday Volatility Spillovers from Crude Oil Prices to Sectoral Stock Indices: Evidence from Oil-Importing and Oil-Exporting Economies

keywords: Crude Oil Prices: Sectoral Stock Indices: Volatility Spillovers: Oil-Importing Economies: Oil-Exporting Economies

detail.abstract: This study examines intraday volatility spillovers from crude oil prices to sectoral stock indices in oil-importing and oil-exporting economies. Using high-frequency data from July 31, 2020, to April 30, 2021, during the global health crisis, the analysis includes five oil-exporting and nine oil-importing countries. Ten sectoral indices are constructed from 1,689 individual stocks to capture market dynamics. The findings show that volatility spillovers remain persistently high in the post-pandemic phase, indicating ongoing cross-market risk transmission. However, the magnitude and direction of spillovers vary across countries and sectors. In markets such as the United Kingdom and Norway, oil prices are net volatility transmitters, while in the United States and Canada, oil absorbs volatility from sectoral indices. Weaker and less consistent linkages are observed in countries like South Korea, China, Mexico, and Australia. This study contributes by emphasizing the role of country-specific economic structures and sectoral characteristics in shaping volatility transmission. The results offer valuable insights for investors and policymakers on risk management and portfolio diversification during periods of market uncertainty.

title: National Distributed Mobility & Energy Continuity Framework: A Diesel-First Registered-User Architecture for Essential Fuel Continuity, Demand Visibility, and Energy-Stress Governance in India
affiliations: DBS Global University

detail.title: National Distributed Mobility & Energy Continuity Framework: A Diesel-First Registered-User Architecture for Essential Fuel Continuity, Demand Visibility, and Energy-Stress Governance in India

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal, financial, commercial, advisory, vendor, implementation, ownership, or employment relationship with any company, startup, fuel retailer, fuel distributor, bowser operator, petroleum marketer, logistics firm, technology vendor, OMC, regulator, or government authority that may have influenced this working paper. The paper is submitted as an independent, non-commercial research and policy contribution for discussion and regulatory consideration only.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required for this working paper because it does not involve human participants, patients, clinical data, personal interviews, surveys, experiments, or personally identifiable data. The paper is based on policy analysis, regulatory review, public-domain institutional sources, and the author's prior research background.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding, grant, sponsorship, consultancy support, institutional funding, corporate funding, or government funding. It was prepared independently by the author.

detail.abstract:
This working paper proposes the National Distributed Mobility and Energy Continuity Framework (DMECN), an independent non-commercial policy contribution for examining essential fuel continuity, demand visibility, and distributed resilience in India’s downstream petroleum ecosystem.

The framework does not propose petrol pump expansion, open fuel resale, unrestricted micro-retail, or petroleum consumption growth. Instead, it presents a diesel/HSD-first, registered-user-only, OMC-linked, PESO-compliant, digitally traceable architecture for essential users such as agriculture, freight and logistics, MSMEs, cold chain, emergency services, disaster response, and district-level public functions.

The paper examines possible future controlled downstream categories, including Rural Micro-Nodes, controlled micro-format access points, authorised fuel wholesalers, regional fuel distributors, licensed storage-only operators, mobile dispenser/bowser operators, registered bulk users, Emergency Continuity Nodes, and digital compliance platforms. These categories are presented only as regulatory hypotheses subject to MoPNG, PESO, OISD, OMC, tax authority, state government, and competent-authority review.

The framework is positioned as an evidence-gated consultation paper, not as an implementation claim, approval claim, commercial proposal, vendor pitch, or funding request. It avoids national GDP, employment, tax revenue, import-bill reduction, fuel-saving, or market-size projections. Instead, it proposes pilot-measurable indicators such as essential-user fulfilment, registered-user demand classification, tax invoice completion, geo-fenced delivery, emergency activation response time, operator cost recovery, dealer-impact observation, and incremental consumption control.

The paper contributes to policy dialogue on energy-continuity stress, essential fuel governance, regulated distributed infrastructure, controlled downstream category design, and last-mile resilience in India.

title: MPA-Net: An enhanced feature aggregation with Pixel-Shuffle for non-cooperative low-altitude small object detection
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Harbin Institute of Technology, University of Electronics Science and Technology of China and Sichuan University

detail.title: MPA-Net: An enhanced feature aggregation with Pixel-Shuffle for non-cooperative low-altitude small object detection
detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of the low-altitude economy results in an increasing number of unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) activities, which significantly raises the likelihood of in-flight conflicts between not only UAVs and UAVs, but also UAVs and non-cooperative airborne objects. Detecting these objects in advance is necessary for guaranteeing flight safety of UAVs. Typically, these non-cooperative low-altitude objects are quite small and have different variations and features in their appearances, making effective detection a great challenge. To address this, we propose a visual detection model named MPA-Net. This model is built on the traditional YOLOv8 nano but is modified with two modules. First, the Module-PS is added by employing a Pixel-Shuffle mechanism to restore the fine-grained spatial features of small airborne targets. Second, the Module-DMC is used to introduce a Dual-Path Multi-Scale Convolution mechanism to aggregate global context for better identifying the irregular shapes of the objects. Experimental results demonstrate that MPA-Net achieves an optimal overall performance (mAP@0.5=58.5%), which surpasses the benchmarks including YOLOv8 nano (mAP@0.5=52.6%), YOLOv11 nano (mAP@0.5=50.7%), RetinaNet (mAP@0.5=44.8%), and Faster-RCNN (mAP@0.5=51.9%). The ablation tests show that integrating Module-PS effectively doubles the detection accuracy for birds from 12.0% to 24.1%, while adding Module-DMC significantly increases the accuracy up to 65.7% when detecting kites. Moreover, MPA-Net has a smaller parameter size and faster detection speed, providing a real-time solution for small airborne object detection.

title: Semantic-similar Multi-concept Disentanglement with SA-LoRA and Token-wise Regularization
affiliations: Macau University of Science and Technology, Macau University of Science and Technology and Chongqing University of Technology (CQUT)

detail.title: Semantic-similar Multi-concept Disentanglement with SA-LoRA and Token-wise Regularization
detail.abstract: While concept personalization has witnessed remarkable progress with new technologies such as Low-rank Adaptation (LoRA), multi-concept personalization in semantically similar scenarios remains constrained by persistent challenges. Specifically, concept entanglement causes feature mixing while concept omission leads to incomplete representations. In this paper, we introduce a novel task termed Semantic-similar Multi-concept Disentanglement, which aims to disentangle semantically similar concepts while learning multi-concept features. To address these challenges, we devise a two-stage method, corresponding to a single-concept model and a multi-concept model. To build the single-concept model, a Sparse-Activated LoRA adapter with a learnable special token (SA-LoRA) is proposed. It builds a compact feature space for learning robust concept representations. The knowledge of stage one is then used in stage two via semantic knowledge transfer for concept disentanglement. The multi-concept model is built in formulated multi-concept scenarios. The adapters optimized for semantically similar concepts are partially merged and injected into the model to effectively learn multi-concept features. Each concept is represented by the learned special token and dedicated subclass tokens. To mitigate concept entanglement and concept omission, we propose a Token-wise Regularization to explicitly regularize the concept tokens' attention maps. To further enhance generation quality, we introduce two strategies in the sampling process: latent smoothing and latent refinement. Comprehensive experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our method on the proposed task.

title: Advanced Machine Learning Approach Using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) and Comparison with RSM for Optimization of Biodiesel Yield from Palm Based Waste Cooking Oil
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Malaya (UM), Universiti Putra Malaysia, University of Gujrat, Universiti Malaya, University of Malaya (UM) - Centre of Advanced Materials and University of Malaya (UM)

detail.title: Advanced Machine Learning Approach Using Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) and Comparison with RSM for Optimization of Biodiesel Yield from Palm Based Waste Cooking Oil
detail.abstract: The increasing environmental concerns associated with fossil fuels have intensified the demand for sustainable and renewable energy sources such as biodiesel. In this study, biodiesel production from palm-based waste cooking oil was optimized using Response Surface Methodology (RSM) and a Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KANs) model. A Central Composite Design (CCD) was employed to evaluate the effects of reaction temperature (55-70 °C), reaction time (60-120 min), agitation speed (500-700 rpm), catalyst concentration (1-5 wt%), and methanol-to-oil ratio (6:1-12:1) on biodiesel yield. The maximum experimental biodiesel yield of 99.7% was obtained under optimized reaction conditions, demonstrating the effectiveness of the transesterification process. The RSM model exhibited coefficient of determination (R² = 0.9597) and identified the optimal conditions as 55 °C reaction temperature, 120 min reaction time, 500 rpm agitation speed, 1 wt% catalyst loading, and 12:1 methanol-to-oil ratio. To further enhance prediction accuracy, a KAN model was developed and evaluated. The KAN model achieved an overall coefficient of determination of R² = 0.9576, with superior training performance (R² = 0.9893). The model exhibited low prediction error (RMSEP = 5.6664), with most relative errors within ±10% indicating strong capability in capturing nonlinear relationships. Comparative analysis revealed that while RSM provides reliable and interpretable optimization, the KAN model offers enhanced flexibility and improved prediction of complex nonlinear interactions. Therefore, KAN presents a promising approach for advanced optimization of biodiesel production processes. This study demonstrates the potential of KAN as a next-generation modeling tool for complex biofuel production systems.

title: Trade Diversion and Government-Led Credit Provision: Evidence from China's VAT Rebate Loan Program
affiliations: Georgetown University

detail.title: Trade Diversion and Government-Led Credit Provision: Evidence from China's VAT Rebate Loan Program
detail.abstract: In this paper, we document how access to a government credit program shapes Chinese exporters' adjustment to AD investigations by combining firm-product-destination customs data with hand-collected adoption dates of a VAT rebate loan program in 325 prefecture-level cities. AD investigations chill exports of the targeted product to the initiating destination and induce cross-destination diversion. The loan program, which allows exporters to pledge unfulfilled VAT rebate receivables as collateral for short-term bank loans, enables AD-hit firms to continue serving the targeted market and reduces their diversion to non-hit destinations. We explain these patterns through higher prices in initiating destinations and increased short-term borrowing among firms with higher rebate-delay ratios. Our results suggest that financial access shapes firms' product-destination investment decisions, and domestic credit policy can moderate the impact of foreign trade barriers.

title: Coordinated Optimization of Routine Maintenance and Emergency Dispatch in Battery Energy Storage Stations and Thermal Power plants
affiliations: Kunming University of Science and Technology, Kunming University of Science and Technology and Kunming University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Coordinated Optimization of Routine Maintenance and Emergency Dispatch in Battery Energy Storage Stations and Thermal Power plants
detail.abstract: Battery energy storage stations (BESS) deployment has expanded markedly in recent years. Analogous to conventional generation assets, BESS demand comprehensive maintenance strategies. However, due to the inherently fault-prone nature of BESS, unplanned outages at BESS are frequent. To address this challenge, this paper presents an optimization approach to coordinate routine maintenance and emergency dispatch of BESS and thermal power plants (TPP). In the first stage, a long term maintenance scheduling model is formulated for TPP and BESS. The second stage constructs Bayesian ambiguity sets to rigorously quantify uncertainty in failures of critical BESS components, upon which a compartment level emergency repair and dispatch model is built. In the third stage, the baseline maintenance plan is adaptively revised in light of realized faults. This three-stage sequential decision process is formulated as a multi-stage distributionally robust optimization, and an algorithm based on recursive decomposition is proposed to solve it. Case study results demonstrate that the proposed approach significantly reduces maintenance costs and alleviates the negative impacts of downtime caused by maintenance activities.

title: Beyond Star Ratings: An Integrated Framework for Multidimensional Product Evaluation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Beyond Star Ratings: An Integrated Framework for Multidimensional Product Evaluation
detail.abstract: Online reviews are a central source of product experience information in e-commerce, but platform interfaces usually compress heterogeneous review evidence into a single star rating. This compression makes it difficult for consumers, sellers, and platforms to identify which product attributes shape evaluations or why similarly rated products reflect different strengths and weaknesses. This study develops a review analytics framework for multidimensional product evaluation in e-commerce. The framework links aspect discovery, syntax-guided weak supervision, multitask aspect localization, aspect-level sentiment scoring, and score aggregation into a continuous evidence chain from review text to product evaluation. Using 32,759 Amazon laptop reviews from 46 brands, the framework achieves 84.14% validation accuracy and 73.23% Macro F1 in aspect localization, outperforming the strongest baselines by 0.51 and 4.18 percentage points, respectively. Model-derived overall scores are positively associated with user star ratings (Spearman = 0.66), while still preserving aspect-level differences hidden by aggregate ratings. The resulting evaluation profiles reveal product-specific trade-offs and provide a practical basis for product comparison, diagnostic improvement, and transparent review-based decision support.

title: Exploring Determinants of Users Adopting Blockchain-Based Real-World Asset Farm Games: From Cognition via Affections to Conation
affiliations: Henan Agricultural University, NOVA University Lisbon - NOVA Information Management School (NOVA IMS), Henan Agricultural University, Henan Agricultural University, Henan Agricultural University and Henan Agricultural University

detail.title: Exploring Determinants of Users Adopting Blockchain-Based Real-World Asset Farm Games: From Cognition via Affections to Conation
detail.abstract: Real-World Asset Farm (RWAF) games are an emerging class of blockchain-based applications that tokenize real-world agricultural assets — including land, crops, livestock, and produce — as non-fungible tokens (NFTs), enabling players to engage in both virtual gameplay and tangible financial investment. Despite their growing commercial and academic prominence, the psychological mechanisms underlying individual adoption of RWAF games remain poorly understood. This study develops and empirically tests an integrated adoption model that bridges the Unified Theory of Acceptance and Use of Technology (UTAUT), the Uses and Gratifications Theory (UGT), and a revised Awareness–Interest–Desire–Action (AIDA) framework, reconceptualized as a three-stage cognition–affection–conation process. The model captures users' financial investment perceptions (performance expectancy, effort expectancy, social influence, facilitating conditions, and perceived risks) and gamification perceptions (hedonic, utilitarian, and content gratification) as dual affective pathways that mediate the relationship between technology awareness and behavioral intention. Covariance-based structural equation modeling was applied to survey data collected from 362 respondents in China. Results indicate that awareness is the most influential determinant of adoption intention, operating both directly and indirectly through all affective mediators except social influence. Among the affective constructs, facilitating conditions, content gratification, and utilitarian gratification exert the strongest effects on behavioral intention. Importantly, financial investment perceptions produce stronger mediating effects than gamification perceptions, suggesting that instrumental motivations dominate the adoption calculus for this dual-purpose technology. These findings advance theoretical understanding of adoption processes in technologies that integrate financial and entertainment functionalities and offer actionable guidance for RWAF game developers, marketers, and policymakers seeking to expand user engagement in blockchain-based gaming ecosystems.

title: Persuaded but Mindful: The Roles of AI Agents, IT Affordances, and IT Mindfulness in Shared Purchase Intention
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Persuaded but Mindful: The Roles of AI Agents, IT Affordances, and IT Mindfulness in Shared Purchase Intention
detail.abstract: E-commerce increasingly features the co-presence of AI agents and rich platform affordances, while purchase decisions are often made with partners or peers rather than individually. Prior research, however, has examined AI agents and IT affordances separately and has largely treated behavioral intention as an individual construct, limiting insight into persuasion in socially embedded, AI-enabled contexts. Drawing on dual process theory and the Elaboration Likelihood Model, this study develops an integrative framework in which AI agent characteristics (perceived usefulness, trust, recommendation quality) and IT affordances (visibility, metavoicing, presence, guidance for shopping, co-experience) jointly shape perceived persuasiveness, which in turn drives shared purchase intention, with IT mindfulness as a boundary condition. Using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling on data from 227 online consumers, the results indicate that trust is the strongest predictor among AI agent characteristics, co-experience is the most influential affordance, and perceived persuasiveness strongly predicts shared purchase intention. IT mindfulness negatively moderates this relationship, indicating that more mindful consumers rely less on persuasive cues and engage in more deliberate evaluation. This study positions shared purchase intention as a key outcome and highlights IT mindfulness as a mechanism of deliberate consumer agency in AI-enabled commerce.

title: Understanding the Role of Algorithm Registers in AI Governance Through Comparative Analysis of China and the UK
affiliations: University of Duisburg-Essen, Zhejiang University - Guanghua Law School and University of Cambridge -- Dept. Computer Science & Technology (Computer Laboratory)

detail.title: Understanding the Role of Algorithm Registers in AI Governance Through Comparative Analysis of China and the UK
detail.abstract: Algorithm registers are increasingly being both considered and deployed as instruments in AI governance. They are often expected to deliver transparency; however, in practice their design, scope, and implementation vary substantially. Currently, we lack a holistic understanding of the potential roles that registers might play in AI governance, and how different design choices both shape and reflect those roles. This paper therefore asks how do algorithm registers differ across jurisdictions, and what do these differences reveal about their roles in AI governance? Towards this, we conduct a comparative analysis of two influential but contrasting algorithm registration mechanisms, China's Beian system and the UK's Algorithmic Transparency Recording Standard (ATRS), drawing on publicly available regulatory documents, registration guidelines, and registry data. Crucially, our analysis shows that an algorithm register, depending on its design and implementation, can serve functions beyond transparency, including pre-market approval, enabling ecosystem-level understanding, and acting as a broader regulatory infrastructure. As algorithm registries proliferate globally, we stress the importance of researchers and policymakers considering and examining the concrete governance functions that algorithm registries can perform as a result of their design and institutional context, rather than approaching them primarily through a transparency lens.

title: Artificial Receivers in Entrepreneurial Finance:How AI Architectures Interpret Entrepreneurial Signals?
affiliations: Ben-Gurion University of the Negev, Peres Academic Center and Ben-Gurion University of the Negev

detail.title: Artificial Receivers in Entrepreneurial Finance:How AI Architectures Interpret Entrepreneurial Signals?
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence is increasingly embedded in entrepreneurial finance, yet signaling theory suggests that evaluation depends on the receiver. This study conceptualizes large language models as artificial signal receivers and examines whether architectural variation shapes startup assessment. Using data on 413 technology ventures founded in 2015 with verified outcomes through 2023, six leading AI architectures generated probabilistic predictions for survival, closure, exit, and follow on funding. Despite identical inputs, the results show substantial differences across architectures in predictive performance, signal weighting, error patterns, and demographic and geographic differentials. Divergence is especially pronounced in ambiguous outcomes, suggesting that interpretive demands amplify architectural heterogeneity. These findings extend signaling theory by showing that evaluation does not converge even under controlled informational conditions, but remains contingent on the structural properties of the receiver. As a result, algorithmic evaluation should not be treated as uniformly objective, but as architecture dependent and interpretively heterogeneous.​

title: When to Act, When to Ask: Simulation-Based Evaluation of Human-in-the-Loop Decision Policies for Enterprise Agents
affiliations: Thapar Institute of Engineering and Technology and

detail.title: When to Act, When to Ask: Simulation-Based Evaluation of Human-in-the-Loop Decision Policies for Enterprise Agents
detail.abstract: Enterprise assistants powered by large language models (LLMs) face a fundamental dilemma: when should they act autonomously, and when should they escalate or ask for clarification? Overly aggressive autonomy risks errors and erodes user trust, while excessive deferral frustrates users and reduces efficiency. We present ActAsk, a framework of executable decision policies that formalize "when to act vs. when to ask" in enterprise contexts. Policies include confidence gating, scope restrictions, confirmations, fallbacks, and audit logging. A calibrated autonomy controller tunes thresholds under safety constraints using a constrained contextual bandit. Unlike prior reports of unverifiable field trials, we evaluate ActAsk entirely through simulation: (1) offline replay of synthetic IT/HR question-answer datasets; (2) scenario-based transcript surveys measuring trust and satisfaction; and (3) policy ablations. The results show that ActAsk reduces incorrect answers, improves escalation precision, and increases perceived trust. Contributions include a taxonomy of executable policies, reproducible simulation methods, design guidelines, and governance templates for responsible enterprise adoption.

title: Multi-Scale Structural Descriptors for Governance-Relevant Patterns in Data Lineage Graphs

detail.title: Multi-Scale Structural Descriptors for Governance-Relevant Patterns in Data Lineage Graphs
detail.abstract: Data governance maturity is typically assessed through surveys, audits, and capabilitymodel checklists that capture stated policy but not realized practice. We propose four multi-scale structural descriptors that detect governance-relevant patterns in the topology of data lineage graphs: community stability under resolution sweep (D1), blast-radius concentration profile (D2), spectral gap and Fiedler structure (D3), and persistent homology of shortest-path filtrations (D4). In controlled experiments on synthetic lineage graphs at three governance levels, D1, D2, and D4 achieve statistically significant differentiation after Benjamini-Hochberg FDR correction at the largest scale tested (N ≈ 130), with Cohen's d exceeding 3.9 for D1 and 15.0 for D4. Validation on an anonymized production dbt lineage graph (223 nodes, 263 edges, 26 domains) yields permutation Spearman ρ =-0.71 between D3 algebraic connectivity and documentation rate across 18 domains (FDR-adjusted p = 0.043). Subset robustness analysis shows this association does not survive restriction to the 6 domains with internal edges (p = 0.19), and layer-stratified permutation confirms D3 is constant within each layer stratum (p = 1.0): the correlation is a between-layer architectural pattern, not a within-layer governance signal. A degree-preserving rewiring null model confirms that D1, D3 Fiedler bimodality, and D4 H1 features capture structure beyond degree sequences (|z| > 2.9); layer-preserving rewiring yields D1 z = +2.68 and D3 alg. conn. z =-2.27. Cross-dataset comparison on 32 graphs from four sources (WfCommons scientific workflows, DLG-DG-23 Huawei Cloud lineage graphs, DW-Bench warehouse schemas, and the dbt manifest) shows that production data lineage graphs from two independent organizations converge on high community stability and small spectral gaps, occupying a region of descriptor space distinct from scientific workflows. Cross-organization validation on two additional public dbt projects (Cal-ITP, 26 domains; Mattermost, 6 domains) finds no replication: the D3 correlation does not reach significance in Cal-ITP and reverses sign in Mattermost, consistent with the between-layer architecture interpretation. The descriptors produce reproducible structural characterization across organizations; governance prediction requires within-organization calibration and cannot be generalized from a single production case; cross-organization validation shows no replication.

title: Prompt Injection and Jailbreak Attacks in Large Language Model-Based Agents

detail.title: Prompt Injection and Jailbreak Attacks in Large Language Model-Based Agents

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares the following: Rizwan Tanveer is employed as Principal Consultant at DTSSolution (Beyon Cyber), a cybersecurity consultancy operating in the Gulf Cooperation Councilregion. The frameworks and standards discussed in this paper, including the OWASP Top 10 forLarge Language Model Applications, the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications, the NIST AIRisk Management Framework, and ISO/IEC 42001, are publicly available reference materials, andDTS Solution does not hold a financial interest in any specific framework or vendor referenced.This paper was prepared as part of the author's doctoral research at Walsh College and does notrepresent a commissioned consulting deliverable.

detail.abstract:
Background. Prompt injection has been ranked the top threat in the OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications since 2023, and the December 2025 OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications places goal hijacking, the agentic manifestation of prompt injection, at position one. The structural cause is that large language models process instructions and data through the same neural pathway, making the boundary between authorised instructions and adversarial content fundamentally permeable. The agentic deployment context, which integrates retrieval, tool invocation, persistent memory, and the Model Context Protocol, has dramatically expanded the prompt-injection attack surface from 2023 to 2026.

Purpose. This paper synthesises the prompt-injection and jailbreak literature, examining direct and indirect injection techniques, the failure modes underlying jailbreak success, retrieval-augmented generation poisoning, Model Context Protocol vulnerabilities, and the evolving landscape of defensive controls. It positions prompt injection as a problem requiring defence-in-depth across input, retrieval, planning, tool execution, and output layers, rather than a single-control problem.

Approach. The paper adopts a narrative literature review methodology drawing on authoritative primary sources, including the OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications (2025) and OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications (2025), foundational jailbreak research (Wei, Haghtalab, & Steinhardt, 2023), indirect prompt injection foundations (Greshake et al., 2023), automated jailbreak research (Zou et al., 2023), recent systematisation-of-knowledge papers, and verified real-world incidents, including the GitHub Copilot CVE-2025-53773 RCE and the CamoLeak CVSS 9.6 exploit.

Findings. Three findings are advanced. First, prompt injection is structural rather than incidental: it arises from the architectural decision to process instructions and data through the same channel and cannot be eliminated through training alone. Second, indirect prompt injection through retrieved content, embedded in agentic workflows, has produced verified real-world security incidents with severities exceeding CVSS 9.0, signalling that the discipline has moved from theoretical to operational. Third, defensive controls require architectural separation of trusted instruction channels from untrusted data channels, output validation, structured policy mediation between agent reasoning and tool execution, and continuous adversarial evaluation.

Implications. Practitioners deploying large language models and agentic systems require defence-in-depth controls aligned to the OWASP Top 10 for Large Language Model Applications and the OWASP Top 10 for Agentic Applications, integrated within ISO/IEC 42001 management system documentation and the NIST AI Risk Management Framework. The paper provides a structured mapping between attack categories and applicable controls.

title: AI Governance Frameworks: ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF, and the EU AI Act

detail.title: AI Governance Frameworks: ISO/IEC 42001, NIST AI RMF, and the EU AI Act

detail.abstract:
Background. Three principal frameworks anchor contemporary AI governance practice: ISO/IEC 42001:2023, the international AI management system standard; the NIST AI Risk Management Framework, the United States voluntary risk function framework with its July 2024 Generative AI Profile; and the EU AI Act, the world's first comprehensive risk-based AI regulation, with its November 2025 Digital Omnibus proposal currently subject to political negotiation. Each framework addresses overlapping but non-identical concerns, applies in different jurisdictional contexts, and requires distinct operational instrumentation. Practitioners deploying AI in regulated environments increasingly face the requirement to demonstrate compliance against multiple frameworks simultaneously.

Purpose. This paper synthesises the structure, scope, and operational requirements of the three principal AI governance frameworks, examines their convergences and divergences, identifies systemic gaps in their coverage of agentic AI capabilities, and grounds the analysis in the emerging regional AI governance instruments of the Gulf Cooperation Council. It proposes a comparative scoring rubric across the frameworks intended for practitioner use in deployment design and assurance.

Approach. The paper adopts a narrative literature review methodology drawing on authoritative primary sources, including ISO/IEC 42001:2023, NIST AI 100-1 and NIST AI 600-1, the EU AI Act (Regulation 2024/1689) and its November 2025 Digital Omnibus amendment proposal, the SDAIA AI Adoption Framework (November 2025), and the UAE Charter for the Development and Use of Artificial Intelligence (2024). Sources were selected for authority, currency, and direct relevance to operational AI governance practice in 2026.

Findings. Three findings are advanced. First, the three principal frameworks are complementary rather than substitutive: ISO/IEC 42001 provides management system framing, NIST provides risk function structure, and the EU AI Act provides legally binding requirements within the EU scope. Second, all three frameworks contain identifiable gaps in coverage of agentic AI capabilities, including multi-agent orchestration, autonomous decision delegation, and emergent behaviour, reflecting that the frameworks were finalised before agentic deployment scaled. Third, the GCC AI governance landscape is converging toward ISO/IEC 42001 as the de facto international standard while developing region-specific instruments that complement rather than replicate it.

Implications. Practitioners deploying AI in multi-jurisdictional contexts require integrated governance programmes that map controls to multiple frameworks simultaneously. The proposed comparative scoring rubric provides a basis for systematic gap analysis at deployment design time. The agentic AI coverage gaps identified in this paper warrant explicit treatment in subsequent revisions to governance frameworks and in the deployment of organisations' supplementary control specifications

title: From Knowledge Economies to Judgment Economies: Predictive Intelligence, Consequential Reasoning, and the Future of the Intelligent Enterprise

detail.title: From Knowledge Economies to Judgment Economies: Predictive Intelligence, Consequential Reasoning, and the Future of the Intelligent Enterprise
detail.abstract:
This paper argues that organizations may be entering a structural transition from knowledge economies toward judgment economies. As generative AI, predictive systems, and large-scale computational models increasingly commodify the production, retrieval, and recombination of knowledge, sustainable organizational advantage shifts away from the possession of information itself toward the capacity to generate robust judgment under conditions of uncertainty. The central scarcity of the intelligent enterprise may therefore no longer be knowledge, but the ability to integrate prediction, causal reasoning, contextual interpretation, governance, and human accountability into coherent decision architectures.

Building on Hayek’s theory of distributed knowledge, Simon’s bounded rationality, Kahneman and Tversky’s behavioral decision theory, Pearl’s causality framework, Arendt’s theory of representative judgment, and contemporary research on human–AI complementarity, the paper develops an integrative theoretical framework centered on three core constructs: predictive intelligence, consequential reasoning, and the intelligent enterprise. Predictive intelligence is conceptualized not merely as predictive analytics or forecasting capability, but as an organizational capability that systematically couples prediction with explanation, contextual interpretation, and governance mechanisms capable of supporting judgment under uncertainty.

The paper further argues that the transition toward judgment economies is not primarily a transition from human to machine, but from the primacy of isolated domain expertise toward the primacy of organizational decision architectures. In this view, the intelligent enterpris is distinguished not by the quantity of data or AI systems they possess, but by their capacity to combine prediction, explanation, institutional learning, and accountable human oversight within adaptive socio-technical systems.

Finally, the manuscript proposes empirically operationalizable constructs, measurement frameworks, and research propositions intended to support future theory development and empirical validation across organization theory, strategy, information systems, behavioral decision research, and AI governance. The paper concludes by outlining a multi-level interdisciplinary research agenda for the study of judgment economies and the intelligent enterprise.

title: Digitalization and International Competitiveness: A Cross-country Exploration of the Relation between Firm-level ICT Use, Productivity and Export
affiliations: Hasselt University, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Maastricht University

detail.title: Digitalization and International Competitiveness: A Cross-country Exploration of the Relation between Firm-level ICT Use, Productivity and Export
detail.abstract: We study the relationship between ICT, total factor productivity, and export at the firm level in Belgium, France, and the Netherlands. In particular, we examine whether ICT has both a direct effect on export and an indirect effect through productivity improvements. We allow for endogeneity, unobserved heterogeneity, dynamic feedback, initial conditions, and correlations between the time-invariant random effects and between the idiosyncratic random effects. We find that ICT increases export (both at the intensive and extensive margins) everywhere, but the transmission mechanism differs between the three countries. In Belgium and the Netherlands, it is to a large extent due to improved productivity driven by ICT, whereas in France ICT affects export mainly through other unidentified (non-productive related) channels.

title: Agentic LLM-Based Simulation for Pharmaceutical Evidence Planning
affiliations: Independent and Gabelli School of Business, Fordham University

detail.title: Agentic LLM-Based Simulation for Pharmaceutical Evidence Planning

declarations.declarationOfInterest: none
declarations.ethicsApproval: n/a
declarations.funderStatement: n/a

detail.abstract: Strategic decisions resist outcome-based evaluation: consequences arrive late, are contested among stakeholders, and remain only partly observable even in retrospect. This structural feature demands a different evaluative logicone focused on the decision process itself rather than on predicted outcomes. This paper proposes agentic simulation using large language models (LLMs) as a systems research instrument for making strategic decision processes inspectable under conditions where outcome-based validation is unavailable. Drawing on the attention-based view of the firm and exploration-exploitation theory, the simulator formalizes information channels, action spaces, evaluator heterogeneity, and institutional feedback loops as explicit structural components, and treats information architecture (which signals are visible to which agents) as a first-order design variable rather than a background assumption. This design logic extends the structural-variation tradition into domains where decision actors engage in open-ended, context-sensitive reasoning that resists reduction to pre-specified rules. The approach is demonstrated through pharmaceutical real-world evidence (RWE) planning, a domain combining competitive interaction, multi-stakeholder institutional evaluation, resource allocation under uncertainty, and systematically delayed feedback. A 40-run pilot experiment, structured as a 2x2 design, varies two information channels (the visibility of evaluator criteria and the competitor's evidence state) across brandteam agents operating in a GLP-1 market scenario. Masking these channels produces asymmetric shifts in evidence-planning behaviorfeedback masking narrows the set of claim channels the agent explores, with downstream score effects driven by portfolio composition rather than broad stakeholder agreement revealing that portfolio coverage and evaluator fit are separable dimensions of strategic quality whose relative priority is shaped by the information environment agents inhabit. These findings illustrate how LLM-based agentic simulation supports strategy rehearsal and organizational learning: by making explicit what actors could see, what they searched, and what they selected across systematically varied conditions, the instrument generates strategic understanding in an auditable form before real-world consequences arrive.

title: Social Benefits and Labor Supply in the Gig Economy: Evidence from Singapore's Platform Workers Act
affiliations: University of Wisconsin-Madison, , University of California, Irvine - Paul Merage School of Business and George Washington University - School of Business

detail.title: Social Benefits and Labor Supply in the Gig Economy: Evidence from Singapore's Platform Workers Act
detail.abstract:
Digital platforms increasingly face regulatory pressure to provide more benefits to gig workers, yet little is known about how such policies affect labor supply when work participation remains flexible and discretionary. We study Singapore's Platform Workers Act as a platform governance intervention that embeds employee-like protections into ride-sharing platforms. The Act requires platform operators to contribute to the Central Provident Fund (CPF), Singapore's mandatory savings system, on behalf of participating drivers. Using trip-level data covering 1.27 million rides on Grab, we first exploit a difference-indifferences design comparing Singaporean drivers with Malaysian drivers to examine how this governance intervention reshapes platform workers' labor supply. 

We find that, following the Act's implementation, Singaporean drivers completed about 20 additional orders per month, worked 1.6 more days, and earned 13.7% more relative to Malaysian drivers. More interestingly, the response is highly heterogeneous: effects are concentrated among high-intensity drivers, with little detectable response among occasional drivers. To explain this heterogeneous response, we develop and estimate a structural model that separates workers' valuation of CPF savings from enrollment frictions. The model shows that limited participation is driven primarily by take-up frictions rather than low valuation of social benefits. Counterfactual analyses suggest that increasing contribution rates would attract few additional participants, whereas reducing enrollment costs would expand participation more effectively. These findings show that platform governance affects not only the provision of social benefits but also who can access and respond to them, highlighting the central role of implementation design in governing platform-mediated labor markets.

title: Cited-Listicle Rank-Tier Exposure, Author Type, and LLM Brand Visibility: A Two-Part Model of Selection and Prominence in Generative Engine Responses Working Paper

detail.title: Cited-Listicle Rank-Tier Exposure, Author Type, and LLM Brand Visibility: A Two-Part Model of Selection and Prominence in Generative Engine Responses Working Paper

declarations.declarationOfInterest: All authors are affiliated with Peec AI. Peec AI develops software and research tools related to Generative Engine Optimization (GEO), brand visibility, and LLM search analytics. The topic of this paper is therefore commercially relevant to Peec AI. The analysis, interpretation, and conclusions are those of the authors.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethics approval was not required because this study did not involve patients, human research participants, clinical data, surveys, experiments on individuals, or intervention with human subjects. The analysis uses proprietary LLM response, citation, and brand-level observational data collected through Peec AI’s internal monitoring infrastructure.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted as part of Peec AI’s internal research program. No external funding was received for this study.

detail.abstract: We study how exposure to repeatedly cited third-party listicles at different rank tiers relates to two outcomes in Large Language Model (LLM) responses: whether a brand is mentioned (the selection equation), and, conditional on being mentioned, where the brand appears (the prominence equation). Using chat-level panel data from three markets (B2B SaaS: 1.67M observations, 21 brands, 6 engines; Emerging MarTech: 1.27M observations, 111 brands, 7 engines; US finance: 2.80M observations, 45 brands, 3 engines), we estimate Part 1 as a Correlated Random Effects logit and Part 2 as an OLS prominence equation on the visibility = 1 subsample, both with prompt × model × date fixed effects and Mundlak brand means (Mundlak, 1978; Wooldridge, 2010). A parallel OLS specification on the full panel summarizes the joint association with the mention-count outcome. Across all three markets, higher-ranked third-party exposure is positively associated with mention probability, and top-tier exposure is associated with earlier conditional placement. The gradient is most monotonic in Emerging MarTech, concentrated at top tiers in US finance, and flatter in B2B SaaS. Author-type and lower-support estimates are interpreted as exploratory. The estimates are conditional within-brand associations, not causal effects of moving a brand's rank on a single listicle.

title: Explainability, Fairness, and Governance in Credit Risk Machine Learning: A Unified Survey and Research Agenda
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Explainability, Fairness, and Governance in Credit Risk Machine Learning: A Unified Survey and Research Agenda
detail.abstract: The application of machine learning to credit risk decisioning has accelerated dramatically over the past decade, driven by advances in gradient boosting, deep learning, and graph neural networks. However, the deployment of ML in regulated lending environments introduces three interconnected challenges that the academic literature has addressed largely in isolation: explainability (providing transparent, audit-ready reasoning for credit decisions under ECOA and Regulation B), fairness (ensuring algorithmic decisions do not produce discriminatory outcomes under civil rights law), and governance (satisfying model risk management requirements under SR 11-7 and Basel IRB frameworks). This paper presents the first unified survey synthesizing research across all three dimensions, covering 247 papers published between 2010 and 2026. We organize the survey around a taxonomy of credit risk ML systems-spanning traditional scorecard methods, ensemble and gradient boosting approaches, deep learning, graph neural networks, and large language model applications-and evaluate each against explainability, fairness, and governance criteria. We identify eight open research challenges and propose a structured research agenda for the next five years. The survey establishes that while significant progress has been made in individual dimensions, no existing system simultaneously satisfies the full set of requirements for production deployment in regulated financial services-a gap that represents the most important open problem in applied credit risk ML.

title: Cybersecurity Best Practices for Small Professional Firms
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Cybersecurity Best Practices for Small Professional Firms
detail.abstract: Small and mid-sized professional firms-accounting practices, law offices, and healthcare providersface a disproportionate cybersecurity burden. They handle highly sensitive data (financial records, legal case files, protected health information) yet typically lack dedicated IT security staff. This paper presents a practical cybersecurity framework tailored to the operational realities of professional service firms with 10 to 200 employees. Drawing on industry-specific compliance requirements (SOC 2, ABA ethics rules, HIPAA/HITECH), current threat intelligence, and real-world implementation experience, we propose a fivelayer defense model that addresses the unique workflows, software ecosystems, and regulatory environments of each vertical.

title: Hallucination Detection and Reduction in Open-source Large Language Models via the Kerimov-Alekberli Information-Geometric Framework: Empirical Evaluation on HaluEval, FEVER, and SimpleQA
affiliations: and Azerbaijan Technical University

detail.title: Hallucination Detection and Reduction in Open-source Large Language Models via the Kerimov-Alekberli Information-Geometric Framework: Empirical Evaluation on HaluEval, FEVER, and SimpleQA
detail.abstract:
Background: Hallucination—the generation of factually incorrect, internally inconsistent, or ungrounded content—remains a major barrier to the safe deployment of large language models (LLMs), particularly in high-stakes domains. Most existing hallucination-detection methods rely on external knowledge bases, model fine-tuning, or cloud-based APIs, limiting their applicability for private or fully local inference environments.

Methods: We evaluated the Kerimov–Alekberli (KA) information-geometric framework as a real-time, inference-time hallucination detector across six open-source LLMs running locally on Apple M5 Silicon hardware using Ollama v0.23.2 with Q4_K_M quantisation. The KA framework monitors the Kullback–Leibler (KL) divergence between consecutive output distributions relative to a Fisher Information Metric (FIM)-derived threshold (τ = 0.065). Hallucination events are identified through First-Passage Time (FPT) alarms triggered when generation trajectories depart from the stable Riemannian output manifold. We evaluated 120 responses (6 models × 20 questions) using prompts drawn from three established hallucination benchmarks: HaluEval (14 questions spanning Fact, Confuse, Date, Num, and Trap categories), FEVER (4 adversarial fact-verification questions), and SimpleQA (2 factual-recall questions). All prompts were classified as Hard difficulty and targeted known LLM failure modes including off-by-one numerical errors, geographical traps, and disputed-attribution confounds.

Results: The KA framework achieved a session-level hallucination detection sensitivity of 90.9% (20/22 hallucinated responses correctly flagged) with zero false positives among correct responses (0/98). Hallucination prevalence varied substantially across models. The reasoning-oriented model deepseek-r1:latest (Qwen3 chain-of-thought architecture; 5.2 GB) exhibited a 95% hallucination rate (19/20 prompts), all correctly detected by the KA framework. In contrast, gemma3:27b (17.4 GB) and gemma3:latest (4.3B; 3.3 GB) produced no hallucinated responses on the evaluated tasks. Two KA false negatives involved highly confident factual errors with KL divergence values below the detection threshold. Mean KL divergence was significantly higher for hallucinated outputs (D_KL = 0.068 ± 0.004) than for correct outputs (D_KL = 0.042 ± 0.016).

Conclusions: The KA framework provides competitive hallucination detection without requiring external knowledge bases, model fine-tuning, or cloud infrastructure, operating in real time with negligible computational overhead. The exceptionally high hallucination rate observed in deepseek-r1 suggests a potentially important trade-off between chain-of-thought reasoning depth and factual precision on concise factual queries, warranting further systematic investigation.

title: Continuous Evidence-Based Cybersecurity Maturity Assessment: A Temporal Decay Model for Automated Control Evaluation

detail.title: Continuous Evidence-Based Cybersecurity Maturity Assessment: A Temporal Decay Model for Automated Control Evaluation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: self-published
declarations.funderStatement: self-funded

detail.abstract: Existing cybersecurity maturity models assess organizational capability through point-in-time evaluations using binary or ordinal evidence classifications. This approach produces assessments that degrade in validity immediately after completion, fails to distinguish between the existence of a control and its sustained operational effectiveness, and cannot differentiate between human attestation and machine-verifiable evidence. We present a continuous maturity assessment model that addresses these limitations through three novel mechanisms: (1) a monotonically decaying freshness function that automatically reduces evidence credit as observations age, (2) a temporal spread requirement that distinguishes one-time control deployment from sustained operational practice by requiring evidence observations to span a minimum duration across independent sources, and (3) a dual-evidence attestation gate that requires convergence of human attestation and automated operational evidence before a practice can achieve full implementation status. We formalize these mechanisms as a compositional scoring function and demonstrate that the model produces maturity scores that degrade naturally in the absence of continued practice, resist gaming through batch evidence submission, and align with the Test of Design / Test of Effectiveness methodology used in professional audit engagements. The model has been implemented and deployed in a production SaaS platform serving B2B technology companies.

title: Information-Geometric Energy Eciency in Local Large Language Model Inference: Empirical Evidence from the Kerimov-Alekberli Framework on Apple Silicon
affiliations: and Azerbaijan Technical University

detail.title: Information-Geometric Energy Eciency in Local Large Language Model Inference: Empirical Evidence from the Kerimov-Alekberli Framework on Apple Silicon
detail.abstract: Background: The thermodynamic cost of local large language model (LLM) inference on consumer hardware is poorly characterised. Unlike data-centre deployments with hardware power monitors (NVML, RAPL), Apple Silicon uniedmemory systems require alternative instrumentation strategies, and no Landauergrounded framework for local inference energy has previously been validated. Methods: We deploy seven open-source LLMs (2.020.2 GB; 3.2B32.8B parameters, Q4_K_M quantisation) on a single Apple M5 MacBook Pro (32 GB unied memory, 25 GB Metal GPU VRAM) via Ollama v0.23.2, instrumenting the system with a custom telemetry daemon (1.5 s polling; top, vm_stat, ioreg, ps). We apply the KerimovAlekberli (KA) information-geometric framework, which monitors KL divergence between consecutive output distributions relative to a Fisher Information Metric (FIM)-derived threshold (τ = 0.065), and compare energy consumption against an unoptimised baseline using a unied Python code-generation benchmark. Energy estimates are grounded in Landauer's thermodynamic lower bound Emin = k B T ln 2, scaled macroscopically by an empirical power-size model. Results: KA achieves a consistent 38 % energy reduction across all seven models, saving 59 mJ (llama3.2, 2.0 GB, 55.7 tok/s) to 32,841 mJ (qwen3:32b, 20.2 GB, 2.6 tok/s) per run. Measured power draw follows a linear model P = 5.0 + 0.75 S GB W (R 2 = 0.97). Token eciency under KA ranges from 1,321 tok/J (qwen3:32b) to 8,287 tok/J (llama3.2). The First-Passage Time (FPT) anomaly detector recorded 602 KL-divergence threshold exceedances across 9,501 total inference tokens; the highest-energy model (qwen3:32b) registered 562 anomalies and the greatest absolute saving. Conclusions: These results constitute the rst empirical validation of a Landauer-grounded energy reduction mechanism in local LLM inference via an information-geometric outputdistribution stabilisation framework, with extrapolated annual savings of 105.4 kJ and 11.7 mg CO 2 per workstation.

title: From Search to Generation: How Generative AI Reshapes Marketing Outcomes
affiliations: HKUST Business School, Peking University - Guanghua School of Management and Hong Kong University of Science & Technology (HKUST) - Department of Information & Systems Management

detail.title: From Search to Generation: How Generative AI Reshapes Marketing Outcomes
detail.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is rapidly displacing search engines as the primary channel through which users acquire information and make decisions, prompting major GenAI platforms to monetize this shift by introducing commercial content alongside AI-generated outputs. As !rms are committing substantial marketing resources to GenAI, a pressing but unanswered question emerges: how does generative engine marketing (GEM) compare to search engine marketing (SEM) in shaping user behavior, and through what mechanisms? We investigate this question through a randomized controlled experiment using a custom-built system. Results show that GEM substantially outperforms SEM on both brand recognition and purchase intention, with the difference particularly pronounced for purchase intention. More importantly, the underlying mechanisms diverge fundamentally. Causal mediation analysis shows that, whereas SEM influences purchase primarily through enhanced brand recognition, GEM operates through an additional mechanism of decision delegation, whereby users perceive GenAI as an agentic artifact and consequently defer to its recommendations as sound judgments. This delegation mechanism also fundamentally alters the position effect: whereas position in SEM primarily determines visibility, position in GEM serves as an implicit signal of endorsement, such that non-top placement significantly reduces purchase intention while leaving brand recognition unaffected. Together, these findings establish GEM as a fundamentally different paradigm from SEM, carrying important implications for !rms, platforms, and regulators.

title: Layered Recursive Structure Model (LRSM) : A Unified Framework for Hierarchy, Recursion, and Structural Stabilization in Complex Systems
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: Layered Recursive Structure Model (LRSM) : A Unified Framework for Hierarchy, Recursion, and Structural Stabilization in Complex Systems

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study does not involve human subjects, personal data, or animal research, and therefore did not require ethics app
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract:
This study proposes the Layered Recursive Structure Model (LRSM), a framework that describes the configuration and interactions of theoretical groups in complex systems by integrating hierarchy and recursive structure.

Conventional analyses have relied on either hierarchical structures, causal chains, or single feedback loops in isolation. However, stable states in actual social, cognitive, and institutional systems cannot be explained by these elements treated separately. This study defines conceptual groups as Layers, Nodes, Edges, and Loops, and further introduces a hierarchy of loops (L0-L4) and Layer Recursion (recursion of layers themselves), thereby providing a unified description of multilayered and self-reinforcing structures.

Through this model, stable states are understood not as the result of a single cause, but as quasi-stable states formed by the mutual coupling of multiple recursive loops. Furthermore, causal relationships are redefined not as linear chains, but through inter-layer feedback and recursive reinforcement.

LRSM extends the object of analysis from individual elements to recursive structures, and functions as a meta-framework that makes the relationships between theories explicit. It thereby provides a unified understanding of structural problems across diverse domains-including social institutions, cognitive structures, organizational behavior, and market structures-and offers a new perspective for designing interventions.
