title: Institutional Actor Modeling in Dodona for Forecasting Central Bank Rate Decisions: Results from the April 2026 Live Campaign

detail.title: Institutional Actor Modeling in Dodona for Forecasting Central Bank Rate Decisions: Results from the April 2026 Live Campaign

contentType.other: research note. results follow up to abstract_id=6589200

detail.abstract: A prior methodology paper [1] introduced institutional actor modeling-a general framework for forecasting decisions emerging from structured deliberations among defined actors with formal rolesand evaluated its first pilot domain: reserve rate decisions for the four most prominent central banks (Bank of Japan, Federal Reserve, Bank of England, European Central Bank). In order to assess its forward looking capabilities, we applied the methodology against those banks' April 2026 central bank decisions, with forecasts publicly pre-registered seven days prior to each decision, along with daily trajectory outlooks across the publication-to-decision window, and post-decision scoring. This companion paper reports results from that first cycle of live application: we exceeded the original paper's 80.6% direction accuracy for hindcasts across 72 historical decisions, as our forecasts achieved 100% direction accuracy across the four decisions. However, we consider that result as favorable but bounded: the live sample is small, market consensus aligned with our methodology in this particular cycle, and our framework's expression of dissent at the per-actor level was less granular than the directional call. As such, we outline ongoing work to address each of those concerns. Note that this particular instance is the first cycle in a sustained program of planned forecast engineering test campaigns whose ultimate scope extends beyond central banks to a wide range of institutionaldeliberation domains.

title: Rethinking the Antitrust-Securities Interface
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong - Faculty of Law

detail.title: Rethinking the Antitrust-Securities Interface
detail.abstract: This article proposes a new theoretical framework for resolving conflicts between antitrust law and securities regulation, which is distinctive in four respects. First, it eschews the traditional approach of resolving antitrust-securities conflicts through implied antitrust immunity, which unjustifiably prioritizes securities regulation above antitrust law. Second, it argues for a narrow definition of conflict, encompassing only conduct presently authorized or required by the securities regime that also has likely and significantly anticompetitive effects; practices illegal under both antitrust law and securities regulation are thereby excluded. Third, this article builds on the literature on the antitrust-intellectual property interface to recommend a structured, rule-of-reason framework for resolving conflicts at the antitrust-securities interface. Unlike implied antitrust immunity, which automatically allows securities regulation concerns to trump antitrust concerns, the rule of reason seeks to strike a proper balance. The analysis begins by asking whether the securities practice has likely and significantly anticompetitive effects. It then inquires into the securities regulation concerns behind the conduct and whether there is a less restrictive means of addressing those concerns. Fourth, a two-stage procedure is proposed for implementing the rule of reason to resolve antitrust-securities conflicts in rulemaking and adjudication, involving the collaboration of the Securities and Exchange Commission, the Department of Justice, and the courts.

title: Fast Heston Volatility and Path-Dependent NIG Clocks

detail.title: Fast Heston Volatility and Path-Dependent NIG Clocks
detail.abstract: Fast stochastic-volatility models are expensive to simulate and calibrate when variance mean reversion and volatility-of-volatility are both large. We prove that, for a Heston/CIR fibre in this regime, the stiff diffusion has a well-posed path-dependent jump limit. The scaling is diagonal: a → ∞, ∆ a ↓ 0, and a∆ a → ∞, where a-1 is the variance relaxation time and ∆ a is the update mesh of a predictable feedback functional of the past price and activity. For frozen feedback, an exponential-affine test function diagonalizes the fast generator; the stable algebraic Riccati root is the local Lévy symbol, recovering the fast-Heston NIG exponent of Mechkov. The main contribution is to prove that these frozen symbols assemble into a self-consistent martingale problem Ψ Φt(X ≤t ,G ≤t) (p, r), where the local NIG-clock law is selected by the limiting stopped path itself. We prove tightness, identify subsequential limits, construct the limit on a common Poisson space, and establish well-posedness through inverse-Gaussian quantile estimates. The reduction also gives exact frozen-step simulation, a generalized-inverse-Gaussian posterior update for the latent activity clock, and uniform convergence of controlled values over compact feedback classes.

title: PMO Maturity and Organization Success: A Critical Review of Traditional Indicators
affiliations: Fundação Getulio Vargas

detail.title: PMO Maturity and Organization Success: A Critical Review of Traditional Indicators

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that there are no personal, professional, institutional, or financial relationships that could reasonably be perceived as having influenced the research, analysis, or conclusions reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This study is a theoretical and bibliographic review based exclusively on published literature and publicly available documents. It did not involve human participants, patients, personal data collection, or identifiable individual records. Therefore, ethics committee approval was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted without external funding and did not receive any specific grant from public, commercial, or not-for-profit funding agencies.

detail.abstract: This article critically examines the relationship between Project Management Office (PMO) maturity and organizational success. Its central thesis is that traditional maturity models measure procedural discipline with relative precision, but are structurally insufficient to capture the PMO's substantive contribution to organizational value. The literature shows, on the one hand, that PMOs are contingent, heterogeneous, and evolutionary structures; on the other, that project success can no longer be reduced to time, cost, and scope. Methodologically, the study adopts a critical, non-systematic but explicitly delimited literature review, combined with documentary analysis of institutional benchmarks. Under an analytically econometric-informed lens, it argues that "PMO maturity" and "organizational success" are latent constructs observed through imperfect proxies, exposing the field to measurement error, reverse causality, omitted-variable bias, and unobserved heterogeneity. As a theoretical contribution, the article proposes a measurement-and-inference critique of the literature, distinguishes between procedural and substantive maturity, presents a four-level maturity typology, and formulates an expanded evaluation framework oriented toward governance, benefits, adaptation, and value creation.

title: vol-eval: A Python Package for Volatility Forecast Evaluation, with a Re-analysis of 30 Published Comparison Papers (2018-2025)
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: vol-eval: A Python Package for Volatility Forecast Evaluation, with a Re-analysis of 30 Published Comparison Papers (2018-2025)
detail.abstract:
This paper introduces vol-eval, an open-source Python package that ships the canonical battery of significance tests for volatility forecast evaluation. The battery covers QLIKE, MSE, MAE, Mincer-Zarnowitz R^2, Diebold-Mariano (1995) with Newey-West HAC standard errors, the Hansen-Lunde-Nason (2011) Model Confidence Set with stationary bootstrap, Hansen's (2005) Superior Predictive Ability test with three p-value variants, White's (2000) Reality Check, and the Giacomini-White (2006) Conditional Predictive Ability test. The package follows a functional API with typed result objects, ships under MIT license, and is verified by 45 unit tests including cross-validation against the arch package's reference implementation.

     We apply vol-eval in two settings. The first is a self-contained seven-model horse race on S&P 500 realized volatility, using the panel of Khan (2026, "Volatility Forecasting with Machine Learning," SSRN 6663418). The second is a sample of 30 published volatility-forecasting comparison papers from 2018-2025, drawn from the Journal of Financial Econometrics, three open-access MDPI venues (Mathematics, Risks, Journal of Risk and Financial Management), and arXiv q-fin.

     Three layered findings emerge. First, a disclosure crisis. The strict-reading mean Reproducibility Disclosure Score across the 30-paper sample is 0.47, materially lower than the 0.78 reported by Khan (2026, "Machine Learning in Quantitative Finance: A Systematic Review," SSRN 6562398) for the broader 99-paper ML-finance sample. Zero of the 30 papers ship both code and publicly accessible data. Second, a methodological gap. 27 of 30 papers (90%) declare a headline winner without applying any formal predictive-accuracy test (DM, MCS, SPA, or Reality Check). Third, a robustness gap. In the 14 papers we could reproduce (the strict-RDS-1 subset, where data is publicly accessible), 12 paper-claimed wins (86%) do not survive significance testing under the vol-eval battery. Only one paper has its claim survive in full, with one additional paper showing partial survival on a subset of assets. Each per-paper reproduction and its caveats are documented in detail.

     The full vol-eval source, the per-paper reproductions, and an audit script that re-derives every numerical claim in this paper from JSON outputs are released at github.com/ayk5511/vol-eval, scoring 2 on the Reproducibility Disclosure Score rubric of Khan (2026).

title: Dynamic Personalized Assortment Planning under Differential Privacy and Inventory Constraints
affiliations: , City University of Hong Kong (CityU), City University of Hong Kong and University of British Columbia

detail.title: Dynamic Personalized Assortment Planning under Differential Privacy and Inventory Constraints
detail.abstract:
While dynamic assortment personalization drives revenue, its reliance on granular customer data raises severe privacy concerns. We address this tension by examining a profit-maximizing firm that offers personalized assortments over a finite horizon, subject to strict privacy constraints. Customer choices follow a contextual multinomial logit model with unknown parameters, in which utilities depend on both item features and customer-specific contextual information. We study privacy-preserving online learning under two differential privacy models: central differential privacy (CDP), where the platform is trusted to access raw data but must protect its public outputs, and local differential privacy (LDP), where the platform is untrusted and only privatized client-side messages are revealed. 
      We first consider the infinite-inventory environment under both stationary and non-stationary context arrivals. In the stationary setting, we develop epoch-based private active-elimination algorithms under both CDP and LDP. In the non-stationary setting, we develop private learning algorithms that allow for continual, fully online updates without storing or reprocessing the entire dataset, based on an online Newton step with online-to-confidence-set conversion (for CDP) and a stochastic-gradient-based private learning method (for LDP). Compared with the maximum-likelihood-estimation-based approach in Cho and Sun (2024), our methods not only circumvent the need to solve full-sample likelihood problems but also provide regret bounds with better scaling. 
      We then extend the framework to the inventory-constrained setting under both CDP and LDP. Under CDP, we integrate private online parameter learning with dual mirror descent. Under LDP, we extend the stochastic-gradient-based private learning method to the inventory-constrained setting. Our analysis establishes sublinear regret bounds across the proposed privacy models and operating regimes, cleanly demonstrating that rigorous privacy guarantees can be achieved without significantly compromising revenue optimality.

title:
The Bithumb-Binance BTC-numéraire Premium: 
A Theoretical Framework with Calibrated Simulation Evidence on BNB Chain Tokens
affiliations: Betalabs Inc

detail.title:
The Bithumb-Binance BTC-numéraire Premium: 
A Theoretical Framework with Calibrated Simulation Evidence on BNB Chain Tokens

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has been active in the blockchain and Web3 industry since 2017, including current roles at Betalabs Inc. and a former CEO position at CyworldZ. The author has no direct equity, advisory, or paid relationship with any cryptocurrency exchange (Bithumb, Binance, OKX, Bybit) referenced in this paper, and has no position in the Venus (XVS) token. As a long-term industry participant, the author may hold incidental positions in major cryptocurrencies referenced herein. The paper uses synthetic data only; no proprietary exchange data was accessed.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding.

detail.abstract:
This paper redefines the price discrepancy between the Korean exchange Bithumb and the global exchange Binance using a new measure of the kimchi premium expressed in BTC units, denoted π^BTC_X(t), accompanied by calibrated simulation evidence based on daily series from 2020 to 2025.

The conventional KRW-denominated premium, π^KRW_X(t), confounds multiple forces—including exchange rate dynamics, capital controls, stablecoin premia, and remittance delays—making it difficult to isolate token-specific asymmetric demand shocks.

As a remedy, this paper proposes:


    π^BTC_X(t) = ( P^B_X / P^B_BTC ) / ( P^N_X / P^N_BTC ) − 1


where P^B and P^N denote prices on Bithumb and on Binance, respectively. Proposition 1 (FX-noise cancellation) proves that this measure is invariant to the exchange rate and to stablecoin-level fluctuations through numerator–denominator cancellation.

The empirical objects of study are: (i) BNB, the gas token of BNB Chain, listed on Bithumb on May 27, 2021; (ii) Venus (XVS), a BSC DeFi governance token; and (iii) ETH, which serves as the ERC-20 baseline.


To control for token-specific price volatility, the paper introduces the normalised variance ratio:


    ρ_X = Var[ π^BTC_X ] / Var[ Δ log P_X ]


OLS regressions are estimated with Newey–West HAC standard errors, and asymmetric volatility is modelled using an EGARCH(1,1) specification with Student-t innovations.

The simulation findings suggest that: (1) the satoshi premium exhibits approximately half the standard deviation of the KRW premium, providing evidence that FX-related noise is substantially removed; (2) after normalisation, both BNB (ρ = 1.13) and XVS (ρ = 0.82) exceed the ETH baseline (ρ = 0.42), tentatively rejecting the hypothesis that BSC tokens benefit from superior arbitrage efficiency; (3) after HAC adjustment, the Korean regulatory dummy loses statistical significance, while the global-shock dummy remains highly significant (p < 0.001); (4) the EGARCH leverage parameter is γ̂ = −0.073 (p < 0.05), supporting the asymmetric volatility hypothesis H2.

title: A Demand–Cost Pass-Through Identity
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Demand–Cost Pass-Through Identity
detail.abstract: This paper studies the link between cost and demand pass-through in oligopoly. When market size and the cost shifter both enter additively, market-size and marginal-cost shifts act as equivalent perturbations to the equilibrium markup, and the two pass-through rates sum to one. The identity holds in any symmetric oligopoly nested in the standard conduct-parameter framework, extends to asymmetric oligopoly in aggregated form, and is independent of conduct. I characterize the demand and cost specifications under which the identity holds and fails, and discuss when it can be invoked as a working restriction or used as a diagnostic in applied work.

title: Information Networks and Mutual Fund Position Decisions: Evidence from Common Holdings in China's A-Share Market

detail.title: Information Networks and Mutual Fund Position Decisions: Evidence from Common Holdings in China's A-Share Market
detail.abstract: Mutual fund managers exchange information with peers and adjust their portfolios in response. Using quarterly top-ten holdings disclosures of actively managed equity and equity-biased hybrid funds in China's A-share market from 2005Q1 to 2020Q4, this paper constructs information networks based on common heavy holdings and examines how network position changes affect individual funds' own position decisions. After controlling for publicly available stock-level information, I document a robust positive association between a fund's position changes and the average position changes of other funds connected to it through a shared heavy stock-consistent with a network information effect. The effect is stronger for funds and networks endowed with richer information resources (older, larger, and more numerous network peers) and weaker for funds whose own managers exhibit high turnover, suggesting that fund managers substitute network information for their own active research. The network information effect is also markedly stronger in bear markets than in bull markets, consistent with managers herding through network channels during periods of heightened uncertainty. Finally, shared educational background is identified as one specific channel through which information flows in the network. The findings extend the application of information network theory in finance and offer a behavioral perspective on the much-discussed phenomenon of mutual fund "grouping" in China.

title:
From Passion, Sympathy, and Judgment to Humanistic Intelligence 
David Hume's Treatise of Human Nature as a Philosophical Foundation for RHIS
affiliations: Independent

detail.title:
From Passion, Sympathy, and Judgment to Humanistic Intelligence 
David Hume's Treatise of Human Nature as a Philosophical Foundation for RHIS
detail.abstract:
This paper argues that David Hume's A Treatise of Human Nature provides a philosophical foundation for RHIS, the Refine Humanistic Intelligence System. RHIS is not presented as a personality typology, a moral ranking scheme, or a behavioral prediction tool in the narrow sense. It is proposed as a structural framework for analyzing how human cognition, emotion, judgment, action, expression, and field pressure operate together in real situations. Hume's project, especially his attempt to introduce an experimental method of reasoning into moral subjects, offers a crucial conceptual precursor to such a framework. 
     
     The paper develops three central correspondences between Hume's theory of human nature and RHIS. First, Hume's claim that reason does not provide the original impulse to action but serves the passions is interpreted as a philosophical basis for the RHIS distinction between logical computation and emotionalmotivational activation. Second, Hume's account of sympathy, vivacity, resemblance, contiguity, and habit is used to explain why emotionally vivid information can propagate through groups and why digital information manipulation often works by activating existing passions rather than by producing purely rational persuasion. Third, Hume's idea of a steady and general point of view is interpreted as a precursor to the RHIS concept of judgment-reference stability: the capacity to maintain a relatively stable evaluative anchor under field pressure. 

     The paper then extends this Humean foundation to contemporary information manipulation. It argues that exploitative information operations should not be understood only as false-content problems. They can also operate as structural interventions into human nature: activating passion, intensifying sympathy transmission, weakening judgment-reference stability, and directing action. RHIS translates these philosophical insights into Chen | RHIS Hume Foundation a modern humanistic intelligence framework capable of describing cognitive vulnerability, adversarial field pressure, and judgment protection without reducing persons to static psychological labels. 
     
     The paper concludes that the ethical purpose of RHIS is not to exploit human nature but to understand and protect it. Hume's account of human nature helps explain why human beings are influenceable; RHIS aims to make such influence structurally visible, auditable, and accountable.

title: AI Procurement as Competitive Advantage: Build, Buy, Partner, and the New Make-or-Buy Decision

detail.title: AI Procurement as Competitive Advantage: Build, Buy, Partner, and the New Make-or-Buy Decision
detail.abstract: The classic make-or-buy decision-central to corporate strategy since Coase (1937) and Williamson (1985)-takes on new dimensions in the artificial intelligence era. Traditional transaction cost analysis assumes that the boundaries of the firm are determined by the relative costs of market transactions versus internal coordination. AI procurement introduces complications that the original framework did not anticipate: the asset specificity of fine-tuned models and proprietary training data, the measurement problem in evaluating AI vendor quality before deployment, the holdup risks created by API dependency on foundation model providers, and the talent market dynamics that make in-house AI development prohibitively expensive for most enterprises. This paper revisits transaction cost economics for AI procurement and proposes the AI Procurement Mode Framework (APMF), a decision framework with four modes-Build (proprietary models developed in-house), Buy (commercial APIs and SaaS AI products), Partner (co-development arrangements with AI vendors), and Compose (combining open-source and commercial components into hybrid architectures)-that extends the traditional binary make-or-buy decision to capture the richer set of options available in the AI era. The framework maps the conditions under which each mode delivers competitive advantage versus commodity parity, using four decision variables: strategic differentiation potential, data proprietary advantage, organizational AI maturity, and acceptable dependency risk. The framework is illustrated through case analysis across financial services, retail, and healthcare enterprises. The paper concludes with implications for Chief Technology Officers structuring AI procurement strategies, procurement leaders evaluating AI vendor relationships, and corporate development teams assessing AI partnership and acquisition opportunities.

title: Patient Access Readiness as a Governable Signal: A Conceptual Model for Responsible AI Adoption in Healthcare Operations

detail.title: Patient Access Readiness as a Governable Signal: A Conceptual Model for Responsible AI Adoption in Healthcare Operations

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is the originator of the AI-PAR conceptual model discussed in this paper. No financial conflicts of interest are reported. The paper is presented as conceptual model development and does not report a live product deployment, paid implementation, clinical intervention, or validated commercial outcome.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This paper does not report human-subjects research, patient data, protected health information, clinical intervention, live deployment findings, or patient-level outcomes. No PHI, payer data, production EHR data, identity verification data, or payment processing data were accessed, analyzed, stored, or used. Therefore, ethics approval or IRB review was not required.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding was received for this paper. The research and conceptual development were independently conducted by the author.
declarations.clinicalTrialRegistration: Not applicable. This paper does not report a clinical trial, patient intervention, clinical experiment, or registered study. No clinical trial registration number applies.

detail.abstract: Patient access is a critical but often under-theorized site of artificial intelligence adoption in healthcare operations. As health systems explore AI-enabled tools for scheduling, eligibility verification, prior authorization, financial clearance, patient communication, and revenue cycle workflows, many lack a structured way to determine whether their access environments are operationally, ethically, and organizationally ready for automation. This paper develops the concept of patient access readiness as a multidomain, governable signal rather than a narrow scheduling status or fragmented set of administrative tasks. Using conceptual model development, applied health information systems analysis, and synthesis of healthcare AI governance, workforce, equity, and revenue cycle literature, the paper proposes AI-PAR, Artificial Intelligence for Patient Access Readiness, as a conceptual model for responsible AI adoption in front-end healthcare operations. The model includes five readiness domains: operational workflow, data and technology, governance and compliance, staff capacity and culture, and equity and patient reality. It also introduces a three-layer architectural concept consisting of a patient-facing Readiness Credential, a Readiness Workflow, and a Staff Readiness Dashboard. Together, these elements position readiness as something healthcare organizations must define, assemble, measure, and govern before AI tools are deployed. The paper contributes a conceptual foundation for evaluating AI readiness in patient access and proposes a future research agenda involving expert review, simulation, design-partner validation, equity testing, and narrow governed pilots. AI-PAR is presented as an early-stage conceptual model and simulated prototype concept, not as a live clinical product, compliance certification, or validated intervention.

title: Sensitivity-Engine Derivative Surrogates: Greek-Regularized and Boundary-Aware Supervision

detail.title: Sensitivity-Engine Derivative Surrogates: Greek-Regularized and Boundary-Aware Supervision
detail.abstract:
This paper presents a derivative-surrogate learning framework built on an earlier sensitivity-engine sequence consisting of BSE, DSE, NDSE, and DBSE, and studies that framework in a first completed empirical implementation. The purpose is not to displace established pricing theory or classical numerical methods, but to transfer pricing structure into supervision. Earlier papers in the sequence provide exact or semi-structured labels for prices, first-order Greeks, mixed second-order Greeks, digital weights, conditional-law blocks, and boundary-sensitive distributional terms under deterministic or stochastic discounting. The present paper organizes those objects into a unified learning framework for derivative pricing, hedging, and local risk approximation.
Methodologically, the paper formulates structured losses and architectures that train on prices together with selected sensitivities and, where appropriate, with boundary-aware auxiliary targets. Greek-regularized losses are interpreted as weighted Sobolev-type objectives. Multi-head decompositions are matched to the product structure already present in DSE and NDSE. Near nonsmooth exercise regions, DBSE motivates mollified targets, adaptive boundary sampling, and auxiliary digital heads. Under stochastic discounting, NDSE motivates measure-aware labels and low-dimensional term-structure encodings that preserve the distinction between the spot leg and strike leg. The framework is therefore broader than the present empirical implementation, while the free-data study reported here tests its price-Greek and boundary-aware components in a controlled setting.
The empirical study uses public S&P 500, Treasury, and implied-volatility data to construct daily market states, then generates synthetic option labels from a Black–Scholes–Merton teacher on a fixed maturitymoneyness grid. Three surrogate specifications are compared: a price-only model, a Greek-regularized model, and a boundary-aware Greek-regularized model. Relative to the price-only baseline, structured supervision improves Delta and Gamma accuracy and reduces local hedging dispersion and tail loss. In the completed empirical study, the boundary-aware specification (Model C) delivers the most favorable overall performance among the three specifications within the present design, with the best global price RMSE, local price RMSE, Delta accuracy, and hedging-dispersion and tail-risk metrics. The Greek-regularized non-boundary specification (Model B) remains a useful conservative benchmark because it retains the best Gamma accuracy. The evidence is therefore consistent with the view that sensitivity-engine-guided learning is most useful through local risk fidelity and hedge robustness, and that boundary-aware supervision can be effective when tuned carefully rather than imposed too aggressively.

title: Multistakeholder Initiatives and Global Governance
affiliations: University of Hamburg

detail.title: Multistakeholder Initiatives and Global Governance
detail.abstract: In the efforts to establish a system of Global Governance at an international level, Multistakeholder Initiatives (MSIs) play a crucial role. In this chapter, we first define MSIs. Against the backdrop of the multitude of different MSIs, we then present a typology before discussing various examples of MSIs. This is followed by a critical analysis of the current discussion on MSIs, in which we examine their contributions to sustainable development as well as their limitations. The chapter concludes with a brief summary and an outlook.

reference: LSE Legal Studies Working Paper No. 3/2026
title: Putting Power Back in the 'Separation of Powers'
affiliations: London School of Economics - Law School

detail.title: Putting Power Back in the 'Separation of Powers'

publicationDetails.detailsText: LSE Legal Studies Working Paper No. 3/2026
publicationDetails.journalName: LSE Law School Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: This chapter reconceptualises the principle of separation of powers by rebalancing attention from institutional "separation" to agential "power." Traditional accounts have treated separation of powers as a structural arrangement among branches designed primarily to prevent tyranny. By contrast, this chapter argues that the principle is best understood as a general grammar for managing power within a purposive constitutional order. Modern constitutions pursue multiple enduring purposes and must contend with a dynamic constellation of powerful agents capable of realising or frustrating those aims. When a constitution chooses to "domesticate" an agent-transforming it into a constitutional actor charged with performing public functions-the principle of separation of powers supplies the managerial logic through which that agent's power is calibrated. Drawing on a taxonomy of agential power and its modalities-capacity calibration, field structuring, incentive modulation, and perlocution-the chapter shows that separation of powers operates not merely by allocating functions or insulating institutions, but by organising how power flows across a constitutional system. On this account, independence, accountability, checks and balances, comity, and collaboration are techniques rather than ends. The principle is instrumentally oriented yet normatively thin: it can serve liberal, socialist, theocratic, or even authoritarian purposes, while retaining a conceptual core. Separation of powers thus emerges as a dynamic practice of constitutional domestication rather than a static institutional blueprint.

title: A structured data-driven methodology for instantaneous fuel consumption estimation on ships using shaft power meter (SPM) signals
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of Strathclyde, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Pukyong National University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A structured data-driven methodology for instantaneous fuel consumption estimation on ships using shaft power meter (SPM) signals
detail.abstract: Accurate estimation of ship fuel consumption is important for operational optimisation and emissions management,but onboard datasets are often affected by irregular sampling, missing values, and sensor noise. This study presents a structured data-driven methodology for estimating instantaneous fuel consumption from shaft power meter signals using shaft RPM, torque, and derived shaft power as inputs.The methodology combines partition-local preprocessing, fold-consistent scaling, blocked stratified cross-validation, and fixed-length autoregressive windows to enable controlled comparison of exogenous-only and autoregressive models using 322,360 timestamped samples from a single vessel.Ridge regression, random forest, LSTM, and Conv1D models were compared, with hyperparameter. A baseline ordinary least squares (OLS) regression using shaft power alone was included for reference.Performance was assessed in both value and first-difference domains. Random forest achieved the strongest value-domain performance under window-level mean RMSE (45.15 ± 0.15 kg/h). Among neural models, the Conv1Dnetwork,trained under recursive rollout, gave the best value-domain result (48.26 ± 1.18 kg/h), while teacher-forced Conv1D performed best in first-difference reconstruction. The results show that estimator ranking depends both on whether emphasis is placed on absolute reconstruction accuracy or short-term temporal fidelity and on the metric chosen as the primary basis for selection.

title: From Place-Based to Quasi-Place-Based: Implications of China's Special Economic Zones Program
affiliations: Peking University, Peking University, Peking University and Peking University

detail.title: From Place-Based to Quasi-Place-Based: Implications of China's Special Economic Zones Program
detail.abstract: Micro-data and geographic mapping are used to analyze the recent evolution of China's Special Economic Zones (SEZs) program. Our analysis reveals that SEZ policies have promoted firm registrations within SEZs; however, their impact on the intensity of nighttime light in these zones has been modest in recent years. This discrepancy stems from the fact that a large number of registered firms no longer conduct their operations within the SEZs. We attribute this phenomenon to the growing prominence of the service sector, where firms register in SEZs to reap policy benefits but place little emphasis on the geographic locations of these zones. Finally, we discuss the implications of this decoupling between firm registrations and actual operations for regional development and policy design.

title: A mechanics-informed digital twin framework for state prediction of walking-type underwater leveling machines
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A mechanics-informed digital twin framework for state prediction of walking-type underwater leveling machines
detail.abstract: Accurate pose control of walking type underwater leveling machines is critical for rubble foundation-bed preparation in gravity caisson wharf construction. However, experience-based control cannot easily adapt to alternating support states, uncertain seabed reactions, hydraulic actuation delays, and hydrodynamic disturbances. This paper proposes a residual physics-informed digital twin framework for next cycle state prediction and pose control assistance of a dual-carrier underwater leveling machine. The framework integrates real time monitoring data, a condensed rigid body prior, and a residual physics-informed neural network. It predicts the carrier attitude, translational motion, and representative cylinder stroke responses. A case study at the Nanhai operation area of Jieyang Port shows that the proposed method outperforms LSTM, GRU, and a physics-only solver, and reduces the mean normalized RMSE to 0.041. The predicted pose deviation and roll-rate are then used for four-colour risk warning and correction guidance. The framework therefore provides an interpretable and adaptive solution for intelligent underwater construction.

title: Integrated Overtaking Model and Safety Analysis for Truck Platooning Requirements on Two-lane Undivided Highways
affiliations: University of Wyoming

detail.title: Integrated Overtaking Model and Safety Analysis for Truck Platooning Requirements on Two-lane Undivided Highways
detail.abstract: Truck platooning is a promising solution for enhancing efficiency and reducing fuel consumption in freight transportation. However, overtaking truck platoons poses safety challenges that need to be addressed. This paper employs an overtaking model incorporate lane change dynamics, and a collision risk assessment to evaluate the safety risks involved in overtaking truck platoons. The safety assessment is presented through a numerical analysis which considers three aspects: roadway geometry, traffic conditions, and driver behavior. Scenarios representing different truck platoon lengths, driver behavior, and opposing traffic conditions are evaluated, highlighting their impact on safety. Two major findings from the assessment are that the overtaking distance and time increase linearly as truck platoon length increases, and potential driver hesitation and the presence of opposing vehicles are shown to increase collision risks. Safety implications are that the length of truck platoons needs to be regulated on two-lane undivided highways; and driver behavior should be considered in safety assessment and regulation of truck platooning, but further investigations are needed. From a perspective of overtaking, this paper emphasizes the need for safety guidelines and regulations for truck platooning. Policymakers, transportation agencies, and industry stakeholders may utilize the findings to establish standardized safety measures and protocols.

title: Deciding Truck Platooning Operational Rules with Stochastic Approximation for Vehicle Safe Overtaking on Two-lane Undivided Highways
affiliations: University of Wyoming

detail.title: Deciding Truck Platooning Operational Rules with Stochastic Approximation for Vehicle Safe Overtaking on Two-lane Undivided Highways

declarations.funderStatement: This work was partially sponsored by the Center for Transformative Infrastructure Preservation and Sustainability (CTIPS). CTIPS is funded by a grant from the US Department of Transportation’s University Transportation Centers Program, Grant No. 69A3552348308 (IIJA / BIL).

detail.abstract: Truck platooning is a promising technology to improve freight transport efficiency. However, this technology has primarily been explored on multi-lane divided highways, neglecting potential applications on two-lane undivided highways prevalent in rural areas. This paper addresses the challenges of deploying truck platooning on such highways, focusing on overtaking safety. We formulate safe overtaking via stochastic approximation as a feasibility problem. An algorithm is proposed to determine operational rules for truck platooning, considering factors including traffic flow, road segment geometry, and vehicle dynamics. Values for truck platooning operational parameters such as speed, inter-truck following gap, and number of trucks in platoon are decided which ensure overall overtaking safety. The algorithm is iterative and depends on first order information, avoiding possible complex computations of stochastic objective with respect to truck platooning operational parameters. The algorithm is general and adapts to different roadway and traffic conditions and weights on platooning parameters. We show that computation of the algorithm is linear in sample size used in approximation. Simulations show that the algorithm-generated platooning rules offer an overtaking safety guarantee of up to 93% on a straight and flat road segment with sparse traffic.

title: Material Change in Circumstance, Force Majeure, Impossibility, and Related Doctrines: A Comparative Law and Economics Evaluation of the Impact of Recent Shocks on Private Contracting
affiliations: and

detail.title: Material Change in Circumstance, Force Majeure, Impossibility, and Related Doctrines: A Comparative Law and Economics Evaluation of the Impact of Recent Shocks on Private Contracting
detail.abstract:
This research addresses how shocks to markets impact private contracting. We compare how private contracting, and judicial systems have responded to Brexit, Covid 19, and the war in Ukraine. The UK, the US, France, and Germany are compared in terms of the legal doctrines that excuse performance due to a market-shocking event. We broadly look at how material change in circumstance, improvision, force majeure, frustration of purpose, and impossibility have been viewed by courts in response to Brexit, Covid-19, and the war in Ukraine. These shocks to markets frustrated the performance of some types of contracts and led to judicial intervention when a party sought an excuse from performing a contract.

We consider the economic impact of doctrines that excuse performance of contractual duties and examine how risk preferences are reflected in private contracting and in judicial applications of these doctrines. This analysis shows how distinct risk preferences among individuals and firms influence contract drafting and performance. Additionally, we suggest that states have adopted risk preferences which are reflected in the development and judicial applications of these doctrines.

When there is a systemwide shock to markets, private parties may face a significantly changed economic outlook for the contracts they have entered. Systemic shocks such as political devolution, health pandemics, and war may make some contracts impossible to perform, economically wasteful to perform, or asymmetrically risky to perform. Private parties and states can adjust their approaches to contracting and contract enforcement to limit the impact of shocks on markets and private contracting. When looking at this decision to adopt a specific approach, ex ante and ex post responses must be weighed against each other. This analysis relates to ex ante risk evaluations by individuals, firms, and states, how much information asymmetry is present in the negotiation stage, transaction costs due to shocks and in anticipation of shocks, the ability of court systems to efficiently function, and the functioning of free markets, and ex post applications of these doctrines, which excuse performance.

By considering private and public responses to Brexit, Covid 19, and the war in Ukraine, we identify how risk preferences may play a role in parties’ decisions. We consider 1. A private party's ex ante decision to enter into and negotiate contracts and allocate potential future risks between contracting parties before they materialize, 2. How private parties make decisions ex post, after a shock representing a risk has occurred, which creates economic uncertainty and an associated increase in performance costs, 3. How states ex ante develop doctrines related to the impact of shocks on private contracting, which can be expressed through the law, which itself reflects risk preference, and 4. judicial interpretations of these doctrines when they are being asserted by private parties seeking an excuse from performance, allocate risk between parties to a contract. We consider the relevant statutory and case law in France, Germany, the UK, and the US to demonstrate how legal systems use doctrines related to excuse of performance. Additionally, we examine how these doctrines have been reinforced or refined by the courts and legislation when states face shocks and their corresponding impacts on private businesses.

title: TASMAC 2.0: A Phased Structural Reform Framework for Tamil Nadu's State Liquor Distribution System
affiliations: Muthayammal Engineering College

detail.title: TASMAC 2.0: A Phased Structural Reform Framework for Tamil Nadu's State Liquor Distribution System

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author holds personal investment positions in United Spirits Limited referenced in Section 4.7. This is disclosed for full transparency. Recommendations were developed independently based solely on international evidence and fiscal analysis. No affiliation with any political party, government body or liquor industry entity.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a policy analysis study based entirely on publicly available secondary data. No human participants or primary data collection involved.
declarations.funderStatement: No external funding. Research conducted independently using publicly available data from Tamil Nadu State Budget documents, WHO publications, and international monopoly annual reports.

detail.abstract:
Tamil Nadu's state-owned liquor monopoly, TASMAC, generates approximately ₹48,344 crore annually — representing 1.53% of state GSDP and nearly 15% of own tax revenue. While fiscally significant, the social costs of the current retail monopoly model — addiction, domestic violence, political corruption in licensing, and public health burden — arguably exceed revenue benefits when properly externality-adjusted. 

This paper proposes a phased 15-year structural reform converting TASMAC from a retail monopoly maximising revenue into a wholesale regulatory body minimising harm, drawing on WHO-endorsed Nordic alcohol monopoly models (Sweden's Systembolaget, Norway's Vinmonopolet, Finland's Alko) and the British Columbia hybrid wholesale-retail model. 

The proposed TASMAC 2.0 framework introduces eight policy pillars: TASMAC wholesale-only restructuring, population-formula corporate retail licensing, RBI-style Fit and Proper promoter vetting excluding political actors, Aadhaar-linked monthly purchase caps, addiction-gateway price floors, full digital supply chain audit, brand experience zones for premium manufacturers, and a mandatory social repair fund.

Revenue replacement pathways totalling ₹48,000–55,000 crore by 2040 are identified across heritage tourism, GST compliance recovery, IT sector expansion, and property tax reform. Each reform phase is designed to be independently implementable across Tamil Nadu's four-to-five year political cycles, making the framework survivable across government changes. 

The paper argues the Bihar prohibition comparison is structurally inapplicable and that the true policy choice is not between TASMAC and prohibition but between a poorly designed state monopoly and a properly designed one.

title: Hybrid Pension Liabilities under Stochastic Interest Rates and Default Risk
affiliations: Qilu Institute of Technology, Qilu Institute of Technology, Shandong Normal University and Corvinus University Budapest

detail.title: Hybrid Pension Liabilities under Stochastic Interest Rates and Default Risk
detail.abstract: This paper develops a stochastic framework for valuing hybrid pension liabilities under stochastic interest rates and sponsor default risk. Building on the hybrid pension model of Broeders et al. (2013), we replace the Vasicek interest rate process with a Cox–Ingersoll–Ross (CIR) specification to ensure non-negative and mean-reverting interest rates, and incorporate a reduced-form defaultable bond framework following Bielecki et al. (2006). The model integrates overlapping generations, stochastic asset returns, and defaultable fixed-income investments within a unified asset–liability structure. Through stochastic simulations, we examine how interest rate dynamics, default risk, and pension hybridization jointly affect long-term liability valuation. The results show that pension liabilities under the CIR specification are systematically higher than those generated under the Vasicek benchmark, implying that simplified interest rate models may underestimate long-horizon pension obligations. In addition, greater exposure to defaultable bonds increases liability volatility and amplifies solvency risk under adverse financial conditions. The findings further indicate that stronger defined-contribution components increase pension liability sensitivity to financial market fluctuations. Overall, the framework provides a tractable approach for analyzing pension sustainability and risk-sensitive asset–liability management in evolving financial systems.

title: Digital Infrastructure and Supply Chain Resilience in the Low-Altitude Economy: Empirical Evidence from China
affiliations: Chongqing Jiaotong University, Chongqing Jiaotong University, Chongqing Jiaotong University, Chongqing Jiaotong University and Chongqing Jiaotong University

detail.title: Digital Infrastructure and Supply Chain Resilience in the Low-Altitude Economy: Empirical Evidence from China
detail.abstract: Under the guidance of the Digital China strategy, digital infrastructure is driving the transformation and upgrading of industries across the board. As a strategic emerging sector heavily reliant on continuous connectivity and real-time data exchange, the low-altitude economy places exceptional emphasis on fostering and enhancing supply chain resilience. Exploring how telecommunications and digital infrastructure development strengthens supply chain resilience in this sector carries substantial policy and practical implications. Drawing on panel data from 31 provincial-level administrative regions in China spanning 2015 to 2023, this study establishes a four-dimensional evaluation system for digital infrastructure, specifically covering telecommunications network infrastructure, digital facilities, and factor inputs/outputs. It then systematically investigates the impact of digital infrastructure construction on supply chain resilience and its underlying mechanisms. The empirical findings reveal that: (1) Digital infrastructure construction significantly improves supply chain resilience in the low-altitude economy; (2) By elevating supply chain operational efficiency and stimulating digital technological innovation, telecommunications infrastructure effectively reinforces resilience; (3) The positive impact is more pronounced in western regions, small and medium-sized enterprises, non-state-owned enterprises, and manufacturing firms. This study provides critical insights for policymakers in regulating spectrum allocation, infrastructure sharing, and ICT investments to enhance supply chain resilience in emerging strategic industries.

title: The Impact of VAT Empowerment Policy Reform on Corporate Digital Transformation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, China University of Political Science and Law and China University of Political Science and Law

detail.title: The Impact of VAT Empowerment Policy Reform on Corporate Digital Transformation
detail.abstract: Against the backdrop of the deepening development of the digital economy, corporate digital transformation has become an important direction for promoting high-quality enterprise development. However, its advancement remains constrained by factors such as capital investment, technological capability, and organizational change. China’s VAT credit refund policy, as an important instrument for reducing taxes and fees for enterprises, has a significant positive empowering effect on corporate digital transformation. Taking A-share listed companies in Shanghai and Shenzhen from 2014 to 2021 as the research sample, this paper examines the impact of VAT empowerment policy on corporate digital transformation. The findings show that the VAT credit refund policy significantly promotes corporate digital transformation; it affects corporate digital transformation by increasing cash flow, alleviating financing constraints, promoting innovation investment, and upgrading the human-capital structure; and the promoting effect of this empowerment policy differs significantly across ownership types and degrees of industry competition. The VAT credit refund empowerment policy is a strong signal from the government in support of enterprise development. Enterprises should make effective use of the policy to promote their own transformation, enhance market competitiveness, and achieve long-term development.

title: Algorithmic Mediation and the Erosion of Commitment: Reconceptualising High-commitment HRM Systems in the Age of Artificial Intelligence
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: Algorithmic Mediation and the Erosion of Commitment: Reconceptualising High-commitment HRM Systems in the Age of Artificial Intelligence

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no personal, financial, professional, or institutional relationships with any individuals or organizations that may have influenced, or could reasonably be perceived to have influenced, the conduct, analysis, or conclusions of this study.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This research did not involve clinical trials or medical subjects. Where applicable, participation was voluntary and based on informed consent, and all data were treated confidentially and reported in anonymized form. The study complied with general ethical principles for academic research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding or financial support from any public, commercial, or non-profit organization. The work was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract:
High-commitment HRM systems have long been recognised as a primary organisational mechanism for
generating employee commitment, discretionary effort, and sustained competitive advantage. The theoretical
power of these systems rests not merely on the individual practices they comprise, but on their synergistic, bundled
delivery as relational signals — communicating to employees that the organisation values them as whole persons
rather than as cost centres to be optimised. The accelerating integration of artificial intelligence into core HRM
functions — encompassing AI-driven recruitment, algorithmic performance management, automated learning and
development, and data-mediated employee voice — introduces a structurally novel transformation that the
existing literature has not addressed: the systematic replacement of human-relational HRM delivery with
algorithmic mediation. This paper develops an original theoretical argument that AI-mediated delivery of highcommitment
HRM practices fundamentally disrupts the causal mechanism through which those practices generate
commitment. Drawing on HR Attribution Theory (Nishii, Lepak, and Schneider, 2008), the AMO framework
(Appelbaum et al., 2000), and the Resource-Based View (Barney, 1991), this paper introduces the concept of the
Relational Integrity Threshold — the point at which AI mediation shifts individual HRM practices from
commitment-generating signals into efficiency-signalling control mechanisms. The paper further proposes the AIMediation
Spectrum (AMS), a six-practice diagnostic framework that maps each high-commitment HRM practice
across three mediation states — human-delivered, AI-augmented, and AI-mediated — and identifies the
conditions under which bundle synergy is preserved, diminished, or destroyed. The paper generates eight
theoretically grounded propositions and a structured agenda for empirical validation. The central implication is
stark: organisations that deploy AI to maximise the operational efficiency of HRM practices without attending to
their relational integrity risk substituting compliance for commitment — achieving administrative modernisation
at the cost of the people-performance relationship that high-commitment HRM was designed to build.

title: Cycle-Consistent Dual-Model with Shared Features for Thermal Process
affiliations: Anhui Institute of Information Technology and Anhui Institute of Information Technology

detail.title: Cycle-Consistent Dual-Model with Shared Features for Thermal Process
detail.abstract: As the core link of cement production, the thermal process is inherently characterized by strong coupling, large time delay, non-linearity, and frequent working condition fluctuations. Its operating status directly determines clinker quality, firing energy consumption, and carbon emission levels, making it a key breakthrough for the intelligent and green transformation of the cement industry.To address the core pain points of traditional models—including single-model pure thermal mechanism models, pure time-series data-driven models, and simple fusion models, such as the difficulty in balancing prediction accuracy and industrial constraints, poor generalization ability, low industrial acceptance caused by black-box decision-making, and poor field implementability, this paper proposes a key technology for thermal process optimization based on a Cycle-Consistent Dual Model with Shared Features (CC-DualModel). The core of this technology is to construct a complete technical framework consisting of shared feature alignment, cycle-consistent mutual supervision, dual-model multi-objective collaborative inference, and hard constraints of industrial processes. The key technology proposed in this paper breaks through the bottlenecks of traditional thermal optimization technologies. It not only provides an efficient, reliable, and field-implementable technical solution for the intelligent optimization of thermal processes, but also offers a referable technical research paradigm for the intelligent optimization of high-temperature thermal processes in the building materials industry.

title: A Mixed-integer Linear Programming Model for Integrated Scheduling of Technicians, Surgeons, and Operating Rooms
affiliations: Kharazmi University, Kharazmi University, Sharif University of Technology and Kharazmi University

detail.title: A Mixed-integer Linear Programming Model for Integrated Scheduling of Technicians, Surgeons, and Operating Rooms
detail.abstract: Operating room staff scheduling, particularly for surgical technicians, remains one of the persistent challenges in operating room management. Field observations in an Iranian hospital indicate that technician scheduling is mainly performed on a monthly basis and is heavily constrained by surgeons’ fixed weekly timetables. This structure limits the flexibility required to properly coordinate surgeons and technicians across shifts. Moreover, assigning different types of surgeries to shifts requires access to operating rooms equipped with compatible facilities; under limited room availability or restricted room flexibility, the planning process becomes increasingly complex.To address these challenges, this study proposes a practical mixed‑integer linear programming (MILP) model that simultaneously considers monthly and weekly planning horizons for the integrated scheduling of operating room and anesthesia technicians, surgeons, and operating rooms. The proposed model incorporates a comprehensive set of real‑world constraints, including productivity rules, compatibility requirements, maximum allowable consecutive rest days, surgeon–technician compatibility, shift preferences, technician experience with different surgery types, and workload‑balancing considerations. Additionally, the impact of allowable overtime is examined under two scenarios: fixed overtime capacity and preference‑based overtime.The results of the model can support the generation of fair and feasible staff schedules, improve coordination among surgical resources, and ultimately enhance operating room service quality and hospital efficiency.

title: Group Evacuation Modeling for Fire Scenarios in Covered commercialstreets in Morocco
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, Mohammed VI Polytechnic University and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Group Evacuation Modeling for Fire Scenarios in Covered commercialstreets in Morocco
detail.abstract: The existence of social groups can significantly affect how well an evacuation goes in emergency situations, especially those brought on by fires in areas with a high population density. Movement patterns and overall evacuation time are significantly influenced by specific behavioral dynamics. This impact is more pronounced in the context oftiny pedestrian alleys, as those seen in covered areas in the historic cities of Morocco because of the high pedestrian density and spatial constraints.The safe exit of a commercial street in Rabat City is investigated in this study. The study considers the Available Safe Egress Time (tASET ) and the Required Safe Egress Time (tRSET). The analysis compares tASET and tRSET in order to examine the factors that influence evacuation effectiveness. According to the simulations, dangerous circumstances(temperature and smoke levels beyond safety limits) appeared in less than five minutes, well before full evacuation could be completed (tASET < tRSET). Crucially, the existence of social groups had a major impact on evacuation effectiveness; a large percentage of groups (up to 50%) shortened the overall evacuation time. These results provide important information for creating emergency plans and safety strategies for crowded, narrow commercial streets.

title: Strategic Drift: Why Deployed AI Systems Diverge from Intended Economic Outcomes Over Time

detail.title: Strategic Drift: Why Deployed AI Systems Diverge from Intended Economic Outcomes Over Time

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no competing financial interests or personal relationships that could have appeared to influence the work reported in this paper.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This article is a conceptual research paper and does not involve human participants, patient data, or animal subjects. Ethics approval was therefore not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence systems improve through feedback, optimization, and repeated interaction with real-world environments. But improvement alone does not guarantee strategic success. Deployed systems may become increasingly effective at optimizing behaviors, incentives, or proxy metrics that diverge from the long-term economic outcomes organizations actually intend to create. This paper introduces the concept of Strategic Drift-the progressive divergence between the behaviors optimized by a deployed AI system and the long-term economic outcomes the organization intends to achieve. Unlike conventional system failure, Strategic Drift often emerges gradually through the interaction of optimization objectives, proxy metrics, reinforcement structures, and adaptive feedback loops. Systems may therefore appear operationally successful while becoming strategically misaligned. The paper argues that Strategic Drift represents a distinct category of strategic risk emerging from adaptive AI systems. The problem is not fundamentally one of technical malfunction, but of governance: deployed systems learn what surrounding structures reward, reinforce, and measure. As AI systems become increasingly embedded within organizational decision-making, governing learning direction may become as important as governing model performance itself.

title: Micro-Dynamics of Regulatory Self-Efficacy and Neurotic Affect How Daily Work Experiences Shape Trait Neuroticism
affiliations: Sapienza University of Rome and Sapienza University of Rome

detail.title: Micro-Dynamics of Regulatory Self-Efficacy and Neurotic Affect How Daily Work Experiences Shape Trait Neuroticism
detail.abstract: Understanding how daily experiences shape enduring personality traits remains a central challenge in personality psychology. Drawing on the TESSERA framework and social cognitive theory, this study examined how daily work stressors influence state neuroticism via regulatory emotional self-efficacy (RESE). A sample of 221 employed adults completed daily surveys over 31 workdays. Using multilevel dynamic structural equation modeling, we captured within-person autoregressive and cross-lagged processes while accounting for between-person variability. Results showed that the subjective intensity, but not occurrence, of work events predicted decreases in next-day RESE and increases in neuroticism. In turn, RESE predicted lower subsequent neuroticism and slightly reduced future event intensity, whereas neuroticism undermined RESE and amplified perceived stress, highlighting cumulative micro-level pathways to trait neuroticism.

title: Incident clearance time; uncertainty quantification; bi-level forecasting; calibrated routing; spatial risk; Tennessee highways
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Tennessee, Knoxville

detail.title: Incident clearance time; uncertainty quantification; bi-level forecasting; calibrated routing; spatial risk; Tennessee highways
detail.abstract: Incident clearance prediction is useful only when it is both accurate and decision ready. Existing bi-level incident-duration models typically rely on hard routing between short and long regimes, producing point forecasts that are brittle near the classification boundary and provide little information about model confidence. This paper develops an uncertainty-aware bi-level forecasting framework using 723,614 Tennessee Statewide Computer-Aided Dispatch System (SWCS) highway incidents from 2020–2025, scaling the bi-level architecture to a six-year statewide corpus.On a stratified 20% hold-out, the Stage 1 classifier achieves weighted F1 = 0.733, outper- forming logistic regression (F1 = 0.618), confirming that nonlinear interactions are important for prediction performance. The regime-specific regressors show distinct performance: Stage 2a reaches R2log = 0.201 with MAE 8.42 min for short incidents, while Stage 2b reaches R2log = 0.455 and MAE 148.52 min for long incidents. The review-band policy achieves empirical 90% interval coverage of 0.911, flags 16.9% of incidents as uncertain, lowers false escalation to 0.67%, and reduces overall MAE from 97.74 to 97.12 min compared with hard routing. A spatial ablation isolates the Density-Based Spatial Clustering of Applications with Noise (DBSCAN) feature contribution: a +0.022 improvement in R2log for the long regime with negligible short-regime effect, confirming that spatial context is regime-specific and that this result is robust across dataset scales. On the six-year corpus, DBSCAN achieves 98.2% incident coverage compared to 49.1% in the single-year study, confirming that denser parameterization is necessary for state-scale corpora.

title: Routing, Scheduling, and Synchronization of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) with Bus Hitchhiking for Last-mile Parcel Delivery
affiliations: The University of Hong Kong, The University of Hong Kong - University of Hong Kong, The University of Hong Kong - Department of Industrial and Manufacturing Systems Engineering and Tsinghua University

detail.title: Routing, Scheduling, and Synchronization of Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) with Bus Hitchhiking for Last-mile Parcel Delivery
detail.abstract: Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) present a transformative solution for last-mile delivery, offering rapid delivery speed that bypasses ground traffic congestion. However, their adoption is constrained by limited flight range and battery capacity. To address these limitations, this paper proposes an innovative ”bus-hitchhiking UAV delivery system”, where UAVs hitchhike on bus rooftops during deliveries while buses serve as mobile charging stations for UAVs. This paradigm has the potential to reduce flight distance and extend the operational duration of UAVs. To optimize UAV delivery routes, schedules, and coordination with buses, we formulate a Mixed Integer Linear Programming (MILP) model. Given the complexity of the model, we develop an Adaptive Large Neighborhood Search (ALNS) algorithm with tailored modifications to solve the problem. Numerical experiments show that the proposed ALNS not only scales efficiently where Gurobi fails, but also robustly outperforms classical metaheuristics, yielding up to a 21.2% cost improvement over the Genetic Algorithm and Simulated Annealing benchmarks. A case study in Shenzhen demonstrates the framework's economic viability, where the bus-hitchhiking UAV system reduces costs by 29.53% and 18.18% compared to standalone UAV and fixed charging station scenarios, respectively. Comparative analysis reveals its practical superiority over traditional Truck-UAV paradigms by extending delivery ranges without the severe capital and routing costs of dedicated ground vehicles. Furthermore, enabling multi-parcel deliveries achieves up to an average 77.42% cost reduction versus single-parcel operations. These findings demonstrate that strategically integrating existing public transit with emerging UAV technologies unlocks unprecedented efficiency, offering a scalable pathway for sustainable urban logistics.

title: A supervisory modeling framework for structural integration in distributed vehicle-edge-cloud intelligent transportation systems
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A supervisory modeling framework for structural integration in distributed vehicle-edge-cloud intelligent transportation systems
detail.abstract: Distributed Intelligent Transportation Systems (ITS) deployed in Vehicle–Edge–Cloud environments require coordinated decision-making across heterogeneous layers under real-time constraints. Existing ITS architectures remain component-centric: learning, orchestration, control, and constraint mechanisms are typically designed independently, limiting architectural coherence and cross-layer coordination. This paper proposes a supervisory modeling framework, where the system state integrates execution conditions, learning dynamics, and constraint margins. The framework introduces an admissible region , an admissible action set, and a multi-timescale transition operator family. A structured evaluation of 47 ITS architectures using a six-dimensional framework covering cross-layer intelligence allocation, learning integration, orchestration, closed-loop control, temporal structuring, and constraint formalisation reveals that no existing architecture simultaneously addresses more than four dimensions. In contrast, the proposed framework integrates all six dimensions within a unified supervisory formulation and provides a consistent mapping to a Vehicle–Edge–Cloud deployment architecture. This establishes an architecture-driven design approach in which decision-making, learning behaviour, and feasibility constraints are jointly defined, while supporting future prototype implementation, comparative benchmarking, and stability-oriented evaluation under realistic deployment conditions.

title: Purposeful Structural Model Design
affiliations: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign

detail.title: Purposeful Structural Model Design
detail.abstract: Structural models enable marketing researchers to evaluate counterfactual decisions such as pricing, market entry, and platform design, yet their credibility depends critically on choices made prior to estimation. In strategic settings, the mapping from primitives to outcomes can be locally flat, so distinct mechanisms generate similar behavior, while equilibrium responses attenuate policy effects and limit their detectability. This paper develops a framework linking identification geometry to counterfactual feasibility, showing that model complexity redistributes identifying information across competing mechanisms and that statistical insignificance can reflect equilibrium constraints rather than lack of data. The results imply that credible structural analysis requires aligning model design with the decision margin and the informational content of the data, rather than relying solely on estimation advances.

title: How do we learn to be multimodal? An urban multimodal mobility route planner coupling Agent-based models and Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning techniques
affiliations: and Universidad Complutense de Madrid

detail.title: How do we learn to be multimodal? An urban multimodal mobility route planner coupling Agent-based models and Multi-agent Reinforcement Learning techniques
detail.abstract: The current climate emergency facing the planet requires both cities and citizens to adopt more sustainable and less polluting mobility measures and travel behaviours. Urban multimodality offers flexible and efficient mobility while minimising environmental impacts, particularly when delivered through digital platforms within the framework of Mobility as a Service (MaaS). However, the lack of fully integrated products and robust public policies compels travellers to learn how to combine transport modes through experience, observation, and imitation. This study proposes a model for planning multimodal routes based on the individual and collective learning of users, who are characterised according to factors such as their propensity to adopt new mobility options and their proficiency in using mobile applications. The model combines an agent-based approach with Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning (MARL) techniques to feed an A*-based route planner, in which the multimodal transport system is represented as a graph. The multimodal network of central Madrid is used as a case study to test the model. The results reveal a clear predominance of the metro as the backbone of urban mobility, appearing in 75% of all journeys. Nevertheless, a tendency to use new app-based mobility modes at least once a week is observed even among users with a low predisposition to adopt them. The model evaluation metrics reinforce the notion of increasing multimodality in urban environments that learn and adapt over time.

title: Comparing Station-Location Approaches for Urban Air Mobility: A Case Study of the Metropolitan Area Ruhr
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Comparing Station-Location Approaches for Urban Air Mobility: A Case Study of the Metropolitan Area Ruhr
detail.abstract: Urban Air Mobility (UAM) is increasingly discussed as a potential complement to existing transport networks in metropolitan regions. However, the performance and practical relevance of UAM station networks depend strongly on the underlying station-location logic. While comparative studies are emerging, cross-logic comparisons of different station-location approaches under consistent spatial data, network sizes, and evaluation criteria remain limited. This paper addresses this gap by comparing three complementary station-location logics in the polycentric Metropolitan Area Ruhr in Germany: a proximity-oriented k-means++ clustering approach, a demand-weighted location-allocation approach based on the p-median problem, and a transport-oriented location assessment (TOLA) used as a practical reference configuration. The resulting networks are evaluated with respect to access distance, catchment coverage, spatial distribution, flight-path characteristics, and representative test routes. The results show that the semi-automated approaches substantially improve accessibility and coverage compared with the practical reference configuration. The k-means++ approach performs particularly well in terms of geometric proximity, while the location-allocation approach provides competitive demand-weighted accessibility for medium and large network sizes. TOLA performs weaker in distance-based metrics but remains useful for interpreting the planning plausibility of optimized solutions. The study demonstrates that early-stage UAM station planning benefits from comparing multiple station-location logics rather than relying on a single method. It thereby contributes to a more transparent and transferable basis for comparing methodological assumptions in early-stage UAM infrastructure planning.

title: Will Business Schools Survive in the Era of Generative AI?

detail.title: Will Business Schools Survive in the Era of Generative AI?
detail.abstract: The rapid diffusion of generative AI is reshaping the value proposition of business education by compressing the labor-market returns that justify high tuition fees. We develop an equilibrium model in which schools set tuition, students weigh expected career returns against fees, and firms hire graduates according to institutional quality. The model generates a survival threshold below which schools can no longer break even, and shows that AI-driven cost savings within institutions cannot fully offset the demand-side erosion of graduate income. Calibrated to the French grandes écoles market and extended to a dynamic stochastic setting, the stylized model predicts that roughly 10% of schools (out of 30) face the risk of a market exit in the 2-3 decades to come under a scenario of limited replacement. If diffusion and substitution accelerate, these exits may instead occur in the next five years.

title: The AI Labor Equation: A Governance Framework for Ethical Workforce Transformation

detail.title: The AI Labor Equation: A Governance Framework for Ethical Workforce Transformation

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is Principal of WTL Governance (White, Turing & Lovelace LLC), a US-registered AI governance advisory firm with Tokyo operations that provides advisory and analytical services to organizations on the subject matter discussed in this paper. The author has no financial relationship with any of the firms, vendors, platforms, or research institutions cited in this paper, and no organization cited herein has reviewed or had editorial input over the manuscript. No external party commissioned, funded, or directed the research.
declarations.funderStatement: This research was conducted as an internal thought leadership initiative of White, Turing & Lovelace LLC and received no external funding, grant support, or sponsorship from any government agency, foundation, corporation, or other institution.

detail.abstract:
Artificial Intelligence has not broken the labor market, but it is reshaping who benefits from it. As of May 2026, the aggregate labor market shows no economy-wide disruption; unemployment metrics remain within historical ranges. Beneath that stable surface, however, a distributional squeeze is compounding along predictable lines. Entry-level job postings have fallen sharply over the past eighteen months, and in the most AI-exposed occupations, employment for early-career workers aged 22 to 25 has declined approximately 13% relative to less-exposed peers. The pattern repeats across the United States, France, the United Kingdom, South Korea, and other jurisdictions: the economy is healthy, the sector is healthy, but the youngest workers are absorbing the cost.

This paper argues that the AI workforce transition is governable, but only if governance and trust are built before the distributional costs documented here become structural.
