detail.abstract: This paper proposes a fuzzy metric-based framework for the construction of composite indicators that avoids normalization and exogenous weighting schemes. Instead of transforming the data, the methodology evaluates observations through their proximity to a reference profile within a fuzzy metric space, preserving the intrinsic geometry of the original variables. The approach introduces an endogenous sensitivity mechanism that adjusts the contribution of each dimension according to its effective discriminatory power, providing a structure-consistent alternative to traditional weighting methods. From a theoretical perspective, the framework is formulated in terms of factorizable fuzzy metrics and aggregation functions that preserve the underlying metric structure. In particular, a multiplicative aggregation scheme is shown to yield a coherent representation consistent with distance-based composite indicators, establishing a formal link with the Pena Trapero distance through an exponential transformation. An empirical application to health system performance illustrates the proposed methodology. The results indicate that the fuzzy metric approach produces stable rankings under sample perturbations and reduces the impact of redundant information. Sensitivity analysis further shows that the resulting rankings are less affected by variations in weights, supporting the robustness and structural coherence of the proposed framework.

title: Why Small Economies Converge to Fiscal Dumping: Scale Asymmetry, Institutional Feedback, and Regime Persistence
affiliations: University College Dublin (UCD)

detail.title: Why Small Economies Converge to Fiscal Dumping: Scale Asymmetry, Institutional Feedback, and Regime Persistence
detail.abstract: A small number of jurisdictions persistently attract a disproportionate share of global multinational profits through fiscal dumping-the systematic undercutting of international tax benchmarks. Existing models of tax competition characterize the strategic interactions sustaining such regimes, but say little about the structural conditions that make them feasible. This paper develops a minimal structural framework in which fiscal dumping emerges endogenously from two forces: the exposure of a jurisdiction to mobile profits relative to its domestic scale, and the institutional feedback generated by established multinational activity. A sharp activation threshold separates jurisdictions for which fiscal deviation is structurally sustainable from those for which it is not. Beyond this threshold, institutional feedback may generate multiple equilibria and path dependence. An illustrative mapping of jurisdictions into the (Θ, α) spacewithout relying on statutory tax rates-shows that economies associated with fiscal dumping tend to cluster in regions where the framework predicts persistent deviation to be sustainable. The results suggest that fiscal dumping reflects structural asymmetries in scale, mobility, and institutional capacity, with direct implications for the design of coordination mechanisms.

title: Financial Conditions and Growth-at-Risk in Jordan: A PCA-based Composite Index Approach
affiliations: Arab Monetary Fund

detail.title: Financial Conditions and Growth-at-Risk in Jordan: A PCA-based Composite Index Approach
detail.abstract:
This study constructs a comprehensive Financial Conditions Index (FCI) for Jordan using Principal Component Analysis (PCA) and examines its implications for downside risks to future economic growth within a nonlinear Growth-at-Risk (GaR) framework over the quarterly period 2005Q1-2024Q4. The analysis integrates macro-financial factor extraction, quantile regression techniques, and regimedependent estimation to assess how financial conditions influence both the average and lower tail of the future GDP growth distribution in a small open emerging economy. 

The PCA-based FCI is constructed using a broad set of domestic and external financial indicators, including interest rates, credit growth, money supply, stock market returns, sovereign spreads, foreign reserves, inflation, and exchange-rate volatility. The estimated index appears to co-move with major episodes of macro-financial stress in Jordan, including the Global Financial Crisis, regional geopolitical instability, the COVID-19 pandemic, and the recent global monetary tightening cycle. 

The GaR estimation results reveal that tighter financial conditions significantly increase downside risks to future economic growth, particularly at the lower quantiles of the GDP growth distribution. Quantile regression estimates show that a one-standard-deviation tightening in financial conditions reduces the 5 th percentile of future GDP growth by approximately 1.4 percentage points, while the impact on median growth outcomes remains comparatively moderate. The nonlinear threshold analysis further demonstrates that the adverse effects of financial tightening intensify substantially once financial stress exceeds a critical threshold level, confirming the presence of asymmetric macro-financial amplification mechanisms. 

The results highlight the potential relevance of financial conditions as a forward-looking indicator of macroeconomic risk and support their use in macroprudential monitoring frameworks in emerging economies. More broadly, the study contributes to the growing literature on financial conditions and tailrisk dynamics in emerging economies by providing new empirical evidence on nonlinear macro-financial transmission mechanisms in a small open economy.

title: Systemic Attrition: The Human, Economic, Legal, and Structural Costs of the 2026 Iran Conflict
affiliations: Independent Policy Analyst

detail.title: Systemic Attrition: The Human, Economic, Legal, and Structural Costs of the 2026 Iran Conflict

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflict of interest. This research was conducted independently with no financial or personal relationships that could influence the findings.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The author declares no conflict of interest. This research was conducted independently with no financial or personal relationships that could influence the findings.

detail.abstract:
The 2026 Iran conflict generated systemic consequences extending far beyond the direct battlefield, affecting interconnected civilian, logistical, financial, maritime, industrial, and energy systems across multiple regions. Originating in the June 2025 precursor escalation and intensifying with the launch of Operation Epic Fury on 28 February 2026, the conflict evolved into a prolonged geopolitical and macroeconomic disruption marked by infrastructure degradation, maritime instability in the Strait of Hormuz, humanitarian displacement, inflationary pressure, and growing fragmentation within alliance and financial structures.

This paper presents a forensic institutional assessment of the conflict through the lens of international law, infrastructure warfare, casualty forensics, macroeconomic shock transmission, industrial attrition, and monetary fragmentation. It introduces the concepts of “Collateral Friction,” describing cascading civilian harm caused by interconnected infrastructure failure, and the “Industrial Attrition Paradox,” referring to the inability of liberalised peacetime defence-industrial systems to replenish advanced munitions at wartime consumption rates.

The paper argues that the defining characteristic of the conflict was not decisive military transformation, but systemic degradation across energy markets, food systems, shipping corridors, and civilian infrastructure, with disproportionate economic burdens falling on neutral Global South economies. It concludes that the conflict demonstrated the declining ability of kinetic military superiority alone to produce durable strategic outcomes within a deeply interconnected global economy.

title: AI-driven Transaction Monitoring and Sanctions Screening in Cross-border Remittances for Terrorist Financing Mitigation
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: AI-driven Transaction Monitoring and Sanctions Screening in Cross-border Remittances for Terrorist Financing Mitigation
detail.abstract: Cross-border money transfers are a lifeline for millions of families. But they also offer a quiet path for terrorist financing-that's the dark side. The usual way of watching transactions-looking for amounts above a certain dollar value and manually checking names against sanctions lists-just doesn't catch small, carefully split payments. Plus manual name screening creates so many false alarms that compliance teams drown in noise. I reckon artificial intelligence can fix both problems. This paper proposes a two-part AI system: one part learns normal sending behaviour and spots strange patterns (using autoencoders and graph neural networks), the other matches names against watchlists using fuzzy logic and machine learning to cut false positives by 70-80%. To ground the idea in reality, we examine eight real court cases from Australia, the UK, the US, the Netherlands and Sweden-all convictions where people used Western Union or hawala networks to fund terror groups. In each case, I show how AI could have detected the scheme within hours or days instead of months, and with far fewer false alerts. The framework follows FATF's latest rules (2025) and is practical enough for money transfer operators to start using today.

title: Optimal recycling of carbon revenues along the net-zero pathway
affiliations: University of Warsaw

detail.title: Optimal recycling of carbon revenues along the net-zero pathway
detail.abstract: Carbon-pricing revenues are temporary; they are substantial during partial decarbonisation and vanish as emissions approach net zero. Recycling these revenues therefore raises two intertemporal questions for governments: whether to return revenues immediately to households or save them for the net-zero phase, and whether financing temporary abatement subsidies from these revenues may distort households' saving and investment decisions. We build an analytical general-equilibrium model to compare three recycling options: immediate lump-sum transfers, public saving to finance future transfers, and abatement subsidies. In a benchmark setup with perfect-foresight households, a single final good, and a closed economy, Ricardian equivalence holds: all three options deliver identical welfare. We show how relaxing benchmark assumptions breaks equivalence. With myopic households, public saving is preferable to immediate transfers when abatement is capital-intensive, policy costs rise over time, or learning-by-doing externalities are present; otherwise, immediate transfers dominate. Financing subsidies lowers welfare: it alters the price of investment relative to consumption, thereby distorting saving decisions. In open economies, it also redistributes resources to foreign capital owners. Simulations of a large-scale computable general equilibrium model calibrated to the Polish economy indicate that public saving outperforms both alternatives.

title: When Does Flexibility Create Value in Electricity Markets? An AI-Based Market-State Approach
affiliations: Illinois Institute of Technology and Old Dominion University

detail.title: When Does Flexibility Create Value in Electricity Markets? An AI-Based Market-State Approach
detail.abstract: Electricity-market volatility does not by itself explain when flexibility becomes economically valuable. A central problem in the current literature is that price forecasting, tail-risk measurement, and flexibility valuation are often studied separately, leaving limited evidence on how observed market conditions map into realized flexibility value. This paper addresses that gap by developing an AI-based State-Price Flexibility Index (SPFI) that learns a flexibility-relevant latent market state from hub-level price and trading information. The framework combines a multidimensional state representation, conditional distribution forecasting, scenario construction, and economic valuation. The novelty is threefold. Theoretically, the paper models flexibility value as state-dependent and multidimensional rather than as a direct function of volatility alone. Empirically, it uses a 2014–2025 hub-date panel with 17,219 observations to estimate and validate the index. Economically, it evaluates the learned state by realized flexibility value, downside-risk reduction, and marginal capacity value. The results show that the SPFI identifies economically informative flexibility conditions.

title: Basel III-IV: Ten Structural Failures That Cannot Be Fixed From Within. SVWORLD STANDARD 73.5 v1.8 as a Complete Architectural Replacement

detail.title: Basel III-IV: Ten Structural Failures That Cannot Be Fixed From Within. SVWORLD STANDARD 73.5 v1.8 as a Complete Architectural Replacement
detail.abstract: This article is a direct continuation of the first comparative analysis of Basel III-IV and SVWORLD STANDARD 73.5 v1.7. While the first article established the philosophical and methodological superiority of the real-backing paradigm over the nominal-value paradigm, this second part performs a systematic forensic audit of ten to twelve specific structural vulnerabilities embedded directly in the official BCBS regulatory texts, including supervisory guidance issued between 2021 and 2026. Each vulnerability is identified by the exact document number, section, and paragraph of the Basel Committee. For each failure point, the corresponding mechanism in SVWORLD STANDARD 73.5 v1.8 is shown to provide a mathematically complete solution. The conclusion is unambiguous: the failures are not accidental gaps that can be patched. They are load-bearing elements of the fiat architecture. Replacing individual rules while preserving the axiom that nominal debt equals real value is impossible. Only a full architectural replacement resolves the problem.

title: The Fiscal Architecture of American Decline: Debt, Deficits, and Structural Impossibility

detail.title: The Fiscal Architecture of American Decline: Debt, Deficits, and Structural Impossibility

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author is not affiliated with any organization.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The author used publicly available information. There were no participants.
declarations.funderStatement: The author funded the research.

detail.abstract: The United States fiscal trajectory is not a policy failure or a partisan choice. It is the structural consequence of an infrastructure transition in which FIRE-dominant economic architecture systematically shifted tax incidence from capital to labor-corporations fell from 31 percent to 9 percent of federal revenue between 1946 and 2023; payroll taxes rose from 8 percent to 36 percent over the same period-while the winning coalition's private-goods benefits expanded and public investment contracted. The result is a fiscal architecture that simultaneously finances the winning coalition's asset positions (federal debt at $28.2 trillion generates $950 billion in annual interest payments, 56 percent of which flows to the Elite and Chamber GOP coalitions) and structurally forecloses the public investment that would address the binding constraints documented in Papers P5 and P6. Federal government productive activities declined from 54 percent of noninterest spending in 1970 to 24 percent in 2023. CBO projects net interest will consume 23 percent of the federal budget by 2054, crowding out every discretionary program. The OASI trust fund depletes around 2033-2034 on current trajectory, at which point Social Security benefits face an automatic 21-23 percent cut-falling most heavily on the MAGA coalition that is the program's largest electoral constituency. The paper introduces binding constraints analysis (Hausmann, Rodrik, and Velasco 2005) at the country level: the U.S. fiscal binding constraint is not excessive spending but a revenue architecture designed to minimize the winning coalition's tax contribution to the public goods it requires. Two registered predictions are examined: P4 (r > g threshold breach by 2031, at which point asset returns systematically exceed GDP growth, accelerating wealth concentration beyond current levels) and P5 (OASI depletion ~2033-2034, with politically definitive benefit cut implications). The closing circle is traced at full resolution: the fiscal architecture suppresses the public investment that would relax the binding constraints that suppress the fertility and labor force growth that would service the debt that the architecture created.

title: Model Predictive Control-Based Optimal Energy Allocation for Generalized Energy Storage Systems Considering Dynamic Variations of SOC and SOH
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Model Predictive Control-Based Optimal Energy Allocation for Generalized Energy Storage Systems Considering Dynamic Variations of SOC and SOH
detail.abstract: To address the issues of high system volatility and insufficient regulation capability under high penetration of wind and photovoltaic (PV) powers, a generalized energy storage system (GESS) is constructed, including wind power, PV, hydrogen energy storage, battery energy storage, and flexible loads. First, a GESS state-space model is established based on model predictive control (MPC) theory. An optimization objective is formulated by comprehensively considering the power constraints of each unit and the state constraints of the energy storage devices, thereby maintaining system power balance and realizing the optimal operation of the GESS. Second, to prevent violations of the state of charge (SOC) and state of hydrogen (SOH) limits, as well as to mitigate the safety and lifetime problems caused by the low-power operation of the electrolyzer and fuel cell, a multi-unit power coordination strategy based on the dynamic variations in SOC and SOH is proposed to optimize energy allocation within the system. Finally, experiments are carried out on the RT-LAB platform. Under operating conditions where storage the SOC limits are exceeded, the fixed-weight strategy and the variable-weight strategy are compared, and the results demonstrate the superior dynamic regulation performance of the proposed method.

title: XTIFN: Grating-based X-Ray Tri-contrast CT Image Fusion via Unsupervised Feature Learning
affiliations: Beihang University (BUAA), Beihang University (BUAA), Beihang University (BUAA), Beihang University (BUAA), Beihang University (BUAA), Beihang University (BUAA), Beihang University (BUAA), Beijing Institute of Aeronautical Materials, Aerospace Research Institute of Materials & Processing Technology, Beihang University (BUAA), Beihang University (BUAA) and Beihang University (BUAA)

detail.title: XTIFN: Grating-based X-Ray Tri-contrast CT Image Fusion via Unsupervised Feature Learning
detail.abstract: Grating-based X-ray tri-contrast imaging can acquire absorption, phase-contrast, and dark-field images in a single scan. However, biomedical analysis often still requires repeated switching among separate contrast volumes. A key challenge is to generate one fused CT image that preserves complementary information from different channels, which may have different intensity ranges, spatial details, and noise patterns. In this study, we propose XTIFN, a one-step unsupervised framework for tri-contrast CT image fusion. XTIFN uses a dual-path generator and a tri-discriminator constraint to integrate structural, edge, and texture information from the three input contrasts. In addition, we introduce an independent entropy-weighted multi-source evaluation strategy to assess the contribution of different source contrasts in the fused image. Experiments on synchrotron-radiation and laboratory tube-source datasets achieved entropy-weighted SSIM values of 0.6731 and 0.6542, respectively. The results were further supported by 3D visualization and a human-tissue case study. This work may provide an additional reference view for the joint inspection and visualization of tri-contrast CT data, rather than replacing the original contrast channels, and may help support the broader application of X-ray multi-contrast imaging.

title: Customer-Facing Offer Design for Mixed Drone-Courier Delivery: Pricing, Promised Times, and Customer Choice
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Customer-Facing Offer Design for Mixed Drone-Courier Delivery: Pricing, Promised Times, and Customer Choice
detail.abstract: This paper studies how an on-demand delivery platform should design customer-facing offers in mixed drone-courier operations. For each new order, the platform decides which service products to display and what prices and promised delivery times to set for rider-only, drone-assisted, and flexible products. Customers then self-select, and the resulting demand mix feeds back into future service conditions. We develop a sequential framework that links offer-design decisions, multinomial-logit customer choice, and fulfillment outcomes through a tractable mode-level surrogate for cost, realized service time, and lateness penalties. Computational experiments compare a transparent dynamic-menu heuristic that jointly adjusts visibility, price, and promised time, a stronger one-step optimized comparator used asa diagnostic benchmark, a price+time variant without visibility control, and dispatch-only and static-menu reference regimes. Across the reported synthetic scenario families, pricing and promised-time adaptation prove to be the primary levers for balancing profit and reliability. By contrast, the additional value brought by visibility control is conditional within the tested heuristic family and can be neutral or slightly negative in some scenarios. The benchmark comparison also reveals substantial performance headroom, showing that the framework is most useful for identifying which customer-facing levers matter and for clarifying how benchmark strength affects the interpretation of lightweight deployable rules. Overall, the paper provides directional evidence on transport service management under stylized conditions rather than direct deployment prescriptions.

title: Rethinking Ecological Economics
affiliations: Norwegian University of Life Sciences

detail.title: Rethinking Ecological Economics
detail.abstract: Despite important successes, ecological economics remains a highly heterogeneous field, characterized by divergent views on what constitutes economics, its philosophical foundations, and the understanding of markets and human action. This internal diversity weakens its ability to function as a clear alternative to neoclassical economics and to fulfill its central purpose of providing a scholarly basis for the transformation toward a sustainable economy. This paper develops a coherent vision of ecological economics by articulating an explicit ethical framework and a distinct definition of what economics is. It argues that critical realism provides the most appropriate philosophical foundation and advances a conception of the economy as embedded in biophysical systems as well as social and political institutions. Rejecting neoclassical models of rationality and behavior, it is argued that ecological economics should develop on the basis of an institutional understanding of human action. It concludes by demonstrating how this rethought ecological economics enables stronger analytical contributions and more productive engagement with dialogues about how a sustainable future might be realized.

title: Deblurred Neural Radiance Field with Dynamic Kernel Estimation
affiliations: Xiangtan University, Xiangtan University and Xiangtan University

detail.title: Deblurred Neural Radiance Field with Dynamic Kernel Estimation
detail.abstract: We present a dynamic kernel-based deblurring method for Neural Radiance Fields (NeRF), aimed at overcoming the limitations of previous methods that use fixed blur kernels. While prior works successfully address blur caused by camera motion or defocus, they can be inaccurate when blur intensity varies across different scenes and regions. To resolve this issue, the proposed method employs a Mask Convolutional Neural Network to dynamically adjust the blur kernel size for each pixel, allowing for more accurate handling of varying blur speeds and areas. By modifying the kernel size and utilizing weighted aggregation, this approach achieves superior results in reconstructing sharp, detailed 3D scenes from blurred images. The experimental results verified the effectiveness of this method in novel view synthesis for per-scene under varying blur conditions. Code is available at https://github.com/XTU-PR-LAB/DK-NeRF.

title: Bi-projection Fusion for 360 Depth Estimation Based on Coordinate Attention
affiliations: Zhengzhou Normal University, Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou University, Zhengzhou University and Zhengzhou University

detail.title: Bi-projection Fusion for 360 Depth Estimation Based on Coordinate Attention
detail.abstract: Monocular depth estimation for 360◦ omnidirectional imagery is a fundamental task for 3D scene reconstruction, yet it is significantly hindered by the non-uniform geometric distortions inherent in Equirectangular Projection (ERP). In this study, we address the latitude-dependent sampling bias of ERP, where the effective receptive field of standard convolutions varies inversely with the cosine of the latitude (𝜃). We propose a novel bi projection fusion framework that synergistically integrates the global contextual continuity of ERP with the distortion-free local structures of Cube Map Projection (CMP). Central to our approach is the Multi-scale Coordinate-Transformer Fusion (MCTF) module, which reinterprets Coordinate Attention (CA) as a deterministic calibration tool. By explicitly encoding vertical coordinates into the feature fusion process, the MCTF module recalibrates spatial weights to compensate for spherical distortions. Furthermore, a Transformer based module is incorporated to maintain long range semantic consistency across the 360◦ field of view. Experimental results on 3D60, Matterport3D, and Stanford2D3D datasets demonstrate that our method significantly outperforms state-of-the-art models. Notably, our approach achieves a 21.2% reduction in RMSE and exhibits superior robustness in polar regions, where it reduces RMSE by 30% compared to the ERP baseline. Our findings validate that coordinate-aware feature recalibration is essential for robust omnidirectional vision.

title: Beyond the Farm: Economy-Wide Effects of Irrigation Development in Sub-Saharan Africa
affiliations: Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, Humboldt University of Berlin, Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Kenya Agricultural Research Institute (KARI), Kenya Agricultural and Livestock Research Organization (KALRO)

detail.title: Beyond the Farm: Economy-Wide Effects of Irrigation Development in Sub-Saharan Africa
detail.abstract: This study investigates the economy-wide welfare implications of expanding irrigation schemes in Africa, taking Benin and Kenya as case studies. We apply a comparative static computable general equilibrium model and, through the setup of scenarios, we distinguish the effects of the short-term construction phase and long-run irrigation expansion. While outcomes for the two cases differ in the details, we find for both countries that the construction phase results in negative welfare effects for most households if the schemes are financed through increasing income tax rates. Yet, these losses can be overcompensated in the operation phase of the irrigation schemes, due to the expansion of export-oriented agriculture and related multiplier effects. In both countries, we find that gross domestic product (GDP) increases by approximately 0.1% for every 50,000 hectares of irrigation expansion. In absolute terms, this translates to an annual GDP growth of 381 USD and 1,835 USD per additional hectare irrigated for Benin and Kenya, respectively. To achieve a pro-poor distribution of welfare, fair access for poor households to the newly irrigated land is crucial.

title: NS-S2FM: An Auditable Neuro-Symbolic Expert Decision System for Scenario-Aware Franchise Operations under Uncertainty​
affiliations: Capital University of Economics and Business, Capital University of Economics and Business and Capital Normal University

detail.title: NS-S2FM: An Auditable Neuro-Symbolic Expert Decision System for Scenario-Aware Franchise Operations under Uncertainty​
detail.abstract: Sports franchise operation provides a high-uncertainty testbed for expert decision systems because competitive performance, market demand, injury exposure, star-player dependency, financial pressure, and league-level events are tightly coupled. This study proposes NS-S2FM, an auditable neuro-symbolic, scenario-aware expert decision system for uncertain franchise operations. The framework turns heterogeneous signals and institutional rules into a decision object that reports an action, a diagnosed scenario, constraint and risk evidence, and an explanation. We evaluate NS-S2FM through controlled simulation, rule-defined franchise profiles, a WNBA 2022--2024 sports-performance and attendance panel with semi-real business variables, ablation analysis, sensitivity analysis, risk-sensitive and constrained comparators, explanation-augmented baselines, and statistical evidence checks. The evidence supports three decision-support advantages: strong multi-objective DSS behavior in controlled settings, first-ranked stakeholder utility under conservative, growth-oriented, and risk-averse operator preferences, and stronger traceability and scenario adaptability in the real-world panel evaluation. Results from the real-world panel also show the intended trade-off: unconstrained and profit-focused baselines remain competitive on short-horizon numerical scores. Evaluation-index sensitivity and constraint-binding analyses make this interpretation scope explicit by showing metric sensitivity and limited feasibility-mask binding. The contribution is an auditable, constraint-aware, and preference-sensitive DSS mechanism under transparent proxy-based evidence; stronger claims about audited business outcomes or organizational intervention effects require future data.​

title: Ballot Box Biology Narratives Reduce Support for Carnivore Protection Initiatives
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, University of California, Berkeley - Division of Epidemiology and Biostatistics, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Ballot Box Biology Narratives Reduce Support for Carnivore Protection Initiatives
detail.abstract: The public’s values related to wildlife are shifting in much of the United States, resulting in a growing number of citizen-led ballot initiatives focused on greater protection of wildlife, especially carnivores, particularly when agencies and commissions are not seen as adequately setting protective policies. To fight these ballot initiatives, traditional constituents motivated to maintain the status quo have used “ballot box biology” messaging, arguing that wildlife decisions should be made by biologists, not the public, and that the public should trust state wildlife agencies to make "responsible, science-based" management decisions. Those in support of ballot initiatives argue that these initiatives are important because both science and values play a role in wildlife management, diverse voices have been excluded in wildlife governance, and current decision-making structures (i.e., commissions) prioritize consumptive users over public values and science-based policy. We conducted a messaging experiment with over 2000 United States residents to examine how these messages impact public support and civic action for carnivore protection ballot initiatives as well as beliefs about wildlife governance. We found that the “ballot box biology” message significantly reduced support for carnivore protection ballot initiatives and reduced beliefs around the importance of citizen engagement. Messages in support of ballot initiatives did not change public support or behaviors but did increase beliefs about the importance of citizen engagement. Overall, our findings suggest that ballot box biology messaging is effective at changing public opinion and thus may undermine future wildlife protection ballot initiatives if counter messaging is not developed and shared.

title: Machine learning-assisted axial fan blade optimization for electronics cooling
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Machine learning-assisted axial fan blade optimization for electronics cooling

keywords.keywords: Bayesian optimizationAxial fanCFDFlow rateNoise levelshaft power

detail.abstract: In an air-cooling system for electronic devices, the axial fan critically determines energy use, heat dissipation, and noise. To address shrinking cooling spaces and noise challenges, this study integrated CFD methods with Bayesian optimization (BO) to design fan blades achieving high airflow with low noise. A CFD model combining the fan with a finned heat pipe cooler simulated CPU cooling scenarios, obtaining flow rate Q at 2000 rpm. Aerodynamic and acoustic simulations further provided pressure fluctuations and sound pressure level (SPL). Starting from a commercial blade profile, parameterization using blade wrap angle and quadratic functions reduced dimensionality. These parameters and Q formed a high-dimensional black-box function. Therefore, a Gaussian process regression (GPR) machine learning model was employed to rapidly identify the optimal Q combination from the explored data. Prototype experiments validated the CFD models. Results showed a 24% increase in Q compared to the original design, reducing CPU surface temperature by over 2°C under a 280 W heat load. Among blades with >20% Q improvement, combinations exist where SPL match those of the prototype fan, achieving the optimization of conflicting parameters. Sensitivity analysis clarified the effect of each parameter on Q, static pressure rise P, and SPL, guiding key parameter optimization for axial fans in electronic cooling.

title: The Fiscal Effects of Mandatory Disclosure: Causal Evidence from Brazil's Freedom of Information Act
affiliations: Universidade Estadual de Mato Grosso, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Universidade Federal de Mato Grosso

detail.title: The Fiscal Effects of Mandatory Disclosure: Causal Evidence from Brazil's Freedom of Information Act
detail.abstract: We estimate the causal effect of mandatory fiscal disclosure on municipal public investment in Brazil. Exploiting the population threshold of 10,000 inhabitants established by Brazil's 2012 Freedom of Information Act (Lei de Acesso à Informação, LAI) as an instrument in a Fuzzy Regression Discontinuity Design, we find that mandatory disclosure raises total municipal investment per capita by R$ 61-138, health investment by R$ 86-150, and education investment by R$ 93-259. Effects emerge with a one-year lag and strengthen through 2016, consistent with an electoral accountability mechanism: the compulsory publication of capital expenditures reduces information asymmetry between mayors and voters, incentivizing mayors to increase visible public spending as a credible signal of managerial competence. A battery of robustness checks - including a density manipulation test, placebo cutoffs at 7,500 and 12,500 inhabitants, pretreatment covariate balance, and an Epanechnikov kernel-confirms the causal identification. Our findings suggest that well-designed transparency mandates can serve as effective instruments for expanding public investment, particularly in health and education.

title: Duty to Remove: Invoking “Costs” and the Second Act of Tibble V. Edison

detail.title: Duty to Remove: Invoking “Costs” and the Second Act of Tibble V. Edison

declarations.declarationOfInterest: N/A
declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: This Essay examines the underdeveloped implications of Tibble v. Edison International and its articulation of a continuing fiduciary duty to “monitor trust investments and remove imprudent ones.” While fiduciary monitoring has become widely operationalized through benchmarking, performance reporting, and fee review, the complementary duty to remove remains comparatively undertheorized in institutional practice. Tibble’s temporal understanding of prudence extends beyond fee litigation and applies more broadly to the evolving costs, constraints, and contractual characteristics of investments over time. Costs associated with exiting investments — including penalties, discounts, lockups, and liquidity restrictions — are not merely transactional inconveniences but characteristics of the investment itself that bear directly on continued prudence under “circumstances then prevailing.” The Essay contends that where contractual structures materially constrain a fiduciary’s future ability to comply with continuing obligations, those constraints themselves may trigger renewed prudence analysis.

title: WaveRiderScan: News-Adjusted Preference Scoring

detail.title: WaveRiderScan: News-Adjusted Preference Scoring

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The AI model discussed in this paper—the Waverider News Assessment Score—is a proprietary technology developed and owned by the author’s organizations. This paper is intended to provide a technical and analytical overview of the model's performance and methodology.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Ethical approval was not required as this study does not involve human participants or animal subjects. The research focuses on the algorithmic assessment of public news data and technical model performance. All data utilized in the study was handled in accordance with standard data privacy and usage policies.
declarations.funderStatement: This research and the development of the AI model were entirely self-funded by SoftTelRG. No external grants or third-party funding were used in the production of this study.

detail.abstract:
Artificial intelligence is increasingly used in financial screening, yet many systems collapse public fundamental data, current news context, user preference, and implied recommendation into a single opaque score. This paper proposes a transparent two-layer scoring architecture that separates user-defined fundamental preference from bounded, AI-assisted news assessment. The first layer produces a Fundamental Preference Score in the range 0 to 50 reflecting how well a financial symbol matches a user's selected preference profile. The second layer, the News Context Assessment Component, produces a signed score in the range −50 to +50 representing the estimated directional effect of current news and events. The composite assessment is the algebraic sum, yielding a transparent range from −50 to +100.

The architecture is governed by two distinct methodologies operating in parallel. Builder authority handles structural changes — modifications to parameters, weights, methods, and rules — through an explicit propose, review, simulate, approve, version process. Self-adjustment via reconciliation handles operational, mechanical, and reversible work through a Voice queue and Provisional Layer that surface proposals based on the system's comparison of prior scores against observed outcomes. The two methodologies coexist by design: structural change is irreversible and judgment-bearing and therefore reserved to the builder; mechanical adjustment is reversible and rule-bound and therefore eligible for governed automation.

The architecture rests on twenty-four numbered commitments that constrain its behavior. The system consults a curated historical record of major events and a three-dimensional reference matrix at assessment time rather than embedding either into model weights. Parameters with associated methods produce bounded, signed contributions to the News Context Assessment; the news score is the algebraic sum of all active parameter contributions, decomposable down to specific historical references. The composite assessment is then produced separately by adding the News Context Assessment to the Fundamental Preference Score. The system begins operation with a small set of representative parameters and grows over time as reconciliation evidence and operational accuracy justify additions through the governed approval process.

title: Why does water quality improvement fail to persist after external nutrient loading reduction? Evidence of internal loading dominance from Yilong Lake
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Yunnan Normal University

detail.title: Why does water quality improvement fail to persist after external nutrient loading reduction? Evidence of internal loading dominance from Yilong Lake
detail.abstract: External nutrient loading reduction is the primary strategy for mitigating eutrophication in shallow lakes. However, many lakes do not exhibit sustained water quality improvement after strict external pollution control; instead, water quality often deteriorates abruptly following short-term recovery, a phenomenon closely linked to internal nutrient release from sediments. Using Yilong Lake as a representative case, this study constructed a long-term-data constrained process-based dynamic model coupled with a Bayesian hierarchical modelling approach, based on multi-year in-situ monitoring data covering external nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) loadings and in-lake water quality from 2014 to 2023. The results demonstrated that despite substantial reductions in external N and P anthropogenic loadings over the 2014–2023 study period, in-lake bulk nutrient concentrations underwent a sharp rebound after 2018. Model simulations revealed that the net release flux of total phosphorus from sediments (1.52 mg N/m³/day) was more than three times the external input, indicating that internal loading had replaced external inputs as the dominant nutrient source. Importantly, this shift coincided temporally with the large-scale decline of submerged macrophytes in 2017. Following the collapse of submerged macrophytes, their functions in inhibiting sediment resuspension and maintaining oxidized surface sediment conditions at the sediment surface were lost. This triggered a positive feedback loop of internal release, algal blooms, declining transparency, and further macrophyte loss, which ultimately offset the effectiveness of external nutrient reduction. This study quantitatively confirms that the dominance of internal loading is the direct cause of water quality deterioration after external nutrient reduction. We emphasize that shallow lake management must shift from exclusive external control to a synergistic strategy combining external and internal control, together with ecosystem structural restoration.

title: Robust Adaptive Trajectory Tracking for a Novel Six-DoF fully actuated UAV Using an ANFIS-Based Sliding Mode Controller
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Robust Adaptive Trajectory Tracking for a Novel Six-DoF fully actuated UAV Using an ANFIS-Based Sliding Mode Controller
detail.abstract: Hybrid Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) offer significant operational flexibility, but their highly nonlinear, coupled dynamics and vulnerability to external disturbances pose major challenges for precise trajectory tracking. Conventional Sliding Mode Control (SMC), while robust, suffers from the chattering phenomenon, which degrades actuator performance. To address these limitations, this paper proposes a novel Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System-based Sliding Mode Controller (ANFIS-SMC). The core innovation lies in replacing the discontinuous switching component of the SMC with a smooth and adaptive output from an ANFIS approximator. This structure mitigates chattering while preserving the inherent robustness of SMC. The ANFIS model is systematically trained offline using the sliding surface as the input and the ideal discontinuous control signal as the target output, enabling it to learn the system’s nonlinearities. Furthermore, a decoupling strategy is implemented to simplify the multivariable control problem into independent subsystems. The finite-time stability of the closed-loop system, including the ANFIS approximation error, is rigorously proven using Lyapunov theory. Comprehensive MATLAB simulations are conducted to validate the proposed controller’s performance against conventional SMC and a Fuzzy-SMC (FSMC) under nominal conditions, parameter uncertainties, and external wind gusts. The results are compelling: using the Integral of Time-weighted Absolute Error (ITAE) criterion, the proposed ANFIS-SMC achieves a tracking error reduction of approximately 91% compared to FSMC and over 98% compared to SMC across all three axes. These findings demonstrate the superior tracking accuracy, robustness, and chattering suppression of the proposed method, highlighting its high potential for real-world deployment in complex autonomous missions

title: Frugal AI Narrative and Electricity Market Prices
affiliations: University of Sousse, Lyon Catholic University, affiliation not provided to SSRN and Trinity University

detail.title: Frugal AI Narrative and Electricity Market Prices
detail.abstract: This paper provides the first empirical evidence on the impact of attention to frugal artificial intelligence (FAI) on electricity prices. Using both constant and time-varying local projection (LP) models, we document a heterogeneous, state-dependent response of electricity prices to frugal AI narrative. The results reveal a positive but short-lived effect in the near term, followed by a persistent and statistically significant negative response on longer horizons. These findings suggest that, although FAI may initially exert upward pressure on electricity demand, it ultimately contributes to moderating energy costs through efficiency gains.

title: Estimation and Prediction of the Burnable Absorber Rod Locations Effect in a Dual-cooled Accident-Tolerant Fuel (DC-ATF) Assembly Using the Gene Expression Programming Algorithm
affiliations: University of Isfahan and University of Isfahan

detail.title: Estimation and Prediction of the Burnable Absorber Rod Locations Effect in a Dual-cooled Accident-Tolerant Fuel (DC-ATF) Assembly Using the Gene Expression Programming Algorithm
detail.abstract: Accident-Tolerant Fuels (ATFs) represent a significant advancement in enhancing reactor safety, with dual-cooled designs offering improved thermal–hydraulic performance. The placement of burnable absorber (BA) rods within such assemblies critically influences neutronic behavior, including reactivity control and power distribution. Traditional high-fidelity simulations for evaluating BA configurations are computationally intensive, limiting large-scale parametric studies. This study proposes a data-driven predictive framework using Gene Expression Programming (GEP) to estimate and predict the neutronic effects of BA rod locations in a dual-cooled ATF (DC-ATF) assembly. A comprehensive dataset was generated via MCNP6 Monte Carlo simulations for 50 distinct assembly configurations with varying BA arrangements. The GEP model was trained to establish explicit functional relationships between the BA rod configuration and key neutronic parameters, such as the thermal, fast, and total neutron flux peaking factors. Results demonstrate that the trained GEP model achieves high accuracy on the training data (R2 = 0.92), providing a computationally efficient surrogate for full-scale simulations. Although validation performance indicates a need for further model refinement, the framework successfully identifies optimal BA patterns that promote a flatter neutron flux distribution. This work underscores the potential of GEP as a transparent and efficient tool for accelerating the design and optimization of advanced nuclear fuel assemblies.

title: Beyond Speech: Social Media Liability and Product Design
affiliations: Stanford University, Law School and

detail.title: Beyond Speech: Social Media Liability and Product Design

declarations.ethicsApproval: N/A
declarations.funderStatement: N/A

detail.abstract: This article argues that contemporary debates over social media liability have been misconstrued as disputes about speech. Drawing on a breadth of interdisciplinary research in human-computer interaction, science and technology studies, psychology, medicine, media theory, and more, this article shows that social media today functions as an engineered environment akin to a designed consumer product rather than a neutral marketplace of ideas. By tracing key Section 230 cases, the evolution of communication law, and data privacy research, the article demonstrates that many platform harms can be regulated as matters of product architecture. This reframing allows lawmakers to target the mechanisms through which digital products generate risk without dismantling Section 230's core speech immunity. It also offers a more accurate and constitutionally sustainable foundation for platform regulation moving forward.

title: Targeted Persuasion
affiliations: , University of New South Wales (UNSW) and University of New South Wales (UNSW)

detail.title: Targeted Persuasion
detail.abstract: Sender maximizes how many receivers buy a widget of uncertain quality. She targets receivers to privately communicate information about the widget's quality. After the target chooses whether to buy the widget, other receivers observe the target's choice with probability increasing in the target's popularity. We prove two results that hold remarkably generally: Sender optimally communicates with targets as if no other receiver exists; a target's popularity is a double-edged sword for Sender. We fully characterize the optimal choice of a single target under multiple communication protocols and establish that Sender can benefit from protocols that constrain her communication.

title: British Citizenship via the EU Settlement Scheme: Some Socio-Legal Reflections
affiliations: University of Cambridge and University of Cambridge

detail.title: British Citizenship via the EU Settlement Scheme: Some Socio-Legal Reflections

publicationDetails.detailsText: University of Cambridge Faculty of Law Research Paper
publicationDetails.journalName: University of Cambridge Faculty of Law Legal Studies Research Paper Series

detail.abstract:
Following the EU referendum, EU citizens and their family members living in the UK had to register under the EU Settlement Scheme (EUSS), introduced in 2019, to secure their continued residency rights under the Withdrawal Agreement. Data from the UK Home Office’s EUSS shows that over 6 million EU nationals have already made applications to the scheme (and many are continuing to apply well after the 30 June 2021 deadline). However, our research with low paid EU migrant workers in Great Yarmouth shows that, for many, their status under EUSS does not feel ‘secure’; British citizenship is considered the ‘gold standard’ of security post-Brexit in the UK. 

We shall argue that many consider applying for British citizenship for reasons of pragmatism, rather than principle; they want the security that comes from holding British nationality because they doubt that the rights under the EU Settlement Scheme are sufficient. Parents particularly want British citizenship for their children because they see it as a way of investing in their child’s future. For others, it is about claiming what they consider as a right to which they are entitled, and an improvement to their social status. None of the explanations given by our participants talk of the general reasons often associated with citizenship, namely principle or patriotism. For our interviewees, their approach is strategic and instrumental, obtaining another passport or citizenship for the benefits and opportunities it offers, a phenomenon well-known in the literature. However, for the particularly marginalised group of low paid workers in Great Yarmouth, the cost of applying for British citizenship, together with the language requirements necessary to pass the English language test, present significant barriers which may frustrate their ambitions.

title: Stablecoin Instability and Volatility Persistence: Evidence from USDT, USDC, and DAI
affiliations: Stevens Institute of Technology

detail.title: Stablecoin Instability and Volatility Persistence: Evidence from USDT, USDC, and DAI
detail.abstract: Stablecoin instability is analyzed using daily panel data for USDT, USDC, and DAI, with emphasis on volatility persistence and tail amplification. Fixed-effects panel regressions, quantile methods, and sGARCH(1,1) models are used to evaluate the relationship between realized volatility and peg deviations across multiple market regimes. Lagged realized volatility is strongly associated with larger next-day peg deviations, while 95th-percentile estimates indicate substantially stronger effects during stress periods. GARCH estimates imply highly persistent conditional volatility across all three stablecoins (𝛼 + 𝛽 ≈ 0.95), consistent with volatility clustering and prolonged vulnerability following market shocks. Event analysis of the March 2023 SVB episode further shows stress clustering, contagion across coins, and relative safe-haven behavior in USDT. The results suggest that stablecoin instability is closely linked to broader crypto-market volatility and liquidity stress.

detail.abstract: Pacific Islands Countries (PICs) stand at a pivotal crossroads in their developmental trajectories. While the global knowledge economy accelerates, these island nations grapple with the dual imperatives of digitising governance systems and institutionalising robust knowledge management (KM) frameworks. This article critically examines the multidimensional challenges confronting PICs in the pursuit of digital transformation, with particular focus on three interlocking domains: physical and telecommunications infrastructure deficits, workforce and human resource capacity constraints, and the chronic underfunding that undermines sustained progress. Drawing on policy frameworks from the Lagatoi Declaration on Digital Transformation of the Pacific (2023), the Pacific Regional Education Framework (PacREF), reports from the Carnegie Endowment for International Peace (2025), the Asian Development Bank (ADB), the International Telecommunication Union (ITU), and the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP), the article constructs an evidence-based analysis of barriers and enabling conditions. It further proposes targeted, context-sensitive recommendations for governments, regional bodies, and development partners to strengthen digitisation and knowledge management systems across the Blue Pacific Continent. The findings underscore that without coordinated investment in infrastructure resilience, systemic workforce development, and dedicated budgetary allocations, digitisation risks remaining superficial, donor-dependent, and ultimately unsustainable.

title: Insurance and Assurance: Government Interventions and Depositor Behavior in Crisis
affiliations: Ghent University, ZEW – Leibniz Centre for European Economic Research, University of Zurich - Department Finance and Ghent University - Centre for Russian International Socio-Political and Economic Studies (CERISE)

detail.title: Insurance and Assurance: Government Interventions and Depositor Behavior in Crisis

publicationDetails.detailsText: Swiss Finance Institute Research Paper No. 26-40
publicationDetails.journalName: Swiss Finance Institute Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: We examine how different forms of government intervention-explicit deposit insurance, implicit guarantees from nationalization, and assurance effects from re-privatizationshape depositor behavior during a banking crisis. Using proprietary monthly accountlevel data, we show that depositors respond to formal insurance limits even in an environment of broad state support, but adjust only partially. Stabilization is markedly stronger after the takeover by a financially strong private bank than during state ownership, despite unchanged statutory coverage. These patterns are inconsistent with a strong bailout-expectations view in which explicit insurance is largely irrelevant and instead point to credibility as a key determinant of depositor behavior. We further show that political trust amplifies the effectiveness of government guarantees. Overall, our findings highlight that the form and credibility of government backstops, rather than coverage levels alone, are central to funding stability during crises.

title: The effect of a Physical Education program on Fundamental Movement Skills in Chilean preschoolers: The Move Kids-24h Study Protocol
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Universidad Mayor, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The effect of a Physical Education program on Fundamental Movement Skills in Chilean preschoolers: The Move Kids-24h Study Protocol
detail.abstract: BackgroundFundamental movement skills’ development in early childhood is central to physical activity trajectories and health. However, most Chilean preschoolers are at risk of inadequate fundamental movement skills development due to socioeconomic vulnerability and limited access to structured, theory-based physical education programs. The Move Kids-24h project aims to evaluate the effects of a structured physical education program on Chilean preschoolers’ fundamental movement skills, movement behaviours (physical activity, sedentary time and sleep), physical fitness levels (muscular strength and speed-agility) and blood pressure.MethodsThe project was designed as a 6-month, 2-arm, parallel-group, cluster-randomized controlled trial with 6 months of follow-up and will include preschool children aged 3-4 years. The intervention will consist of 3 sessions/week, with a 45-minute duration, delivered by physical education teachers, while the control group will continue receiving their usual activities. All the baseline assessments will be repeated at the end of the intervention (6 months) and at follow-up (12 months). Statistical analysis will be conducted using Stata 18, based on analysis of covariance (ANCOVA).DiscussionThe results of this trial have the potential to inform future guidelines for physical education classes in Chilean preschoolers and strengthen the scientific knowledge on this type of intervention in this population.

title: Shareholder Empowerment and Corporate Information Environment: Evidence from Changes in Majority Voting (MV) Laws
affiliations: West Texas A&M University and Wilkes University - Jay Sidhu School of Business and Leadership

detail.title: Shareholder Empowerment and Corporate Information Environment: Evidence from Changes in Majority Voting (MV) Laws
detail.abstract: We examine whether majority voting laws improve a firm’s information environment despite concerns that such reforms are largely symbolic. We find that firms incorporated in states adopting MV laws experience a statistically significant decline in information uncertainty, measured by idiosyncratic stock return volatility, relative to firms in non-adopting states. The effect is concentrated in firms with higher earnings management and greater financing frictions. Overall, our findings suggest that even potentially diluted governance reforms can produce meaningful informational benefits.

title: The Anchored Risk Metric: Resolving the Capital Denominator Problem in Short VXX Positions
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Anchored Risk Metric: Resolving the Capital Denominator Problem in Short VXX Positions
detail.abstract: Shorting the VXX exchange-traded note offers returns driven by the structural decay of VIX futures roll yield. However, violent, mean-reverting price spikes often lead to forced margin liquidations, a state of mechanical ruin. By analyzing 441 price extrema spans in split-adjusted data from 2009 to 2025, this study identifies a historical multiplier ceiling: VXX has never increased by a factor greater than 6.0 from a preceding minimum within an extrema span. The Anchored Risk Metric (ARM) is proposed, which transforms the capital required for survival from a stochastic variable into a deterministic constant. This framework resolves Return on Capital (ROC) indeterminacy and demonstrates that risk-adjusted efficiency paradoxically increases during high-volatility regimes.

title: Green Conscience or Green Strain? Biodiversity Risk and Corporate Tax Avoidance
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Green Conscience or Green Strain? Biodiversity Risk and Corporate Tax Avoidance
detail.abstract: Biodiversity loss is a first-order source of financial risk, propagating through supply chain disruption, pharmaceutical resource depletion, zoonotic disease emergence, and tightening environmental regulation, with estimated annual damages of $4 to $20 trillion. Does this ecological pressure strain firms into more aggressive tax avoidance, or discipline them into fiscal restraint? We adjudicate these competing hypotheses using text-based 10-K biodiversity risk measures (Giglio et al., 2023) on 4,567 U.S. firms over 2001 to 2020. We document a robust disciplining effect: greater biodiversity risk, measured by disclosure frequency, negative sentiment, and regulatory orientation, produces significantly lower permanent book-tax differences and higher effective tax rates. The economic magnitude is substantive. A unit increase in the Regulation Score compresses permanent book-tax differences by 84 percent of the sample mean. Instrumental variable and propensity score matching estimates confirm the causal interpretation; OLS materially attenuates the true effect. Our finding of a negative association contrasts with recent positive evidence (Lin and Song, 2025; Trinh, 2025), a divergence we attribute to our sharper identification strategy. The results favor the reputational and political cost hypothesis: ecological scrutiny raises the implicit cost of aggressive tax planning above its marginal benefit. Our study advances the nascent biodiversity finance literature (Karolyi and Tobin-de la Puente, 2023; Guedhami et al., 2024) by demonstrating that ecological risk disciplines not only asset pricing but also internal corporate financial decision making.

title: Assessing CMIP6‐based future climate impacts on pearl millet yield under climate‐smart management across Senegal’s agroecological zones using DSSAT‐CERES‐Millet model
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Assessing CMIP6‐based future climate impacts on pearl millet yield under climate‐smart management across Senegal’s agroecological zones using DSSAT‐CERES‐Millet model
detail.abstract: Climate change threatens pearl millet production in West Africa’s drylands, requiring robust, evidence‐based adaptation options for smallholders. This study assesses mid‐century (2040–2069) climate impacts on pearl millet yields under climate‐smart management across four agroecological zones (Old Peanut Basin, New Peanut Basin, Eastern and Upper Casamance, and Sylvopastoralism Zone) in Senegal using the DSSAT CERES‐Millet model driven by six CMIP6 GCMs under SSP2‐4.5 and SSP5‐8.5, relative to a 1985–2014 baseline. Three management intervention strategies were evaluated: improved dual‐purpose and local varieties, optimized plant density (25,000 vs 12,500 hills ha⁻¹), and organo‐mineral micro‐dosing fertilizer strategies. Simulations projected declines up to 25% in precipitation, shortened growing seasons, and temperature increases of 1.4–3.4 °C, leading to yield reductions up to about 30% without adaptation options. Organo‐mineral fertilizer strategies (1.25–2.5 t ha⁻¹ manure combined with mineral fertilizer) reduced yield sensitivity by 12–21% under SSP5‐8.5 relative to mineral fertilizer alone, while higher planting density lowered climate‐related yield losses by 7–15%. Dual‐purpose varieties increased yields by 6–17% under the current climate but showed greater climate sensitivity, with declines of 6–27% under SSP5‐8.5. The Sylvopastoral zone emerged as the most vulnerable, whereas Old and New Peanut Basins showed more moderate yield declines. These results demonstrate that microdosing fertilizer strategies, optimized plant density, and context‐specific variety choice can enhance millet yield resilience under climate change and provide actionable guidance for climate‐smart agricultural planning in Senegal’s drylands and similar Sahelian systems.

title: Forecasting S&P 500 stock prices using Transformer models and hybrid LSTM-Transformer architectures: A comparative analysis
affiliations: University of Valencia, Polytechnic University of Valencia, Universitat de València and Polytechnic University of Valencia

detail.title: Forecasting S&P 500 stock prices using Transformer models and hybrid LSTM-Transformer architectures: A comparative analysis
detail.abstract: Stock price forecasting remains a challenging problem in financial econometrics due to the inherently nonlinear, highly volatile, and non-stationary characteristics of financial time series. This study examines the application of deep learning approaches based on Transformer architectures and hybrid LSTM–Transformer models for predicting closing prices of S&P 500 constituents. Using historical data spanning from 2015 to 2026, four modelling frameworks are evaluated: Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM), Bidirectional LSTM (BiLSTM), a pure Transformer architecture, and a hybrid LSTM–Transformer model. The empirical results indicate that attention-based architectures are capable of effectively capturing complex temporal dependencies in financial data.In particular, the proposed hybrid specification integrates the LSTM’s capacity for modelling sequential dependencies with the Transformer’s ability to capture long-range interactions through multi-head attention mechanisms. Overall, this study contributes to the existing literature on financial time series forecasting by providing a systematic comparative evaluation of contemporary deep learning architectures applied to a large-scale dataset of S&P 500 equities.

title: Divergent regulatory effects on denoised quantile-frequency spillovers between cryptocurrencies and Chinese financial markets ​
affiliations: Henan University of Science and Technology, Henan University of Science and Technology, Henan University of Science and Technology and Henan University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Divergent regulatory effects on denoised quantile-frequency spillovers between cryptocurrencies and Chinese financial markets ​
detail.abstract: This paper examines denoised quantile-frequency risk spillovers between cryptocurrencies and China's financial markets under divergent regulatory policies. We combine EMD-DFA denoising with the QVAR-BK spillover model and use event study and regression analysis to test heterogeneous policy impacts, based on daily data from 2020 to June 2025. We find that risk spillovers rise sharply under extreme market conditions. Mainland China's stock market is a persistent net risk receiver, while Hong Kong's stock market acts as a net risk transmitter during extreme conditions. Long-term fundamental factors dominate cross-market risk transmission. Restrictive policies in Mainland China significantly amplify risk spillovers, whereas Hong Kong's supportive regulatory policies dampen spillovers with a stronger effect. Our findings provide precise implications for cross-border cryptocurrency regulation and investor risk management.

title: Financial Market Spillovers during the U.S.–Iran Conflict: Evidence from a Quantile Connectedness Approach
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, and Adelaide University

detail.title: Financial Market Spillovers during the U.S.–Iran Conflict: Evidence from a Quantile Connectedness Approach
detail.abstract: We examine cross-asset spillovers among nine major financial markets, including crude oil, the U.S. dollar, gold, silver, the iShares 20+ Year Treasury Bond ETF (TLT), Bitcoin (BTC), Ethereum (ETH), the S\&P 500 index (SPX), and the CBOE Volatility Index (VIX), during the 2026 U.S.–Iran conflict using 5-minute intraday data and a quantile connectedness framework. Under extreme market conditions, a clear two-cluster structure emerges, where VIX, Brent, and DXY form a macro-financial risk cluster, while cryptocurrencies, equity, and precious metals constitute a broader asset cluster, with BTC, SPX, and TLT serving as transmission channels between the two groups. BTC, SPX, and ETH consistently act as net shock transmitters under tail conditions, whereas Brent and DXY primarily absorb spillovers. Time-varying connectedness reaches approximately 88\% during the peak of military escalation in mid-March before declining to around 60\% following ceasefire developments in late April. These findings highlight the distinctive characteristics of financial market connectedness during the U.S.–Iran war.

title: What Do Crypto Options Tell Us? Risk Premia Implied by BTC Option Prices
affiliations: , Simon Fraser University (SFU), and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: What Do Crypto Options Tell Us? Risk Premia Implied by BTC Option Prices
detail.abstract: We use Bitcoin (BTC) option prices to study the pricing of option-implied risk premia. Using a large cross-section of BTC options from Deribit, we recover the risk-neutral distribution and construct option-implied measures of variance, variance risk premium (VRP), and volatility-of-volatility (VoV). We show that (i) VRP is positive and highly persistent, (ii) higher-order risks are economically important in crypto markets, and (iii) option-implied factors—particularly VoV---predict BTC excess returns. These results hold in a market with limited institutional hedging demand and decentralized market making, providing evidence that option-implied premia are not solely driven by intermediary-based mechanisms but reflect compensation for risk.

title: The decision-usefulness of stock recommendations in analyst reports: Evidence from long-window excess returns
affiliations: Central University of Finance and Economics (CUFE)

detail.title: The decision-usefulness of stock recommendations in analyst reports: Evidence from long-window excess returns
detail.abstract: Using daily stock return data for 5,175 A-share firms listed on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges covering 2,187 trading days and investment rating data from 444,506 analyst reports over the 2016–2024 period, this study investigates the long-window excess returns of stocks recommended in analyst reports. The findings indicate that, after controlling for other factors, stocks recommended by analysts (i.e., those with standardized ratings of "Strong Buy" or "Buy") exhibit higher long-window excess returns relative to other stocks over the window from the report issuance date to the 240th trading day thereafter. Further analysis reveals that analyst-recommended stocks generate higher Alpha returns and more pronounced positive earnings changes following report publication. Finally, this study documents that institutional investors tend to initially increase their holdings in analyst-recommended stocks after report issuance before gradually reducing them, ultimately achieving a balanced position. By evaluating the decision-usefulness of analyst report investment ratings for long-term investment at the "stock–trading day" level, this study sheds light on how two key analyst capabilities—valuation and earnings forecasting—underpin the decision-usefulness of their recommendations, and further enriches empirical evidence on the interaction between analysts and institutional investors.

title: Scenario-Robust Irradiance Correction with Multivariate Meteorological Features for Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Forecasting under Complex Weather Conditions
affiliations: Northeast Electric Power University, Northeast Electric Power University, Northeast Electric Power University, Northeast Electric Power University, China United Network Communications Co Ltd and Politecnico di Torino

detail.title: Scenario-Robust Irradiance Correction with Multivariate Meteorological Features for Short-Term Photovoltaic Power Forecasting under Complex Weather Conditions
detail.abstract: Photovoltaic power forecasting (PVPF) under complex weather remains challenging because numerical weather prediction (NWP) irradiance often contains large errors, while rapid irradiance fluctuations weaken the generalization capability of conventional models. Existing post-processing methods improve irradiance forecasts, but they still struggle to characterize mixed irradiance patterns and scenario heterogeneity. To address these limitations, this study proposes a scene-adaptive deep learning framework for short-term PVPF. First, two representative complex-weather scenarios, sustained low-irradiance processes and strong irradiance ramp processes, are analyzed, and a cloud-wind composite disturbance index (CWCDI) is developed to characterize meteorological disturbances. Then, an irradiance correction model integrating Graph WaveNet and a mixture-of-experts layer, denoted as GWNet-MoE, is constructed. Graph WaveNet captures spatiotemporal dependencies among multiple PV plants, while the MoE layer learns scenario-specific correction patterns. Finally, the corrected irradiance and multi-source meteorological variables are fed into a channel-independent patch time series Transformer for PV power forecasting. Experimental results show that the proposed framework consistently outperforms comparison models under complex weather, reducing RMSE by 14.01% on average and demonstrating strong forecasting accuracy and scenario adaptability.

title: Divergent regulatory effects on denoised quantile-frequency spillovers between cryptocurrencies and Chinese financial markets ​
affiliations: Henan University of Science and Technology, Henan University of Science and Technology, Henan University of Science and Technology and Henan University of Science and Technology

detail.title: Divergent regulatory effects on denoised quantile-frequency spillovers between cryptocurrencies and Chinese financial markets ​
detail.abstract: This paper examines denoised quantile-frequency risk spillovers between cryptocurrencies and China's financial markets under divergent regulatory policies. We combine EMD-DFA denoising with the QVAR-BK spillover model and use event study and regression analysis to test heterogeneous policy impacts, based on daily data from 2020 to June 2025. We find that risk spillovers rise sharply under extreme market conditions. Mainland China's stock market is a persistent net risk receiver, while Hong Kong's stock market acts as a net risk transmitter during extreme conditions. Long-term fundamental factors dominate cross-market risk transmission. Restrictive policies in Mainland China significantly amplify risk spillovers, whereas Hong Kong's supportive regulatory policies dampen spillovers with a stronger effect. Our findings provide precise implications for cross-border cryptocurrency regulation and investor risk management.

title: Gentrification and the Amenity Ecology of Urban Neighbourhoods: Evidence from Paris
affiliations: ESSEC Business School

detail.title: Gentrification and the Amenity Ecology of Urban Neighbourhoods: Evidence from Paris
detail.abstract: ​​Using an establishment-level panel for Paris from 2014 to 2025, this paper studies how urban amenities adjust to neighbourhood upgrading. I use variation from a school-sector reform to validate housing price appreciation as a proxy for gentrification intensity. The results show that neighbourhoods experiencing stronger price growth exhibit systematically slower expansion of market-driven amenities, particularly those serving lower-income households. This effect operates primarily through reduced establishment entry, consistent with rising commercial costs limiting the profitability of marginal entrants. Spatial constraints play a central role in shaping this adjustment. In central Paris, where commercial space is scarce, even higher-income amenities do not expand despite rising demand. In contrast, in the broader Île-de-France region, where constraints are weaker, higher-income amenities expand strongly in high-growth areas. These findings highlight how spatial constraints determine the response of urban consumption environments to local demand shocks.

title: An Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Framework for Economic Zones: Conceptual Map of Core Variables and Statistical Associations
affiliations: Maalexi Inc.

detail.title: An Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Framework for Economic Zones: Conceptual Map of Core Variables and Statistical Associations
detail.abstract: Special Economic Zones (SEZs) are among the most widely deployed instruments of economic development policy worldwide, yet empirical research on the conditions that support their entrepreneurial potential remains limited. This study develops and empirically explores an eighteen-variable Entrepreneurial Ecosystem Framework for Economic Zones (EEF-EZ) by integrating entrepreneurial ecosystem theory with the SEZ policy literature. Seven variables adapted from Isenberg's (2011) foundational model and eleven variables derived from the SEZ empirical literature were assessed through a purposive multi-country survey of 83 senior practitioners and decision-makers across 23 countries, collectively representing approximately 55 percent of global SEZ activity. The study measures practitioner perceptions of variable relevance-not objective zone performance outcomes-and all inferences are accordingly scoped as exploratory. Descriptive statistics with significance testing, inter-item correlation analysis, principal component factor analysis (with Varimax rotation), and per-variable multiple regression analysis are employed. Factor analysis yields three structural dimensions-Capital, Stabilisation, and Institutional-accounting for 67.25 percent of total variance. Regression analysis, with Bonferronicorrected significance thresholds (p < .003), identifies nine high-salience variables (R² ≥ .64) exhibiting strong statistical associations with other perceived variables, and seven lower-salience variables with weaker or more contextually specific patterns. Per-construct reliability statistics are reported for all eighteen variables.
