affiliations: Goethe University Frankfurt - Finance Department, Goethe University Frankfurt,  and Goethe University Frankfurt - Department of Finance

detail.title: Optimizing Retirement Financial Strategies: Integrating Annuities, Defined Contribution Plans, and Long-Term Care Costs
detail.abstract: Nursing home costs in the United States now exceed $100,000 per year, and government assistance programs such as Medicaid help out only when retirees are largely destitute. Moreover, health shocks driving the need for such care can arise suddenly in old age, are frequently permanent in nature, and can be associated with declining mental and physical abilities. These facts raise the important question of how households can best prepare to finance this final phase of life. Building on past research, we determine how retirees should manage payouts from defined contribution plans to balance trade-offs between consumption and health care cost shocks, using both retirement plan assets and annuitization. Our analysis explicitly integrates the role of taxes, required minimum distributions, bequest motives, and the possibility of retiree insolvency. We conclude that payout annuities, especially deferred and variable annuities, can be quite valuable for retirees, even when they face health shocks in later life.

title: The Impact of Good Governance on Ease of Doing Business in Madhesh Province, Nepal
affiliations: Madhesh University

detail.title: The Impact of Good Governance on Ease of Doing Business in Madhesh Province, Nepal
detail.abstract: Madhesh Province-Nepal's southernmost federal unit bordering India-possesses significant agro-industrial potential yet consistently ranks at the bottom of provincial competitiveness indices. This paper investigates the relationship between the quality of governance and the ease of doing business in Madhesh Province through a secondary data analysis drawing on the World Bank's Worldwide Governance Indicators (WGI), the Nepal Competitiveness Index (NCI, 2025), World Bank Doing Business archives, and national investment climate assessments. Employing a descriptive-analytical framework and comparative provincial benchmarking, the study identifies chronic deficits in political stability, regulatory quality, control of corruption, and government effectiveness as proximate causes of weak investor confidence, limited formal-sector enterprise registration, and poor infrastructure service delivery. The paper further maps five governance dimensions against ease-of-doing-business sub-indicators relevant to sub-national contexts. Findings suggest that governance failures-particularly political instability and corruption-constitute the primary structural barriers to private sector development in a province with otherwise considerable economic endowments. Policy recommendations target provincial legislative reforms, one-stop investment facilitation, and digitisation of land and permit services.

title: Law on Related Party Transactions for Private Companies in Cyprus, Poland, and Belgium: A Comparative Overview

detail.title: Law on Related Party Transactions for Private Companies in Cyprus, Poland, and Belgium: A Comparative Overview

declarations.funderStatement: This research and author were supported by EU Horizon Europe under the Marie Skłodowska-Curie COFUND grant No 101081327 YUFE4Postdocs.

detail.abstract: EU law remains largely silent on related party transactions (RPTs) in private companies. Nevertheless, agency conflicts between shareholders and directors or managers may still arise, making it crucial to protect creditors and other external stakeholders. These issues are typically regulated under domestic law. This article provides a comparative examination of the existing safeguards against value-decreasing RPTs in private companies in Cyprus, Poland, and Belgium. It concentrates on the following forms of entrepreneurial entities: the private company limited by shares (Ltd.) in Cyprus, the limited liability company (sp. z o.o.) in Poland, and the private company (BV/SRL) in Belgium.

title: Financing the Freight Railway Infrastructure: An Underappreciated Policy Option?
affiliations: U.S. Department of Justice - Economic Analysis Group

detail.title: Financing the Freight Railway Infrastructure: An Underappreciated Policy Option?

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares that he has no personal or financial interests that may have or could be perceived to have influenced this study.
declarations.funderStatement: None

detail.abstract: Reform and restructuring of state-owned monopoly freight railways have generally followed one of two strategies. Each has had some success, but the European model of competing train operating companies over a monopoly track has suffered from a lack of reliable infrastructure funding, while the Americas model of competition among vertically integrated railways has suffered from the difficulty of protecting "captive" shippers. This paper proposes a third option that arguably addresses the weaknesses of both models: the "competitive rules joint venture" already observed in US, Canadian, and Mexican port and belt railroads.

title: Credit Shocks and Populism
affiliations: and Brown University - Watson Institute for International and Public Affairs

detail.title: Credit Shocks and Populism
detail.abstract: This paper shows that credit shocks are key drivers of populist sentiment. Exploiting spatial variation in exposure to an exogenous lending cut by a large German bank in 2007-08, we find that exposure to the credit shock leads to a persistent increase in populist political preferences. To explore the shift in demand for populism activated by the shock, we measure the degree of populist rhetoric and the salience of bank-related topics to each party over time using a machine learning technique on the corpus of parliamentary speeches in Germany. A countylevel analysis suggests that the underlying mechanism lies in the perceived decay of the local economy across voters that stems from the credit shock. A machine learning decomposition of the individual causal effects indicates that labour market history is the most important factor shaping the response in populist preferences.

title: Sex, Drugs, and LLMs: Social Desirability Bias in Language Models
affiliations: , Stanford University, University of Chicago,  and

detail.title: Sex, Drugs, and LLMs: Social Desirability Bias in Language Models
detail.abstract: When surveys ask about sensitive topics, respondents often shift their answers toward what seems socially acceptable, underreporting behaviors such as drug use or infidelity and overreporting behaviors such as voting, exercise, or charitable giving. We show that large language models (LLMs) often exhibit the same pattern. This cannot be explained solely by safety-related refusals: although some models decline to answer the most sensitive questions, across 13 models and 15 case studies, responses were generally closer to biased human self-reports than to the best available behavioral benchmarks. Using an open weights LLM, we show that information about actual behavior remains present in the model's internal representations, even when its final answer is pulled toward the socially desirable response. Steering those activations moves responses closer to actual behavior in 13 of 15 case studies. Prompting is less effective: providing the true base rate improves accuracy somewhat, while instructing the model to ignore social norms or warning that its answers will be checked has little effect. We interpret these results as evidence of a gap between internal representation and reported output in LLMs. Social desirability bias therefore provides a useful setting for studying this mismatch. At the same time, because accuracy can be substantially improved, LLM-based social simulations should not be written off.

title: What Ties Us Together? Explaining Synchronized GDP Volatility
affiliations: Universidad de Alicante, University of Granada and Federal Reserve Bank of Boston

detail.title: What Ties Us Together? Explaining Synchronized GDP Volatility
detail.abstract: Amidst heightened policy uncertainty, understanding the drivers of global macroeconomic instability becomes increasingly critical. While the dynamics of individual country volatility are widely documented, the factors that explain their co-movement internationally remain less understood. This paper studies the determinants of output volatility synchronization using data for 42 economies worldwide. We construct a bilateral time-varying index of volatility synchronization and infer its drivers using Bayesian Model Averaging, complemented by Weighted Average Least Squares and LASSO. We find that differences in Total Factor Productivity volatility, interest rate volatility and fiscal policy volatility are the most robust predictors of crosscountry synchronization, with some nuances when differentiating between developed and developing countries. Overall, the results highlight the role of technological divergence and macroeconomic policy uncertainty in shaping the international co-movement of output volatility.

title: Dependency & Regime Modelling in Probabilistic Valuation
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Dependency & Regime Modelling in Probabilistic Valuation
detail.abstract: Monte Carlo valuation ranges are only interpretable if readers understand how risk factors are allowed to move together. In real estate, the critical joint behaviour is often regime-shaped: when liquidity tightens, weaker leasing, wider yields, and more conservative buyer underwriting can arrive together, and diversification across "independent" assumptions evaporates. This paper sets out a minimum-defensible approach to modelling dependency without turning probabilistic valuation into a fragile, highparameter copula exercise. It compares four practical options-(i) independence (explicitly disclosed), (ii) a fixed correlation matrix, (iii) a stress-correlation overlay applied only to labelled stress intervals, and (iv) regime-switching scenarios that swap the dependency structure (and optionally marginal inputs) across states. The paper then proposes "dependency disclosure tiers" (basic → intermediate → advanced) aligned to evidence quality and governance capacity, and it provides two concrete outputs: a standard dependency declaration suitable for valuation files and audit review, and a stress overlay recipe that a valuation committee can approve once and apply consistently. The emphasis throughout is on transparency, parameter parsimony, and auditability: the objective is not to predict crises, but to avoid understating tails by accident.

title: End-of-life Medical Spending: Patterns and Household Spillovers
affiliations: Johannes Kepler University Linz - Department of Economics and

detail.title: End-of-life Medical Spending: Patterns and Household Spillovers
detail.abstract: Medical spending is highly concentrated at the end of life and varies widely across patients, raising a first-order welfare question about whether marginal end-of-life spending reflects waste or generates meaningful benefits. Using Austrian administrative data, we document that end-of-life spending has grown markedly over time and remains highly dispersed even conditional on diagnosis, with predicted mortality explaining only a small share of the variation. We then study a largely underexplored margin: spillovers onto surviving spouses. Event study estimates show large and persistent changes in spouses’ employment and healthcare use around spousal death. However, these dynamics are essentially invariant to the decedent’s end-of-life spending intensity, a finding that is robust to different measures of spending intensity and to an instrumental variables design exploiting provider-level practice variation. Together, these results are consistent with an important role for inefficiencies in end-of-life care.

title: Patents, Firm Rents, and Worker Compensation: Causal Evidence from Quasi-Random Patent Allocation
affiliations: and Halle Institute for Economic Research, Centre for European Economic Research (ZEW)

detail.title: Patents, Firm Rents, and Worker Compensation: Causal Evidence from Quasi-Random Patent Allocation
detail.abstract: This paper provides new causal evidence on how patent allowances affect firms and their employees based on quasi-random assignment of patent applications to examiners. Exploiting employer–employee records with newly linked German firm data and web-scraped patent documents, we show that patent-induced shocks reduce firm exit, improve productivity, and increase wages, with rent-sharing elasticities between 0.10 and 0.21. Wage gains are broadly observed across occupational tasks, with high heterogeneity: managers benefit disproportionately in publicly traded firms, whereas broader wage increases accrue to workers in non-traded firms. Our findings highlight the role of institutional features and firm organization in shaping how rents are shared.

title: The Macroeconomics of Wage Rigidity and Job Separations
affiliations: Federal Reserve Banks - Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta, University of Texas at Austin, Columbia University and

detail.title: The Macroeconomics of Wage Rigidity and Job Separations
detail.abstract: We study the macroeconomic implications of wage-rigidity-induced job separations in an equilibrium labor market model with four features: worker productivity shocks, staggered wage contracts, search frictions, and two-sided lack of commitment. Endogenous quits and layoffs are unilaterally initiated whenever a worker’s wage-to-productivity ratio or markdown moves outside an inaction region. We derive sufficient statistics for the labor market response to inflationary shocks based on the distribution of markdowns, which we show how to identify using microdata on wage changes and worker flows between jobs. Using an extension of the model for quantitative analysis, we find that aggregate shocks generate significant cyclicality in endogenous job separations, including 62 percent of the empirical quit volatility and 94 percent of the empirical layoff volatility.

title: Fiscal Policy and Transition Risk
affiliations: Georgia State University, Georgia State University, Georgia State University - Department of Economics and

detail.title: Fiscal Policy and Transition Risk
detail.abstract: We study how climate policy can interact with distortionary fiscal policy and potentially lead to transition risk. Using an environmental dynamic stochastic general equilibrium model that features financial frictions and preexisting labor and capital taxes, we simulate a carbon tax and an abatement subsidy under different scenarios for returning carbon tax revenue or financing the subsidy. We find novel policy implications and important differences between the carbon tax and the subsidy. Under both policies, transition dynamics can differ sharply from long-run outcomes. For the carbon tax, transition dynamics depend on both financial frictions and the choice of revenue recycling. For the abatement subsidy, distortionary financing can generate contractionary transition dynamics, because of financial frictions. Macroprudential policy can mitigate transition risk under the carbon tax but has little effect under the subsidy.

title: A solver-in-the-loop framework for end-to-end differentiable coastal hydrodynamics
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A solver-in-the-loop framework for end-to-end differentiable coastal hydrodynamics
detail.abstract: Numerical simulation of wave propagation and run-up is a cornerstone of coastal engineering and tsunami hazard assessment. However, applying these forward models to inverse problems, such as bathymetry estimation, source inversion, and structural optimization, remains notoriously difficult due to the rigidity and high computational cost of deriving discrete adjoints. In this paper, we introduce \texttt{AegirJAX}, a fully differentiable hydrodynamic solver based on the depth-integrated, non-hydrostatic shallow-water equations. By implementing the solver entirely within a reverse-mode automatic differentiation framework, \texttt{AegirJAX} treats the time-marching physics loop as a continuous computational graph. We demonstrate the framework's versatility across a suite of scientific machine learning tasks: (1) discovering regime-specific neural corrections for model misspecifications in highly dispersive wave propagation; (2) performing continuous topology optimization for breakwater design; (3) training recurrent neural networks in-the-loop for active wave cancellation; and (4) inverting hidden bathymetry and submarine landslide kinematics directly from downstream sensor data. The proposed differentiable paradigm fundamentally blurs the line between forward simulation and inverse optimization, offering a unified, end-to-end framework for coastal hydrodynamics.

title: Bias-Aware Water Table Fluctuation: From Point Estimator to Decision Framework for Groundwater Recharge
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Bias-Aware Water Table Fluctuation: From Point Estimator to Decision Framework for Groundwater Recharge
detail.abstract: The Water Table Fluctuation (WTF) method is widely used to estimate groundwater recharge from water-level records but suffers from two basin-scale limitations: spatial averaging of specific yield ([[EQUATION]]) and an unquantified structural bias in the WTF identity itself. We reframe WTF as a biased observation operator that requires correction and independent bounding to recover physically meaningful recharge. We propose three coordinated components — a Soil-weighted upscaling using national digital soil-map polygons, a hierarchical Bayesian[[EQUATION]]inference layer, and a learned bias-correction regression trained on a multi-layer cascade vadose surrogate — and evaluate them on a five-scenario synthetic benchmark and a seven-well, two-watershed field application in Yeongcheon, South Korea.The Soil-weighted estimator reduces grid-scale RMSE by 21–75% relative to a lumped baseline and matches Ensemble Kalman Filter accuracy at ~56× lower computational cost. Calibration against the cascade surrogate exposes a 5–49% bias of the WTF estimate against the cascade truth, which is independently bounded from above by a Richards mixed-form reference (§6.6); the bias-correction regression ([[EQUATION]] via 5-fold cross-validation; random and block-CV indistinguishable, §4.4 Table 5) reduces the residual mean bias from [[EQUATION]] to [[EQUATION]] and lowers per-cell RMSE by 46%. A user-controllable conservatism parameter α attenuates the correction; we report the [[EQUATION]] reporting triple (9.33–9.34% / 10.32–10.40% / 13.73–14.11% of [[EQUATION]]) rather than a single calibrated value, since no in-situ recharge measurement is available to anchor a calibrated optimum at the Yeongcheon wells (§4.5).Two independent physically-based references at the Yeongcheon site — UZF kinematic-wave (gravity-only; 7.2% of[[EQUATION]]) and HYDRUS-class Mixed-form Richards (capillary + gravity; 20.6% of[[EQUATION]]) — bracket all WTF-based estimates ([[EQUATION]]: 9.3–14.1%) and the FAO-56 SWB result (16%) for Loam under the actual climate. Critically, the cascade truth itself (24.6%) lies above the Richards upper bound, providing model-independent evidence that cascade-class synthetic surrogates overestimate recharge for medium-textured soils and reinforcing the [[EQUATION]] ceiling on cascade-strength correction (§6.6). The factor-of-three width of the resulting model-structure envelope — which no proxy combination in this study could narrow further — is itself a substantive result: the WTF community’s de facto practice of reporting a single point estimate implicitly claims an envelope of zero, which the present multi-proxy analysis falsifies. We therefore argue that WTF-based recharge estimates intended for decision support should be reported as a triple-plus-bracket — at minimum a cascade–Richards physical bracket and an independent multi-proxy band around an α-spectrum — rather than as a single point value.

title: A Distributionally Robust Cooperative Optimization Scheduling Approach for Multi-Microgrid Systems with P2P Negotiation Mechanism
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: A Distributionally Robust Cooperative Optimization Scheduling Approach for Multi-Microgrid Systems with P2P Negotiation Mechanism
detail.abstract: With the transformation of energy systems toward distributed and cooperative paradigms, multi-microgrid (MMG) systems have emerged as a critical platform for renewable energy integration, attracting significant attention for their cooperative scheduling and distributed trading strategies. This study focuses on the cooperative optimization problem of MMGs under a peer-to-peer (P2P) trading framework, proposing an innovative bargaining mechanism-driven two-stage distributionally robust optimization (DRO) model.First, an energy management model for MMG cooperative scheduling is formulated by incorporating wind-photovoltaic units, gas turbines, energy storage systems, and controllable loads, where affine policy-based adjustment rules are employed to handle renewable power uncertainty.Second, a two-stage DRO model is established to address the day-ahead and real-time decision-making sequence.Furthermore, an adaptive P2P bargaining algorithm is designed, where each microgrid independently solves its optimal decisions via the column-and-constraint generation (C&CG) algorithm in a parallel manner. The P2P electricity prices are dynamically adjusted through boundary information exchange until convergence is achieved.Finally, simulation tests on the IEEE 123-bus distribution system validate the effectiveness of the proposed model, demonstrating its dual advantages in economic efficiency and renewable energy accommodation.

title: Multiattribute Q-Learning: Identification, Economic Interpretation and Behavioral Testing in a Route Choice Experiment
affiliations: University of Chile, Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile and University of Chile

detail.title: Multiattribute Q-Learning: Identification, Economic Interpretation and Behavioral Testing in a Route Choice Experiment
detail.abstract: Random Utility Maximization (RUM) models do not capture relevant psychological aspects underlying travel behavior decisions, learning processes being one of them. However, RUM models can be enriched by drawing on the cognitive psychology literature to represent the dynamics of learning and the effects of expe- riences on choices. Reinforcement Learning models, particularly Q-Learning, have been widely studied in psychology to represent the effects of rewards (i.e., decision outcomes) on future choices, subject to identifi- able cognitive parameters such as the learning rate. However, typical RL formulations adopt unidimensional rewards, with assumed known positive or negative effects on subjects. That is, rewards are not formulated as a function of attributes and are not conditioned on subjective taste parameters. Rather, the subjective value of the reward is assumed to be known by the modeler. These limitations constrain the applicability of learning models to real-life transport choices and beyond, where the subjective valuation of a multidimen- sional vector of attributes is central. In this article, we extend Q-Learning to capture multiattribute rewards accounting for individuals’ subjective perceived satisfaction with each attribute. The model is shown to be identifiable and well behaved under varying reward sizes, learning rate magnitudes, and sample sizes. More- over, the model preserves a simple, flexible, and interpretable structure. We discuss the economic meaning of the model, analytically showing that marginal rates of substitution can be straightforwardly derived and interpreted. Finally, we estimate the model using a route choice experiment and show that it can be further extended to capture inter- and intra-individual heterogeneity. These results extend Q-Learning to real-life applications in transport and beyond, and enrich our modeling toolbox to capture the underlying learning processes behind human choices.

title: Adaptive Semantic-Visual Routing with Hierarchical Semantic Guidance for Few-Shot Image Classification
affiliations: Shimane University, Jiangsu Ocean University, Jiangsu Ocean University, Communication University of China, University College London - Bartlett School of Sustainable Construction, affiliation not provided to SSRN, Anhui University of Science and Technology and Jiangsu Ocean University

detail.title: Adaptive Semantic-Visual Routing with Hierarchical Semantic Guidance for Few-Shot Image Classification
detail.abstract: Few-shot image classification recognizes unseen classes from limited labeled data, where the main challenge is to construct reliable class representations while effectively exploiting transferable visual knowledge from different depths of a pre-trained backbone. Existing methods often rely on flat semantic cues and fixed feature fusion, which limits their ability to fully utilize hierarchical transformer representations and to adapt feature usage to categories with different semantic complexity. To address this issue, we propose Adaptive Semantic-Visual Routing (ASVR), a framework that organizes class knowledge into a semantic hierarchy spanning category identity, contextual description, taxonomic definition, and fine-grained visual attributes, and then uses these cues to guide dynamic aggregation of transformer features across layers. In this way, ASVR enables more flexible semantic-visual alignment by emphasizing shallow visual evidence for coarse-grained recognition and deeper semantic features when subtle distinctions are required. ASVR performs strongly on several few-shot benchmarks. Performance surpasses strong baselines. Ablation studies and visualization reveal hierarchical semantic guidance and adaptive routing support complementary aspects of the model.

title: Dynamic Fiscal Scarcity and State-Constrained Green Capital Reallocation
affiliations: Corvinus University of Budapest

detail.title: Dynamic Fiscal Scarcity and State-Constrained Green Capital Reallocation
detail.abstract: We study a finite-horizon optimal-control problem in which a planner reallocates an exogenous replacement flow between dirty and clean capital under a pathwise fiscal-space constraint. The control affects only the composition of new capital inflows. Fiscal space evolves endogenously through capital-linked fiscal contributions, carrying returns, and support expenditures, and must remain nonnegative at all dates.We characterize the optimal policy using a state-constrained maximum principle. The pointwise support rule compares the reallocation shadow gain from shifting investment toward clean capital with a scarcity-adjusted marginal support cost. The associated fiscal wedge is forward looking: it equals the discounted value of future state-constraint pressure. Fiscal scarcity can therefore tighten current support even when the fiscal boundary is not currently binding.The optimal path is organized by arc structure. On slack arcs without future fiscal stress, policy coincides with the unconstrained reallocation benchmark. On slack arcs with anticipated future binding, support is tightened by the scarcity wedge. On binding arcs, support is pinned down by a flow-feasibility ceiling rather than by the unconstrained interior condition. The model therefore generates endogenous attenuation, capping, shutdown, and release of support along the transition path.A computational illustration based on residential heating implements the problem as a hard state-constrained nonlinear program. Two scenarios, holding fixed the technological, preference, and cost primitives while varying the institutional fiscal environment, demonstrate the mechanism: a baseline scenario displays anticipatory scarcity with terminal binding pressure, while a high-scarcity institutional stress test exhibits a visible interior binding arc followed by release. The computation shows that the analytical arc geometry and the binding-arc support ceiling can appear in a quantitatively disciplined transition environment.

title: Stochastic Dual Dynamic Programming for Industrial Decarbonisation Investment Planning with Ancillary Market Flexibility
affiliations: University of Sheffield, University of Sheffield and University of Wisconsin-Madison

detail.title: Stochastic Dual Dynamic Programming for Industrial Decarbonisation Investment Planning with Ancillary Market Flexibility
detail.abstract: Industrial decarbonisation requires capital commitments on 20–30 year asset lifetimes under uncertain energy, carbon, and technology costs. This paper presents the first application of stochastic dual dynamic programming (SDDP) to site-level decarbonisation investment planning, coupling discrete technology commissioning and timing with hourly operational dispatch and ancillary market participation under correlated price uncertainty. Applied to a UK industrial CHP plant, the adaptive investment policy reduces expected 30-year cost by 6.3% ($23 M) relative to deterministic planning by deferring commitment until price signals resolve, and selecting different technologies on different realisations. This cost saving comes at an environmental cost. The same deferral that lowers expected cost keeps the existing gas CHP running during the waiting period, so the adaptive policy systematically emits 7–32% more CO₂ than a single-technology deterministic commitment, even with carbon priced at $80–150/tCO₂. This emissions premium responds to three parameters: ancillary market reward level (23% swing in technology adoption), price volatility regime (adoption shifts from diversified to concentrated hydrogen), and the interaction between operational flexibility instruments (27% super-additivity relative to independent evaluation). The framework generalises to other industrial sectors and regulatory jurisdictions.

title: Obscure disclosures: Strategic information concealment by informed traders
affiliations: Macquarie University, University of Technology Sydney (UTS), University of Technology Sydney (UTS) and University of Technology Sydney (UTS), UTS Business School, Students

detail.title: Obscure disclosures: Strategic information concealment by informed traders
detail.abstract: We examine strategic concealment of private information by major shareholders through obscured disclosures, and the impact this has on market quality. Information that is obscured by handwriting compulsory shareholding disclosures displays characteristics of informed trading, resulting in a significant long-term price reaction upon their announcement. Obscured disclosures are more common when the value of information is larger, in stocks with higher levels of information asymmetry, and are submitted during times of higher volatility. Further, we observe a significant post-announcement drift in returns following handwritten filings indicating that obscure informed disclosures undermine market efficiency.​

title: A Control-Oriented Digital Twin Architecture for Hybrid HVAC Systems: Conceptualization and Modelling on the HESTIA Energy System
affiliations: National University of Science and Technology POLITEHNICA Bucharest and National University of Science and Technology POLITEHNICA Bucharest

detail.title: A Control-Oriented Digital Twin Architecture for Hybrid HVAC Systems: Conceptualization and Modelling on the HESTIA Energy System
detail.abstract: This paper presents the HESTIA Digital Twin (DT), a control-oriented digital-physical architecture for real-time state estimation of a multi-source hybrid HVAC system. This experimental infrastructure integrates an air-source heat pump (ASHP), a methane gas condensing boiler, a puffer storage tank, and a rooftop photovoltaic array. The DT is organized as a four-layer hierarchical architecture encompassing physical instrumentation, data acquisition, model computation, and data visualization. The Model and Decision Layer is composed of three independent predictive sub-models: a Physics-Informed Neural Network (PINN) for ASHP performance prediction, a semi-empirical model for the gas boiler analysis, and three-node stratified ordinary differential equation model for the puffer tank. For the PV energy production data from the inverted was considered. A total seven-mode finite state machine encodes the economic dispatch logic, dynamically adapting the heat pump competitiveness threshold to prevailing electricity and gas tariffs. The ASHP PINN enforces four structural thermodynamic constraints, and the model was trained on 7,389 datapoints and 3,060 EN 14511 certified references obtained from two open-source databases. On the held-out test set, the model achieves R² = 0.796, MAE = 0.351, and RMSE = 0.515 for COP prediction, R² = 0.957 (MAE = 0.219 kW) for thermal output, and R² = 0.917 (MAE = 0.126 kW) for electrical power consumption, with zero violations of the Carnot upper bound recorded across all test samples. The gas boiler model reproduces manufacturer- declared efficiencies of 97% and 105% at the rated condensing and non-condensing operating conditions, with deviations below 2%. ​

title: ZID-Net: Zero-Inference Diffusion Prior Decoupling Network for Single Image Dehazing
affiliations: Hohai University, Hohai University, Hohai University, Hohai University and Hohai University

detail.title: ZID-Net: Zero-Inference Diffusion Prior Decoupling Network for Single Image Dehazing
detail.abstract: Single image dehazing is often constrained by a trade-off between restoration quality and computational efficiency. While efficient, CNN networks struggle to learn robust priors for dense and non-homogeneous haze. Conversely, diffusion models provide strong generative priors but suffer from severe inference latency and sampling instability. To address these limitations, we propose ZID-Net, a novel framework that explicitly decouples diffusion supervision from feed-forward inference. For efficient inference, we design a frequency-spatial decoupled feed-forward backbone. Within this backbone, a Channel-Spatial Laplacian Mask (CSLM) filters haze-amplified noise to extract purified structural details, while Lightweight Global Context Blocks (LGCBs) establish long-range spatial dependencies to capture the global variations of haze. A Dynamic Feature Arbitration Block (DFAB) then adaptively fuses these semantic and structural features for robust reconstruction. To provide this backbone with physical priors without the inference cost, we introduce a Zero-Inference Prior Propagation Head (ZI-PPH) during training. ZI-PPH leverages a conditional diffusion process to predict residual noise, providing degradation-aware structural supervision to the backbone. By discarding the diffusion branch at test time, ZID-Net integrates diffusion priors into a pure feed-forward architecture for accurate and efficient restoration. ZID-Net achieves 40.75 dB PSNR on the synthetic RESIDE dataset and outperforms existing methods with a 1.13 dB gain on real-world datasets. Additionally, it yields a 3.06 dB PSNR gain on the StateHaze1k remote sensing dataset with an inference time of just 19.35 ms. The project code is available at: https://github.com/XoomitLXH/ZID-Net.

title: Multi‐Source Domain Adaptation Method Based on Bhattacharyya distance Alignment and Mutual Information Distillation
affiliations: Anhui Polytechnic University, Anhui Polytechnic University and Anhui Polytechnic University

detail.title: Multi‐Source Domain Adaptation Method Based on Bhattacharyya distance Alignment and Mutual Information Distillation
detail.abstract: In multi-source domain adaptation, domain shifts among multiple source domains and the target domain often degrade classification performance on the target domain. To address this issue, this paper proposes a multi-source domain adaptation method that integrates Bhattacharyya distance joint distribution alignment and mutual information distillation.First, the proposed method models the Bhattacharyya distance between multiple source domain distributions and the target domain distribution as a convex optimization problem. Under the guidance of the optimal solution, the model is optimized to achieve simultaneous alignment of multiple source domain distributions and the target domain distribution in order to reduce the negative impact of cross-domain distribution discrepancies. Second, a cross-modal knowledge distillation mechanism is introduced. During iterative pseudo-label refinement, a vision-language model is employed to provide auxiliary supervision. Mutual information distillation further encourages the model to learn generic semantic knowledge from the vision-language model, improving the stability and robustness of cross-domain knowledge transfer. Experimental results on four public datasets show that the proposed method achieves improved average classification accuracy, demonstrating its feasibility and effectiveness.

title:
Publicly Available, Yet Still Inside Information under MAR: 
A Critical Appraisal of an Unfortunate Generalisation in Brännelius (CJEU, 4th ch., 16 April 2026, C-229/24)*
affiliations: Sorbonne Law School

detail.title:
Publicly Available, Yet Still Inside Information under MAR: 
A Critical Appraisal of an Unfortunate Generalisation in Brännelius (CJEU, 4th ch., 16 April 2026, C-229/24)*
detail.abstract: Called upon to rule directly, for the first time, on the conditions under which information ceases to be "non-public" within the meaning of Article 7(1)(a) of Regulation (EU) No 596/2014 on market abuse (MAR), the Court of Justice of the European Union, in its Brännelius judgment of 16 April 2026, enshrines a formal and exclusive conception of publicity: only a publication satisfying the cumulative requirements of Article 17 of MAR and of Article 2(1) of Implementing Regulation (EU) 2016/1055, relating to the permanent disclosure obligation of listed issuers, is apt to deprive information of its confidential nature. This generalisation, made in response to a case which by no means required it, calls for sustained discussion. It breaks with a European doctrinal and regulatory consensus to which the major traditions had rallied-the position of the European Securities and Markets Authority in its Q&A, German, Austrian, Italian and British scholarship, and the case law of France, Spain and Italy-which accepted, with nuances as to the perimeter of the relevant circle, that information may become public through means other than the issuer's formal publication. It is also part, together with the Finansinspektionen v. Carnegie Investment Bank judgment of 19 March 2026, of a movement extending the concept of inside information at both ends of its life span. Above all, by enshrining the principle that information that is factually public remains legally nonpublic until the issuer has published it in the prescribed forms, the judgment effects a reversal that opens the door, in a manner that is difficult to accept, to the prosecution of transactions based on information that is genuinely accessible to all. The silence opposed to the rigorously constructed thesis of Advocate General Kokott, which nevertheless reflected the state of European scholarship and the internal coherence of the regulation, completes the case for criticism of Brännelius and deprives it, at the very least, of the argumentative foundation that the importance of the question decided called for.

detail.title: From Policy to Market: The Role of Local Governance in the Creation and Effectiveness of Biodiversity Markets

declarations.declarationOfInterest: there is no such relationship

detail.abstract: This paper examines the role of the governance quality of local authorities in shaping the creation and effectiveness of biodiversity markets. Drawing on a novel, hand-collected dataset covering all registered Biodiversity Gain Sites (BGSs) created as part of England's Biodiversity Net Gain (BNG) programme between March 2024 and October 2025, 1,149 transactions across 677 developments, and governance and environmental data for all 337 English Local Planning Authorities (LPAs), we provide new evidence on the determinants of the creation and functioning of biodiversity markets. We show that ecological conditions primarily determine whether BGSs are established, while institutional capacity plays a more important role in shaping market outcomes, particularly the sale of biodiversity units. These findings reveal a clear division between the drivers of supply and those of market performance. Overall, our findings suggest that improving LPAs' administrative capacity may be as important as ecological targeting in ensuring the effectiveness of biodiversity markets. Strengthening LPA capabilities could therefore play a critical role in enabling the successful implementation of the BNG framework.

declarations.ethicsApproval: No patients/participants.

detail.abstract: Legislative efforts to restrict Pharmacy Benefit Managers' ("PBMs") steering practices and vertical integration rests on flawed economic assumptions. Economic analysis demonstrates that integrated PBM-insurers face strong incentives to lower rather than raise patient out-of-pocket prescription costs. Because insurers collect premiums and bear responsibility for patients' overall healthcare expenses, they internalize the costs of medication non-adherence caused by high drug prices, including increased hospitalizations representing approximately $100 billion annually. In contrast, independent pharmacies do not bear downstream healthcare costs, thus rationally set higher prices. Policy restrictions on steering and vertical integration therefore appear to prioritize independent pharmacy commercial interests over patient welfare, likely increasing costs and worsening health outcomes.

detail.title: Joint estimation of health status and remaining life of lithium-ion batteries based on 1D Residual CNN and Transformer attention mechanism
detail.abstract: This paper proposes a multi task learning model based on 1D Residual CNN and Transformer attention mechanism, aiming to improve the accuracy and stability of lithium-ion battery health state (SOH) and remaining useful life (RUL) estimation. By conducting charging and discharging experiments on two 18650 lithium batteries under different operating conditions, a large amount of data was collected, including battery discharge efficiency, energy, and SOH changes. The experimental results show that in the SOH estimation task, the MSE of this model under standard operating conditions is 0.00021, the RMSE is 0.01450, and the R ² is 0.9935; In the RUL estimation task, the MSE of the model is 13.23, RMSE is 3.64, and R ² is 0.9871, significantly better than traditional and advanced models. The ablation experiment further proves that the Transformer attention mechanism and multi task learning architecture contribute significantly to the performance of the model. In summary, the model proposed by this paper demonstrates excellent robustness and stability, and has strong practical application value.

title: Spatially varying determinants of motorbike ban acceptability in Hanoi: a multiscale logistic regression approach using GAMs
affiliations: University of Leeds, University of Auckland, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and University of Leeds

detail.title: Spatially varying determinants of motorbike ban acceptability in Hanoi: a multiscale logistic regression approach using GAMs
detail.abstract: Motorbikes in Hanoi cause congestion and have road safety and environmental impacts. A recent directive will progressively ban petrol (gasoline) motorbikes from inner urban districts by 2030. This paper describes statistical and spatial analyses of a travel survey of ~25,700 Hanoi residents to model the relationships between different socio-economic factors and support for such a ban. It applies a standard global binomial logistic regression which is extended to a spatial regression to quantify how these relationships vary spatially. A novel Generalized Additive Model (GAM) smooth framework was used to construct spatially varying coefficient (SVC) models. Critically, the approach undertakes model selection, and evaluates multiple models (~350,000) to determine which variables to include in spatial smooths. The best ranked model by AIC included spatial smooths for all but one of the predictor variables indicating the presence strong spatial dependencies in response to predictor relationships. The global model identified car ownership, car use and private property ownership as the strongest positive predictors of ban support, and distance from public transport as the dominant negative predictor. The SVC GAM provided a substantially better fit than the global model, capturing almost twice as much variation in the outcome. Three groups of response to predictor relationships were identified. The mapped coefficient surfaces indicate how the response to predictor relationships vary over space, highlight a transit rich inner core and where the relationship with ban support varied. These findings have direct policy implications and demonstrate the inferential value of using non-stationary approaches to examine such data.

title: The Regulatory Arbitrage Window: How Cross-Border AI Governance Asymmetries Create Strategic Opportunities and Risks

detail.title: The Regulatory Arbitrage Window: How Cross-Border AI Governance Asymmetries Create Strategic Opportunities and Risks
detail.abstract: AI governance regimes are diverging across jurisdictions at a pace that creates both strategic opportunity and compliance peril for multinational enterprises. The European Union's AI Act establishes the world's most comprehensive risk-tiered regulatory framework. China enforces algorithmic recommendation and deepfake regulations with distinct compliance logics and enforcement mechanisms. India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act creates data localization obligations without a binding AI-specific framework. The United States maintains a sector-specific patchwork of state and federal rules with no comprehensive federal AI legislation. This divergence creates what this paper terms the Regulatory Arbitrage Window-a transitional period during which multinational enterprises can exploit jurisdictional asymmetries in AI regulation for competitive advantage, but also face mounting compliance complexity, reputational risk, and the accumulation of what this paper terms compliance debt: the future cost of retroactively meeting standards that the enterprise chose not to meet when they were optional. This paper maps the current AI regulatory landscape across twelve major markets, identifies the specific arbitrage opportunities and risks for AI-deploying enterprises, and proposes the Regulatory Convergence Readiness (RCR) framework-a strategic compliance approach that prepares companies for the eventual harmonization of AI governance standards while operating effectively in the current fragmented environment. The central argument is that companies optimizing for current regulatory minimums are building compliance debt that will prove substantially more costly to discharge than proactive convergence-ready strategies would have cost to implement. The paper concludes with implications for Chief Legal Officers structuring global AI compliance, corporate strategists navigating regulatory fragmentation, and policy analysts assessing the trajectory of international AI governance harmonization.

title: Metastability in Monetary Systems: When Stable Flows Mask Instability
affiliations: University College Dublin (UCD)

detail.title: Metastability in Monetary Systems: When Stable Flows Mask Instability
detail.abstract: Credit-based monetary systems exhibit a persistent empirical puzzle: flow variables appear stable, while stock variables drift systematically. We show that this coexistence is not accidental, but reflects a structural property of monetary expansion. Our central result is that stability is representation-dependent. Flow dynamics remain bounded and weakly responsive to shocks, yet the accumulated state of the system exhibits persistent drift. This divergence is sustained by a feedback gap: accumulated imbalances do not generate effective corrective adjustments in subsequent flows. As a result, the system operates in a metastable regime-locally stable in flows, globally drifting in accumulated states. Stability in observable dynamics therefore does not reflect convergence, but the absence of state-dependent feedback. These findings imply that frameworks focused on stabilizing flow variables are inherently incomplete. Because instability unfolds through the gradual accumulation of imbalances, it remains largely invisible in standard flow-based diagnostics.

title: The Returns to Trade Litigation: Evidence from the WTO Cotton Dispute
affiliations: Universidade do Estado de Mato Grosso, Universidade Federal de Mato Grosso and Universidade Estadual de Mato Grosso, affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: The Returns to Trade Litigation: Evidence from the WTO Cotton Dispute
detail.abstract: We estimate the causal eect of a WTO dispute settlement ruling on the winning complainant's export market share. We exploit Brazil's decisive victory in the Cotton Case (DS267)the most consequential agricultural trade dispute in WTO historyas a quasi-natural experiment. The dispute, initiated in 2002, challenged U.S. subsidy programs estimated to cost US$3.4 billion annually that were suppressing world cotton prices and displacing Brazilian exports. The mutually agreed settlement, concluded in October 2014, compelled the United States to reform its cotton support programs. Employing a Synthetic Dierence-in-Dierences (SDID) estimator (Arkhangelsky et al., 2021) on a balanced panel of 49 cotton-exporting countries over 20002021, we nd that Brazil's log cotton exports increased by 1.286 log points (95% CI: [0.991, 1.637]; p < 0.001) relative to a synthetic counterfactualequivalent to a 261.7% rise in exports. Results are robust across Two-Way Fixed Eects DiD, Propensity-Score-Matched DiD, and Synthetic Control benchmarks, and survive a complete battery of placebo permutation tests and an event-study pre-trend diagnostic. We nd no comparable eect in any country of the donor pool. The ndings demonstrate that multilateral dispute settlement can deliver export gains an order of magnitude larger than the direct compensation agreed, with broad implications for how developing countries should value WTO litigation as a trade policy instrument.

title: ATS-Mediated Erosion of the Overnight Reversal Anomaly: Evidence from Korea's NXT Launch

detail.title: ATS-Mediated Erosion of the Overnight Reversal Anomaly: Evidence from Korea's NXT Launch

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author has no relevant financial or non-financial interests to disclose. The author declares that no competing interests exist.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This study uses publicly available financial market data (Korea Exchange daily OHLCV and publicly disclosed NXT trading statistics) and does not involve human subjects, animals, or sensitive personal information; therefore, ethics review is not required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no specific grant from any funding agency in the public, commercial, or not-for-profit sectors.

detail.abstract:
We exploit Korea's March 2025 launch of NXT---the first independent alternative trading system (ATS) to produce premarket prices outside the KRX consolidated tape---as a natural experiment for the structural decay
of the overnight reversal anomaly. Using a daily panel of Korean common stocks from 2015 to 2026, we document that a strategy buying stocks with extreme negative overnight returns at the open and selling
them at the close earns a mean daily return of \SI{49.5}{\bps} (Newey--West $t=11.06$) over the full sample. The economic and statistical magnitude collapses around NXT's launch: a one--percentage--point increase in NXT's share of total daily volume is associated with a \SI{6.4}{\bps} decline in the strategy's daily return ($t=-2.89$,
$R^{2}=0.024$), and the regression-implied break-even share, at which the strategy's expected daily return is zero, is approximately \SI{11.8}{\percent}---a threshold the data have now crossed. The attenuation is robust to point-in-time universe construction, a $5\times5$ grid of transaction-cost assumptions, the inclusion of
forcibly delisted firms, two-factor (market and size) alpha regressions, and a Chow/sup-$F$ structural-break test. We interpret these findings as evidence that the overnight reversal anomaly in Korea was sustained by the absence of independent premarket price discovery, and that NXT's entry attenuated the very informational friction the strategy was monetizing. The Korean experience differs systematically from the U.S.\ dark-pool environment along three institutional dimensions, which we identify and discuss.

title:
The Cliff After Graduation: Transition Failure in Special Education 
A Conceptual Policy Analysis of Postsecondary Outcomes for Students with Disabilities

detail.title:
The Cliff After Graduation: Transition Failure in Special Education 
A Conceptual Policy Analysis of Postsecondary Outcomes for Students with Disabilities
detail.abstract:
Students with disabilities continue to experience disproportionately poor postsecondary outcomes despite decades of inclusion reform, transition planning mandates, and compliance based accountability structures within American public education systems. Although the Individuals with Disabilities Education Act (IDEA) requires schools to develop transition plans intended to support movement into adulthood, many students continue to leave secondary education academically credentialed but functionally underprepared for employment, independent living, higher education, and meaningful community participation. 

This paper argues that special education systems frequently prioritize procedural compliance over measurable adulthood outcomes, creating what many families experience as a "cliff after graduation." Through a conceptual policy analysis grounded in disability studies, transition research, implementation science, and Educational Architecture, this paper examines the structural limitations of compliance-centered transition systems, fragmented adult services, workforce exclusion, and inequitable access to community-based preparation opportunities. 

The paper further argues that inclusion without infrastructure results in performative equity rather than authentic adulthood readiness. In this context, performative equity refers to systems that create the appearance of inclusion through procedural access while failing to produce meaningful long-term participation outcomes.

title: Extorting the Next Generation of Lawyers: How Law Schools Use the Credential Assembly Service to Fix the Price of Law School Applications
affiliations: affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: Extorting the Next Generation of Lawyers: How Law Schools Use the Credential Assembly Service to Fix the Price of Law School Applications

declarations.funderStatement: This research was not funded, but the article was written for course credit for the Boston College Law Review

detail.abstract: Law schools have formed an illegal price-fixing cartel to fix the minimum price of a law school application. They have done so through their joint venture, the Law School Admissions Council (LSAC), a membership organization for law schools that, among other things, administers a centralized clearinghouse for application materials. The clearinghouse, called the Credential Assembly Service (CAS), makes the process of applying to law school more efficient for both schools and applicants, but it comes at a cost: applicants must pay the LSAC over $200 to subscribe to the service and then $45 for every application they send, in addition to the fee they pay law schools directly to apply. This Note argues that by charging fixed minimum rates for applications, law schools are price-fixing in violation of Section 1 of the Sherman Act under both a per se and rule of reason analysis. It reasons that while centralizing application processing is efficient and thus procompetitive, a less restrictive alternative exists: a pricing model where, like the Common Application for undergraduate admissions, schools rather than applicants pay to use the service. Ultimately, it argues that adopting a schools-pay model would be the most desirable remedy in this price-fixing case.

title: Forward-Looking Risk, Regime-Dependent Persistence and Distributional Asymmetry: An Integrative Review of Three Non-Redundant Dimensions in Capital Market Conditioning

detail.title: Forward-Looking Risk, Regime-Dependent Persistence and Distributional Asymmetry: An Integrative Review of Three Non-Redundant Dimensions in Capital Market Conditioning

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: Not applicable. This is a theoretical review paper that does not involve empirical data collection from human or animal subjects.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding.

detail.abstract: This review develops the theoretical foundations for an integrated treatment of three dimensions of capital market behaviour widely documented as empirical departures from classical mean-variance equilibrium: forward-looking volatility expectations embedded in option-implied measures; conditional persistence in price dynamics; and asymmetry in the return distribution. The three dimensions are captured, respectively, by the directional dynamics of the VIX index, by exponential moving averages applied to price series and by rolling estimates of realised skewness. Each is grounded in established asset pricing theory: Merton's (1973) Intertemporal CAPM provides the rational equilibrium justification for conditioning on state variables that describe the investment opportunity set, while Lo's (2004) Adaptive Markets Hypothesis explains why exploitability is episodic rather than uniform. Three claims are developed: that the dimensions are theoretically distinct, that they are empirically non-redundant and that pairwise combinations in the existing literature have not been integrated within a theoretically ordered conditioning architecture. The synthesis identifies an open research direction: the joint conditioning structure motivates future empirical investigation of whether theoretically ordered multi-signal architectures improve risk-adjusted performance relative to single-signal and pairwise benchmarks across capital market instruments.

title: Structural Macroeconomics with Daily Data: A Matrix-Free Mixed-Frequency VAR Approach
affiliations: Monash University - Department of Econometrics & Business Statistics

detail.title: Structural Macroeconomics with Daily Data: A Matrix-Free Mixed-Frequency VAR Approach
detail.abstract: Financial markets reveal monetary-policy news at a daily or even intraday frequency, while output and prices are observed only monthly or quarterly. This paper argues that the mismatch is not only a measurement problem but an identification problem: aggregating financial variables to the macroeconomic frequency can blur immediate financial responses with delayed real adjustment and change the inferred transmission of monetary policy. I develop a daily Bayesian mixed-frequency VAR in which low-frequency macroeconomic aggregates are treated as latent daily processes observed through aggregation equations. To make the daily system feasible, the long lag polynomial is represented by a low-dimensional basis expansion, and the missing daily macroeconomic paths are drawn with a matrixfree sampler that avoids forming or factorising the large precision matrix. In an application to U.S. monetary policy combining quarterly output, monthly prices, and daily financial variables, the daily system delivers immediate financial responses and gradual declines in output and prices after a contractionary shock, without the price puzzle found in low-frequency recursive VARs. The results show that temporal aggregation can obscure structural monetary transmission, and that estimating the system on the daily clock changes the economic conclusions.

title:
Can You Get There from Here? 
Reachable States in Economics

detail.title:
Can You Get There from Here? 
Reachable States in Economics

declarations.declarationOfInterest: NA
declarations.ethicsApproval: NA
declarations.funderStatement: NA

detail.abstract: Equilibrium results in economics typically establish that a particular state s * has certain properties that it is a xed point of the framework's operations, that small neighborhoods of it converge under those operations, or that it satises stated welfare conditions. Whether s * is reachable from the actual starting state of the system the framework describes is a separate question. This paper proposes that the question deserves to be a routine check, on the order of looking in your mirrors before backing out of a parking space. The check is cheap, usually returning ne, proceed, occasionally returning do not back up. The lens we propose recovers the conditional rigor the founders of equilibrium theory practiced and that parts of contemporary practice, from Econ 101 to DSGE work, have stopped doing routinely. It is a way of seeing whether the use one is about to make of an equilibrium result is a use the careful tradition would support. The check has a simple formal core (a reachability lemma), a structural diagnosis (the self-undermining condition), and a verication procedure that is the substantive work in any application and will usually require the most work. We apply it to seven well-known frameworks: the ChamleyJudd capital tax result, where the basin is nonempty but has been shown by later work not to include the United States; and six cases where the basin is empty Nozick's rectication principle, the Coase theorem, strong-form ecient markets, perfect competition as policy goal, the classical gold standard (in two distinct self-undermining structures), and the Great Moderation under Minsky's nancial instability hypothesis. The Reachability Lemma's proof is not hard; the work that earns the paper its keep is to show, case by case, that the failure condition actually applies. To do this we need substantive economic and philosophical arguments due to among others Coase, Hsiung, GrossmanStiglitz, Schumpeter, Polanyi, Eichengreen, Trin, Minsky. A strong form of Goodhart's law is one consequence of the lemma; the conation between xed-point and reachability claims that the check identies lives at every translation step from technical statement to policy claim. The check does not adjudicate what to do when a framework's target is unreachable; that is a separate, welfare-theoretic question we do not take up. The check is what the paper oers; the seven cases are demonstrations of when it matters.

title: When Independence Becomes Too Expensive: A Threshold Theory of Self-Discounting Entry under Unequal Protection

detail.title: When Independence Becomes Too Expensive: A Threshold Theory of Self-Discounting Entry under Unequal Protection

declarations.declarationOfInterest: This research received no external funding.
declarations.ethicsApproval: The author declares no competing interests or conflicts of interest.
declarations.funderStatement: This paper is a theoretical and conceptual study. It does not involve human participants, patient data, surveys, interviews, experiments, or identifiable personal information. Therefore, formal ethics approval was not required.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a threshold theory of self-discounting entry under unequal protection. I argue that weaker actors do not always respond to asymmetry by improving value, waiting for reciprocity, or exiting the field. When independent survival becomes costly, attachment payoff becomes concentrated, and viable alternatives weaken, actors may instead seek admission into stronger protective nodes by lowering their own effective entry price through prior concession. I call this mechanism self-discounting entry: the preemptive surrender of price, autonomy, status, or bargaining leverage before reciprocal commitment is secured. The paper’s central claim is that this shift is nonlinear. Self-discounting entry rises sharply once composite dependency pressure crosses a threshold shaped by resource asymmetry, independent survival cost, attachment payoff, alternatives, and normative-institutional resistance. To capture this structure, the paper proposes a threshold model in which asymmetry alone is insufficient; rather, asymmetry becomes behaviorally potent when it interacts with costly independence and concentrated attachment payoff. The paper then applies this mechanism comparatively to two domains: historical dependency arrangements under concentrated protection and modern intimate entry competition under visible protective asymmetry. The claim is not one of institutional identity, but of mechanism homology. Relative to Emerson, the paper dynamicizes dependence into a thresholded process of entry under pressure. Relative to Sassen, it supplies a micro-mechanism of protective admission beneath macro-level expulsion and exclusion. Relative to Granovetter-style threshold reasoning, it relocates threshold structure into the field of dependence and unequal protection. The broader contribution is to recast dependence not only as a structural condition, but as a thresholded admission process through which unequal protection transforms quality competition into entry competition

declarations.ethicsApproval: This study involves no human participants, patients, identifiable patient data, biospecimens, or animal subjects. The analysis relies exclusively on publicly available federal data sources (CMS Healthcare Cost Report Information System, CMS Notice of Funding Opportunity documents, Public Law 119-21 statutory text, 42 CFR § 485 regulatory text) and publicly available third-party policy analyses (Kaiser Family Foundation, Bipartisan Policy Center, National Rural Health Association). The representative Critical Access Hospital facility used in the worked example (Section V.D) is a synthetic composite constructed from sector-median values published in CMS HCRIS public-use files and Chartis aggregate reporting; it does not represent any identifiable facility, provider, or patient. Accordingly, no Institutional Review Board approval, ethics committee review, or written informed consent was required for this work.
